title: On boundaries of boundary value problems: The cases of Regularity and Neumann problems
abstract:

These results are analogues of an approximation result recently discovered by the first two authors in the case of the Dirichlet problem with data in $L^p$.
  Moreover, we show that an analogous approximation theorem is not viable for the Dirichlet-Regularity problem, nor for the variational Dirichlet problem. All of the results are new even in the case of the Laplacian and on the unit ball.

title: Rigidity for Families of Abelian Varieties over $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$
abstract: We provide a new proof of Farb's theorem on the global rigidity of the period map $\mathcal{M}_{g,n} \to \mathcal{A}_g$. We extend this classification to essentially include the period map for $\mathcal{M}_{2,n}$. We also provide a classification of holomorphic maps $\mathcal{M}_g \to \mathcal{A}_{h}$ for $h \leq 2g-1$. The only nonconstant maps in this range are given by taking the Jacobian of a curve and attaching a fixed Abelian variety. In addition to the group theory of the mapping class group, we make extensive use of the theory of variations of Hodge structures and the birational geometry on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_2$.

title: History independence and base-dominant rigidity for polynomial skew products
abstract: We study history independence of fast directions and its relation to the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula for regular polynomial skew products of degree $d\ge2$. Assuming uniform expansion on the support of the measure of maximal entropy and a base Lyapunov exponent larger than the vertical exponent, we prove that history independence is equivalent to conjugacy to a polynomial product by an affine shear map. Under history independence, the measure of maximal entropy satisfies the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula. If, in addition, the splitting is dominated, the dimension formula also implies history independence. The proof first upgrades the measurable fast direction to a holomorphic line field and then uses its invariance on periodic fibers to force the affine product structure. The converse dimension implication combines an entropy comparison argument with rigidity of local symmetries of periodic fiber Julia sets.

title: Global Lanczos with stochastic error correction for trace estimation of matrix functions
abstract: We propose a new method for computing the trace of a matrix function $f(A)$, where $A$ is a large, sparse, symmetric matrix. Our approach combines a deterministic global Lanczos approximation with a stochastic correction of its error. Starting the global Lanczos process with the identity matrix yields a direct approximation of the trace through a small tridiagonal matrix. The resulting basis matrices are polynomials in $A$, allowing the process to be implemented using sparse matrix-matrix multiplications when low-degree polynomials in $A$ have moderate fill-in. However, increased fill-in may limit the number of iterations that can be performed efficiently. To address this limitation, we derive an exact representation of the global Lanczos error as the trace of a matrix function and apply a stochastic estimator to the remainder. Even a moderately accurate estimate can substantially improve the accuracy, combining the deterministic method with the rapid initial convergence of stochastic trace estimators. We discuss error bounds and variance reduction, and present numerical experiments that compare the resulting method with existing ones.

title: Modified scattering and asymptotic completeness for a massive Dirac-wave system in dimension three
abstract:
We establish global well-posedness and modified scattering for the three-dimensional Dirac-Klein-Gordon system with a massive spinor and a massless scalar field, for small, sufficiently regular and localized initial data. This answers a question posed by Dong, Li, and Yuan in \cite[Case IV]{DLY23}. We also identify a Majorana-type condition on the initial data that yields linear scattering, showing that both linear and modified scattering solutions coexist in this model.
  Conversely, we establish asymptotic completeness for small asymptotic profiles satisfying suitable regularity and decay assumptions. The forward argument combines the hyperboloidal foliation method with testing by wave packets, whereas the backward construction relies on a contraction argument in suitably chosen norms.

title: A toric construction of the spectral Tate curve
abstract: We develop toric geometry spectral algebraic geometry. In particular, we lift toric varieties to flat schemes over the sphere spectrum. Furthermore, we prove several rigidity and strictness results allowing us to define and produce strict group actions of flat algebraic tori. As an application, we give a construction of the Tate curve in spectral algebraic geometry. This approach lets us produce a lift of the Tate curve to $\mathbb{S}[[q]]$. We furthermore describe how to lift (arithmetic) toric stacks.

title: Construction and discrete approximation of the renormalized fractional parabolic Anderson model
abstract: For a directed polymer in a discrete fractional Gaussian environment, we identify the scaling limit of its partition field with the renormalized Stratonovich solution of the one-dimensional parabolic Anderson model with fractional noise and flat initial condition. The underlying walk is simple and symmetric, and the temporal and spatial Hurst indices satisfy $H_0>\frac12$, $\frac12\le H_1<1$ and $2H_0+H_1<2$. After an explicit deterministic normalization, the interpolated partition field converges in law in $C_{\rm loc}([0,\infty)\times\R)$, with convergence of all finite moments of its supremum norm on compacts. We construct the limiting field directly by smoothing the noise in the equation and subtracting the corresponding stationary counterterm. The classical solutions converge in $L^p(Ω;C(\mathcal K))$ for every $1\le p<\infty$ and every compact space-time rectangle $\mathcal K$, including those that meet the initial line $t=0$. For $2H_0+H_1>\frac53$, the limit agrees with the solution that Chen, Ouyang, Tindel and the author constructed using regularity structures. The construction also covers the new range $\frac32<2H_0+H_1\le\frac53$. The proofs rely on Feynman-Kac representations and on estimates and invariance principles for weighted self- and mutual intersections of random walks and Brownian motions, together with uniform increment estimates and Gaussian hypercontractivity.

title: Lower semicontinuity of dimension for quasi-Bernoulli measures under conformal projections
abstract: We study the dependence of the Hausdorff dimension of projected quasi-Bernoulli measures on a conformal iterated function system on the real line. For every fixed quasi-Bernoulli probability measure on the symbolic space, we prove that the dimension of its push-forward under the coding map is lower semicontinuous in the $C^{1+θ}$ topology, without any separation assumption or shift-invariance requirement on the symbolic measure. The proof combines bounded distortion and finite-scale entropy estimates with uniform control of the entropy dimension over measures whose densities are bounded above and below. For invariant Gibbs measures associated with Hölder continuous potentials, we also prove joint lower semicontinuity with respect to the defining system and the potential. As an application, we obtain a generic dimension formula: for each fixed shift-invariant quasi-Bernoulli measure, a dense $G_δ$ set of systems with derivative moduli strictly less than 1/2 has projected dimension equal to the minimum of one and the entropy-to-Lyapunov-exponent ratio.

title: The Maximum Number of Sets for 16 Cards is 26
abstract: In SET, each card has four properties with three values each, and three cards form a \emph{set} when every property is all the same or all different. We prove that the maximum number of sets among $13$, $14$, $15$, and $16$ cards is $16$, $19$, $23$, and $26$, respectively. Viewing cards as points of $\mathbb{F}_3^4$ and sets as lines, we show that a configuration that leaves one of the $40$ line directions of $\mathbb{F}_3^4$ unused projects into $\mathbb{F}_3^3$ without losing a set, which reduces the problem to three properties, where exhaustive search is feasible. We force an unused direction by counting repeated directions in the planes through a card on many sets, and treat configurations containing a magic square separately.

title: Learning the Average Dose-Response Function with a Right-Censored Treatment
abstract: This paper considers estimation and inference for the average dose-response function under right-censored treatment duration and missing outcomes for censored units. Using the duration lower bounds provided by censored records, we construct a novel multiply robust estimator through augmented local estimating equations. Under suitable regularity conditions, the estimator remains consistent when any two of the outcome regression, treatment density, and censoring survival function are consistently estimated. We establish its convergence rate and asymptotic distribution within a cross-fitting framework under appropriate conditions on nuisance estimation. To address local smoothing bias that can distort confidence interval coverage, we further develop a debiased estimator that supports asymptotically valid pointwise inference without undersmoothing. Under additional uniform conditions, we construct simultaneous confidence bands using a Gaussian multiplier bootstrap. Simulation studies evaluate estimation accuracy, the validity of pointwise and uniform inference, and robustness to nuisance model misspecification. A semi-synthetic study calibrated to NHANES illustrates the proposed methods in a setting with a known dose-response function.

title: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian equations on uniformly $(k-1)$-convex domains
abstract: In this paper, we mainly study the sum Hessian equation with general boundary values in the case $2\leq k\leq n$. Under the conditions that the boundary is uniformly $(k-1)$-convex, the right-hand side is monotone non-decreasing in $u$, convex in the gradient, and has a suitably small linear gradient growth, we prove the existence of a unique smooth admissible solution. The proof constructs the global subsolution and gradient barriers by using strictly $k$-convex function, and derives the boundary second-order estimates from the tangential linearizations and a duality inequality for the boundary curvature.

title: Matricial stability and central corrections for generalized Jordan derivations on amenable $C^*$-algebras
abstract: We study norm stability of third-type generalized Jordan identities, allowing their auxiliary maps to be arbitrary. A canonical normalization eliminates these witnesses with a factor of four. For a unital $C^*$-algebra and a unital contractive Banach bimodule, the zero-defect maps are precisely sums of a derivation and multiplication by a central module element. We characterize scalar stability by the closed range of the normalized Jordan-defect operator. For operator bimodules, two explicit $2\times2$ tests recover an ordered Leibniz defect and a commutator defect. If the algebra has an approximate diagonal bounded by $M$ and the module is weak$^*$ closed, these tests yield approximation by an inner derivation plus a central multiplier with error at most $8M$ times the normalized matrix defect. The corresponding completely bounded estimate holds at all matrix levels. For full matrix algebras the constant is $8$, independently of their size, and weak$^*$ closedness is unnecessary. When the map vanishes at the identity, the constants improve to $2M$ and $2$, respectively.

title: Psyquandle Fares
abstract: We introduce a new infinite family of invariants of singular knot and links and of pseudoknots by extending the biquandle fares construction to the case of psyquandles. We give the axioms explicitly for four cases of fare-based invariants: 1-fares, signed crooked 2-fares, signed through 2-fares and signed complete 2-fares. We provide examples of each type, illustrating the method of computation and collecting some results for toy examples using small-cardinality psyquandles and abelian coefficient groups.

title: Stokes Waves in a Finite-Depth Fluid via a Conformal Transformation
abstract: Euler equations for a spatially periodic surface in a two-dimensional fluid of a finite depth are reduced to a system of evolution equations after a conformal transformation. Compared to the previously developed formal approach, we show that the system of evolution equations is complemented by two constraints which determine the new depth in conformal variables and the Bernoulli integration constant. A locally unique continuation of the traveling Stokes waves with respect to the wave speed is studied by using arguments based on the implicit function theorem. We show that the constraints on the traveling wave profile recover the correct small-amplitude expansion of Stokes waves in physical variables. We also prove for the co-periodic stability problem that the real unstable eigenvalues may bifurcate from the zero eigenvalue only at a critical point of the wave energy. Finally, we perform numerical approximations of the wave profiles for both small and large amplitudes and illustrate different bifurcations along the solution family.

title: Learning-Enhanced Reduce-Repair-Refine-Optimize Framework for Real-Time Train Platforming
abstract: Real-time train platforming under disruptions requires rapid revision of routing, platforming, and timing decisions. Dense traffic and shared infrastructure create tightly coupled conflicts, making real-time optimization computationally demanding. This paper proposes a learning-enhanced Reduce-Repair-Refine-Optimize framework that reduces and selectively relaxes the routing search space to balance computational efficiency, feasibility, and solution quality. The reduction stage constructs a restricted MILP by fixing selected routing decisions using route-specific predictive models and thresholds, thereby accounting for heterogeneity across routes. Two adaptive mechanisms subsequently modify the reduced search space: repair selectively releases route fixings to restore feasibility, while refinement releases additional fixings to recover routing alternatives and improve solution quality without reverting to the unrestricted problem. Computational experiments on real-life disrupted station-area instances show that the framework matches or improves upon a recent rTPP heuristic in more than 80% of instances within 60~s. Under the common 180~s budget, the framework obtains strictly better terminal incumbents than the unrestricted MILP in 56.7% of all instances and 77.4% of hard instances. Moreover, it obtains better terminal incumbents than an otherwise identical variant without refinement in 71.9% of hard instances. The results demonstrate that learning-based search-space reduction is most effective when the reduced search space remains adaptable during optimization, enabling high-quality feasible solutions within the real-time computation budget.

title: NeRI: Neural Residual Iteration for Elliptic Operator Equations and Variational Inequalities
abstract: In this work, we propose a so-called {\it Neural Residual Iteration} (NeRI), a weak-form neural-network framework for solving a class of elliptic operator equations and variational inequalities, including nonlinear and nonsymmetric problems that may not admit a global energy functional. The key idea is to construct, at each iteration, a state-dependent linear functional whose derivative with respect to the trial function recovers the current weak residual. A single gradient step is then performed on the residual, yielding a residual-driven neural update without requiring a global energy functional or an additional test network. From a function-space perspective, NeRI can be interpreted as a neural-tangent-kernel-preconditioned realization of classical residual iterations, thereby bridging classical iterative solvers and neural-network optimization. We further extend NeRI to elliptic variational inequalities (VIs) through penalized and constraint-preserving formulations. For wide two-layer networks under gradient flow, we prove finite-time lazy-training estimates and derive an $H^1$-error decomposition relative to the exact weak solution. Numerical experiments on several elliptic problems demonstrate the effectiveness of NeRI, particularly for nonsymmetric and low-regularity problems.

title: Rank Functions of Flag Matroids with Applications to Order-Neutral Submodular Valuations
abstract: We provide a rank function axiomatization for flag matroids and show that it is cryptomorphic to the definition of flag matroids as a sequence of matroid quotients. Afterwards, we present some applications of flag matroid rank functions by providing solutions to selected problems. In particular, we discuss connections between flag matroids and submodular valuations in computational economics by showing that rank functions of flag matroids of length $k$ are precisely the same as $\{0, 1, \dots, k\}$-order-neutral submodular valuations. We then prove that $v:2^E\to \mathbb{R}$ is an order-neutral submodular valuation if and only if $v$ can be written as $v(X) = b|X| + \sum_{i=1}^l c_ir_{N_i}(X), \quad b \in \mathbb{R}, c_i > 0$, where $N_{i+1}$ is a quotient of $N_i$. Doing so allows us to prove that every order-neutral submodular valuation is a gross-substitute valuation and that not every order-neutral submodular valuation is a Rado valuation. Furthermore, we prove that if $|E|\geq 3$, then a set $A$ is a Sidon set if and only if all $A$-submodular valuations are order-neutral, if and only if all $A$-submodular valuations are gross-substitute valuations.

title: Observables and Symmetries in Causal Fermion System
abstract: We investigate the interplay of observables and symmetries in the framework of causal fermion systems (CFS). We show that position observables transform covariantly under unitary symmetries and for static CFS we derive their Heisenberg-type evolution. To give these results a geometric interpretation, we establish conditions under which spacetime isometries induce symmetries of CFS constructed from solutions of the Dirac equation. The crucial link is provided by the Dirac equation itself, which relates the infinitesimal generators of the geometric and CFS symmetries. In static spacetimes, this allows us to identify the generator of the induced unitary symmetry with the spatial Dirac Hamiltonian.

title: On the extension of meromorphic mappings and correspondences with finite volume
abstract: Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold. Using Bishop's extension theorem, we show that a meromorphic map, or more generally a meromorphic correspondence, $f\colonΔ^k_*\to X$ extends meromorphically across $0$ if and only if its graph has finite $2k$-dimensional volume near $\{0\}\times X$; equivalently, all mixed integrals $\intω_E^{k-m}\wedge(f^*ω)^m$, $1\le m\le k$, are finite. The criterion extends to arbitrary proper analytic subsets, and yields an energy criterion with a sharp exponent, a dichotomy for maps into Hopf manifolds, a rationality criterion for maps between projective manifolds, and, for $k=2$ and pluriclosed targets, the equivalence of extension with finiteness of the single integral $\int(f^*ω)^2$.

title: A Fast and Accurate Time-Space Decomposition for Unit Commitment With Storage
abstract: Grid-scale batteries couple decisions across time. This makes unit commitment (UC) with thousands of buses, batteries, generators, and alternating current constraints intractable. We introduce a time-space decomposition (TSD) heuristic to solve the problem. We first calculate target net battery charge or discharge rates on a zonal level, relaxing spatial constraints. We then incorporate this target into the Relax-and-Round UC (RRUC) solver from our previous work. RRUC enforces the spatial transmission constraints and transfers power between zones, if that reduces costs. We show that our TSD produces an error of about 0.1% on a simpler economic dispatch problem with batteries. This is larger than the error produced by RRUC in the tests in our previous work. So, we conjecture that the combined error of our two approximations is not much larger than 0.1%. We show that TSD with RRUC can solve systems with 10,000 buses in about 6 minutes, with sub-quadratic scaling, making it suitable for real time operations on an ISO-sized system.

title: Blow-up profile decomposition and optimal Harnack inequalities for the $n$-Liouville equation
abstract: We consider the problem $- Δ_n u = h(x) e^u$ in a bounded domain $Ω$ of $\mathbb R^n$, where $Δ_n$ stands for the $n$-Laplacian and $h$ is a continuous function satisfying $0 < a \leq h \leq b$. Several new a priori estimates are obtained for the sets of solutions whose boundary oscillation is uniformly bounded by some constant. Those results are exploited to provide a profile decomposition in $L^\infty$-sense for a sequence of blowing-up solutions. We also present an optimal Harnack type inequality, which states that on a compact set $K \subset Ω$ we have a universal estimate $\displaystyle \sup_K u + (n-1)\displaystyle \inf_Ω u \leq C$.

title: Quasi-product and multiplicative Markov measures Radon-Nikodym problem, random walks: the free group case
abstract: The purpose of this paper is a conceptual clarification of the role of a special class of measures on topological Markov chains - multiplicative Markov measures - in the context of random walks. It is achieved by combining the interpretation of multiplicative Markov measures on the boundary of a free group as the unique solutions of the Radon - Nikodym problem for product cocycles of the boundary action and the fact that the Radon - Nikodym cocycle of the harmonic measure of a nearest neighbour random walk on a free group is a product one.

title: Landau's problems through ratios of $L$-functions
abstract: Very recently, Lee announced a proof of the Twin Prime Conjecture assuming the Ratios Conjecture for the Riemann zeta function. We obtain conditional asymptotic formulas with power-saving errors for each of Landau's four prime problems. In the function field setting, using Sawin's estimates for factorization functions in squarefree progressions and a discriminant cohomology argument, we obtain unconditional Goldbach and prime-pair asymptotics over sufficiently large fixed odd fields, including prime fields. Similar results may be possible for other problems in analytic number theory.

title: A treatment of d-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians with noninteger quantum numbers and their connection to the radial momentum operator
abstract: The Bagci-Hoggan exponential-type orbitals, the generalization of Coulomb-Sturmians to noninteger quantum numbers, were recently identified as d-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians. In the present study, this identification is treated in detail. The radial differential equation for these orbitals is derived directly from their closed form. It represents the general Coulomb-Sturmian differential equation for quantum numbers with real values. The solution is verified through a power series representation and a first-order matrix form based on the Green's function of the radial Laplacian. New transformation relationships between these orbitals and Slater-type orbitals with noninteger principal quantum numbers are established. The radial differential equation is expressed in terms of the radial momentum operator. The expectation values of the position and radial momentum operators are obtained in closed form. The radial and Heisenberg uncertainty products, the Shannon entropy and the Fisher information are derived in general form.

title: Invariant measures with uniform projection on surfaces and billiards
abstract:
In this paper, we study probability measures on the unit tangent bundle which are invariant under the geodesic flow and whose projection to the base manifold is the normalized Riemannian volume. We show that the Liouville measure is the only such measure on a complete oriented surface of finite area with ergodic geodesic flow. In particular, this resolves a conjecture of Katok--Knieper--Weiss in dimension two. The same holds for ergodic planar billiards with piecewise C2 boundary, such as the Bunimovich stadium, the Sinai billiard, and generic polygons. The proof combines the Fourier analysis in the fibers with holomorphic functions on the transport twistor space.
  As a consequence, on these surfaces and on the Bunimovich stadium, a high-energy sequence of normalized Laplacian eigenfunctions tends to be equidistributed in the phase space if and only if it tends to be equidistributed in the physical space. In particular, on every stadium, every failure of equidistribution in the phase space implies scarring in the physical space. Combined with Hassell's theorem, this gives a new proof of scarring in the physical space for almost every stadium.
  In higher dimensions, we obtain an entropy bound for the ergodic components of such measures. We also construct counterexamples for hyperbolic toral automorphisms.

title: An ODE to Changing Variables: $v = y/x$ Is For Victory
abstract: Most first courses in differential equations introduce students to very special differential equations which can be solved in closed form from a small set of techniques (such as separable equations and integrating factors). Frequently other equations can be converted to one of these forms through a change of variable; however, these transformations are usually just given without any explanation of \emph{how} people found them, or \emph{why} problems of these forms have nice solutions, but not related ones. We consider the first order differential equation $dy/dx = f(x,y)$ where $f(x,y)$ does not factor as $A(x)B(y)$, and assume $f(x,y) = g(y/x^r)$ for some nice function $g$ and some real number $r$. This can be reduced to a separable equation only when $r=1$. We then discuss generalizations and what conditions on $f$ lead to a change of variables yielding a separable equation. Our goals are twofold. First, to encourage students and instructors to be active, questioning the methods and results, seeing how far they can be extended and why they work. Second, we discuss how to appropriately use AI to take ideas and special cases as prompts and quickly create extensions and editable notes that can be shared with students, freeing up professors (and students) from straightforward calculations \emph{without} sacrificing learning and understanding.

title: Zariski Topology of (Krasner) Hypermodules
abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative Krasner hyperring with identity and $M$ an $R$-hypermodule. We consider the prime spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}_R(M)$, consisting of all prime subhypermodules of $M$. In this paper, we introduce a Zariski topology on $\operatorname{Spec}_R(M)$ and investigate its fundamental topological properties, including irreducibility, connectedness, compactness, and separation axioms, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for each. In particular, we prove that $\operatorname{Spec}_R(M)$ is irreducible if and only if the nilradical of $M$ is a prime hyperideal, and that it is connected precisely when the underlying hyperring is not a nontrivial direct product. We further investigate the functoriality of the Zariski topology in the category of Krasner hyperrings and hypermodules. Moreover, using the fundamental relation $ε^{*}$, the smallest regular relation on $M$ for which the quotient $\overline{M}=M/ε^{*}$ becomes an $\overline{R}=R/Γ^{*}$-module, we establish a correspondence between the Zariski topologies of $M$ and $\overline{M}$. We show that this correspondence is functorial and thereby relate the hypermodule-theoretic setting to the classical theory of modules over rings.

title: The length of the longest path in random acyclic orientations of a complete multipartite graph
abstract: We study the distribution of the length of the longest path in a uniformly random acyclic orientation of a complete multipartite graph. We derive an explicit analytic expression for the probability generating function of the longest path length, and, for an arbitrary fixed number of parts of equal size, we apply analytic combinatorics in several variables to obtain asymptotics (as the part size tends toward infinity) for its mean longest path length.

title: Normalized ground states of Kirchhoff equation on waveguide manifolds
Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
abstract:
In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter.
  As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

title: Intervals in affine Bruhat order
abstract: Let $(W,S)$ be an irreducible affine Coxeter system. We study Bruhat intervals in $W$ via the well-known characterization of Bruhat order in terms of galleries. We start by using folded galleries to formulate an analogous order on the coweight lattice, which we call Iwahori order. This allows us to reduce the description of certain Bruhat intervals to that of the corresponding Iwahori intervals. We next give closed-form descriptions of all Iwahori intervals, using the quantum Bruhat graph (QBG). More precisely, we show that lower Iwahori intervals saturate pseudo-Weyl polytopes (that is, certain intersections of negative cones), and upper Iwahori intervals saturate certain unions of positive cones, with the cone points given by explicit formulae involving paths in the QBG. We then describe arbitrary Bruhat intervals by partitioning them into their core, a large region which is (in most cases) completely determined by an Iwahori interval, and their crust, the complementary boundary region. We conclude by proving that, under a super-regularity assumption, the crust is covered by certain locally-defined tesselating shapes. All statements and proofs are rank- and type-free.

title: On the Flucher--Rumpf isoperimetric question for the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem: a conformal reformulation, quantitative bounds and the second variation at the disc
abstract: Let $c(Ω)$ be the Bernoulli constant of a bounded domain $Ω\subset\R^N$, that is, the infimum of the parameters $λ$ for which the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem $Δu=0$ in $Ω\setminus K$, $u=0$ on $\partialΩ$, $u=1$ and $|\nabla u|=λ$ on $\partial K$ admits a classical solution. Flucher and Rumpf asked whether $c(Ω)\ge c(Ω^*)$, where $Ω^*$ is the ball of the same volume. The variational analogue was settled by Daners and Kawohl, but the variational constant differs from $c$ already for the ball, and the original question remains open. We prove the following. (i) Through a conformal parametrisation of $Ω\setminus K$ by an annulus, every classical solution in a simply connected planar domain with connected, filled free set satisfies $λ\geμ/R$, where $πR^2=|Ω|$ and $μ\approx 2.485268$; hence $c(Ω)\ge 0.9142\,c(Ω^*)$ for every bounded planar convex domain of class $C^1$. (ii) In this class, the Flucher--Rumpf inequality is equivalent to an area inequality for analytic functions in an annulus, which also provides an explicit generator of exact solutions. (iii) A Rellich--Pohozaev identity yields, in every dimension $N\ge2$ and for every strictly star-shaped domain, $c(Ω)\ge\max\{\sqrt{θ(Ω)},κ_N\}\,c(Ω^*)$, where $θ(Ω)\in(0,1]$ is an explicit geometric quantity equal to $1$ only for balls and $κ_N$ is an explicit constant with $κ_3\approx0.650$ and $κ_N\to1$ as $N\to\infty$.

title: Optimal Capital Injections in a Microlending Group under External Shocks
abstract: Motivated by static models of group default in microlending, we study a dynamic problem in which the members of a lending group are exposed to external shocks, such as droughts or floods, and the manager of a common emergency fund decides at each shock how much capital to inject into the members who were hit. Shocks arrive at random times, the set of members that a shock hits may depend on which members the previous shock hit, and the losses may spill over to members who were not hit directly. Between shocks, the members' wealth follows a linear stochastic differential equation in which members support each other, and the fund grows with interest and member contributions up to a cap. The cost balances the members' shortfall below a poverty line, a welfare measure that contains a standard poverty measure as a special case, against the administrative cost of the injections and the benefit of keeping money in the fund. We formulate the problem as a Markov decision process embedded at the shock times and prove that the embedded process is Markov with a weakly continuous transition kernel. When the discount rate exceeds a growth rate determined by the wealth dynamics, we show that the expected total cost is finite under every policy, that the finite-horizon optimal values converge to the infinite-horizon one at an explicit rate, and that there exists a stationary optimal injection policy, which can be chosen independent of calendar time.

title: Spherical functions of the quantum symmetric pair of type FII
abstract: We prove Schlösser's conjecture relating quantum FII spherical functions to Askey--Wilson polynomials for equal left and right coideal parameters and determine the corresponding radial operator. An explicit transport formula gives the shifted restrictions for arbitrary nonzero parameters.

title: Equivariant intersection cohomology of some $4$-dimensional locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds
abstract: Locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds are singular analogues of quasitoric manifolds. In this paper, we study a certain class of four-dimensional locally standard $T^2$-pseudomanifolds over convex polygons. We establish an Orlik-Raymond type classification and study their ordinary and equivariant cohomology, as well as their intersection and equivariant intersection cohomology. We also introduce ring structures on middle-perversity intersection cohomology and equivariant intersection cohomology via change of perversity. We show that these rings can be described in terms of the cohomology and equivariant cohomology of associated nonsingular spaces, which are quasitoric manifolds or $S^4$. Furthermore, we give combinatorial descriptions of the equivariant cohomology and equivariant intersection cohomology in terms of labelled graphs.

title: Relational Semantics and Completeness for Onto-Epistemic Logic
abstract: This paper investigates a relational semantics for onto-epistemic logic with two semi-negations. The frames carry two pairs of quasi-orders and two commuting involutions. Some frames have nondistributive lattices of stable sets. The four- and nine-valued entailments are recovered as joint entailment on two particular finite frames. Sound and complete binary consequence calculi are given for both component entailments and for joint entailment. The joint Lindenbaum algebra embeds subdirectly into the product of its two component quotients. This embedding shows that joint derivability is the intersection of the two component derivability relations. The finite model property is proved using Dedekind-MacNeille completion and a filter-ideal representation of the resulting lattice. All three entailments are decidable by interleaving the search for a derivation with the search for a finite countermodel.

title: Sum of Powers with Matrix Coefficients
abstract: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We consider polynomial maps with constants $ω(x,y)=A_1x^k+A_2y^k$ on $M_n(F)$, where $A_1$ is invertible and $k\geq2$. We show that the necessary condition for surjectivity obtained by Saini and Singh (Polynomial maps with constants on matrix algebra, Linear Algebra Appl. 752 (2027), 256-277) is not sufficient in any dimension $n\geq6$. We also completely characterize surjectivity for $n=5$ and $6$.

title: Strong Well-Posedness for One-Dimensional Quantile-Dependent SDEs with Hölder-Continuous Diffusion
abstract:
We establish strong well-posedness for one-dimensional stochastic differential equations whose drift and diffusion coefficients depend on a prescribed quantile of the solution's marginal law. The diffusion coefficient is uniformly non-degenerate and Hölder continuous in space. The drift is the sum of a non-increasing Hölder-continuous component and a globally Lipschitz component of at most linear growth. Both components are Lipschitz continuous in the quantile variable. The main obstacles are the limited spatial regularity of the diffusion and the quantitative control of quantiles in terms of the $L^1$-distance between densities.
  We freeze the quantile path and combine uniform Hölder estimates for the resulting densities with a cancellation argument for the second-order diffusion perturbation. This yields an $L^1$-stability estimate for the frozen density flows and, together with uniform tail bounds and positive lower density bounds, a Volterra-type estimate for the frozen quantile map. An exponentially weighted supremum norm makes this map a strict contraction on $[0,T]$, giving a unique self-consistent quantile path and hence a unique strong solution. When the diffusion coefficient is independent of the quantile variable, the Yamada--Watanabe approximation also yields stability with respect to the initial condition.

title: Generalized particle systems: a locality-factorized metamodel for self-propelled particles and agent-based models
abstract: We propose a single formal object, the generalized particle system (GPS), under which self-propelled particle systems (SPPS) and agent-based models (ABMs) are instances of one construction. A GPS is a typed finite population, a per-particle state space with arbitrary internal structure, a global environment, a neighbourhood map that may depend on the configuration, and type-indexed local rules; these assemble into a generator whose iteration is a monoid action, i.e. an autonomous dynamical system. Update schedules and stochastic rules are added at the same generality, so sequential and noisy models (the original Primordial Particle System, Vicsek) are covered, not approximated. The construction isolates the one ingredient separating the two communities: in the classical ABM reading the dependency graph is fixed; in an SPPS it is a function of the state. Under an exchangeability axiom (rules see neighbours only through the multiset of their types and states) the generator is equivariant for type-preserving permutations and descends to a dynamical system on counting measures, the setting of kinetic limits of swarming models. We read the tuple as a metamodel: its structural components coordinatize a space of models inside which numerical parameters live. Six pre-registered experiments on one engine implementing the generator test the claims: freezing the neighbourhood map destroys alignment ($\varphi = 0.91 \to 0.04$) while yielding a different, non-aligned aggregation; the realized neighbourhood graph rewires up to 64% of its edges per step, its rewiring rate anti-correlated with order ($-0.99$); a topological instead of metric neighbourhood reshapes a flocking phase diagram; the same rule with cohesion and separation off shows a Vicsek-type transition whose susceptibility peak grows with system size. One prediction failed and one subsumption claim is unconfirmed; both are reported.

title: Quaternionic Wave Numbers and the Dirac Equation: Resolving the Nielsen--Ninomiya Barrier and Infinities
abstract: We exemplify the applicability of the rational wave numbers by formulating the relativistic Dirac equation on the discrete sequence space $\mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}$ over the quaternions $\mathbb{H}$ and demonstrating how this resolves fundamental issues relating to Dirac's equation. Generating $\mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}$ from the primitive basis $\mathcal{P}_0 = \{E_Z, E_{\bar{1}}\}$ as both a static closure and a dynamic enumeration, we show that coupling local quantum kinematics with global cosmological expansion leads to the following results: (1) Dirac 4-spinors and the Clifford algebra $\mathrm{C}\ell_{1,3}(\mathbb{R})$ emerge from the second Cayley--Dickson doubling (biquaternions $\mathbb{H} \otimes \mathbb{C}$); (2) under dynamic generation on an integer clock lattice with causal horizon $Λ_m$, relativistic difference operators require temporal depth, establishing clock beat $m = 2$ as the universal Matter Genesis Threshold; (3) the Nielsen--Ninomiya fermion doubling barrier is circumvented on modular sequences $\mathbb{Z}/Q\mathbb{Z}$ because candidate zone-edge doubler modes ($p = Q/2$) are actively pruned at the generational boundary by the coprime sieve projector $\mathcal{S}_Q$ ($\gcd(Q/2, Q) > 1$), preserving exact chiral symmetry without Wilson terms; (4) the discrete fermionic Green's function $S_Q(n, m)$ possesses no coincident-point singularity ($n = m$), converting ultraviolet loop integrals into finite Dedekind and Kloosterman character sums, realizing Dirac's demand for an infinity-free theory; and (5) Zitterbewegung is resolved as an observable stroboscopic beat against vacuum reference $E_Z$, identifying rest mass $m_0$ as a vacuum coupling beat frequency for stationary periodic cycles on the saturated quotient graph.

title: q-completely monotonic and q-Bernstein functions
abstract: For $0<q<1$, we study (q)-completely monotone and q-Bernstein functions defined by the Jackson derivative. We establish the positive linear closure of the latter class and prove an integral characterization of q-Bernstein functions continuous at zero on a geometric lattice. The representing measures satisfy the natural Lévy integrability condition, and the corresponding integral kernels are positive semidefinite. We prove that classical completely monotone and Bernstein functions belong to the respective q-classes and examine composition with absolutely monotone functions. Explicit examples show the limits of product closure, composition, and definiteness with respect to ordinary addition.

title: Intersection Cuts for Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programs via Decision-Diagram-Free Sets
abstract: We introduce a novel decision-diagram-based framework for generating intersection cuts to strengthen polyhedral relaxations of bounded mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) with general nonlinear constraints. Building on decision diagrams (DDs) that provide outer approximations of MINLP feasible regions, we propose the concept of DD-free sets, which are convex regions whose interiors do not intersect the sets represented by the DDs. By exploiting the underlying graphical structure, we develop efficient methods for constructing these regions without requiring restrictive assumptions on the functional form of nonlinear constraints or access to distance oracles. We investigate the maximality properties of DD-free sets and devise algorithms for obtaining maximal forbidden regions within several structured classes. The resulting intersection cuts exploit geometric information retained in DD representations, enabling further strengthening of relaxations beyond what can be achieved through conventional DD-based convexification. We also introduce interval DDs to facilitate the representation of general nonlinear constraints and establish convergence results for intersections of constraint-specific DDs, providing a theoretical foundation for their integration into global optimization frameworks. Computational experiments on challenging open instances from MINLPLib, encompassing a broad range of nonlinear and nonconvex structures, demonstrate that the proposed approach can substantially improve dual bounds and achieve greater optimality-gap closure than state-of-the-art global optimization solvers. These findings highlight the potential of exploiting graphical representations of infeasible regions to develop stronger cutting planes for general MINLPs.

title: Monotonicity properties of ratios of Ferrers and conical functions related to a Riemannian nonlocal eigenvalue problem
abstract: Recently, for a given Riemannian manifold with certain curvature constraints, S. Kajántó and A. Kristály [KK24] formulated a variational problem (on either positively or negatively curved Riemannian model spaces) and computed the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions in terms of the radii, curvature and weight. Moreover, they conjectured that a saturation phenomenon exists also in the case of positively or negatively curved Riemannian model spaces (not only in the Euclidean case), and this is based entirely on the incompatibility of a system of nonlinear equations involving special functions, like Ferrers functions of the first kind and conical functions of the first kind. In this paper, we provide a partial solution for both positive and negative curvature case.

title: Mean-field Token Steering
abstract: We consider stochastic token steering through a deep stack of transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for an interacting particle system on the unit sphere, where interactions arise from the attention mechanism. In the mean-field limit, the token population evolves via a controlled integro-partial differential equation where the feedback control acts as a corrective vector field guiding the population toward an aggregate configuration of tokens in the representation space. We deduce the minimum effort control to accomplish this task over a fixed time horizon interpreted as normalized layer depth. We show that the resulting controlled dynamics for the token population can be understood as a mean-field Schrödinger bridge adapted to the sphere geometry. Building on this, we propose a novel generalization of the dynamic Sinkhorn recursion to compute the consistent token evolution. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed approach achieves exact steering of the token population.

title: NS-bialgebras, the NS-Yang-Baxter equation and dendriform D-bialgebras
abstract: In this paper, we develop a bialgebra theory for NS-algebras via the Manin triple approach. We first study representations of NS-algebras and establish an equivalence among NS-bialgebras, matched pairs and Manin triples of NS-algebras. We then introduce the NS-Yang-Baxter equation (NS-YBE) and show that its symmetric solutions induce triangular NS-bialgebras. We further investigate the relationship between symmetric solutions of the NS-YBE and $\mathcal O$-operators of NS-algebras, and characterize pre-NS-algebras in terms of invertible $\mathcal O$-operators. As an application, we investigate the relation between NS-bialgebras and dendriform D-bialgebras via double constructions of Connes cocycles. In particular, we show that every NS-bialgebra induces a dendriform D-bialgebra structure on the direct sum of two copies of its underlying vector space.

title: The first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable
abstract: We show that any ring of totally real abelian integers has a JR-number and therefore the first-order theory of every ring of totally real abelian integers is undecidable. It then follows that the first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable and that there is one formula without parameters defining $\Z$ in any such ring. The main arithmetic input is a recent paper of Bajpai, Das, Kedlaya, and Mello proving that the houses of cyclotomic integers form a well-ordered subset of $\R$.

title: Betti numbers of powers of Ferrers ideals and edge ideals of threshold graphs
abstract: We provide explicit formulas for the Betti numbers of all powers of Ferrers ideals and edge ideals of threshold graphs.

title: Log-optimal two-sample testing by betting
abstract: For each standard Borel observation space, we construct a single anytime-valid two-sample procedure that is asymptotically log-optimal for every pair of unknown probability laws and every limiting ratio of diverging sample sizes, including zero and infinity. For independent balanced pairs, the optimal log-wealth rate is $2\JS(P,Q)$, where $\JS$ is the Jensen--Shannon divergence. Unequal sizes yield weighted Jensen--Shannon information and the one-sample limit $\log W(n_1,n_2)/n_2\to\KL(Q\|P)$ when $n_1/n_2\to\infty$. Refining finite partitions and logarithmic-loss learning with measurable characteristic kernels provide universal constructions. Our main contribution is the generality of our construction, and its connections to classical batch efficiency notions. Practical implementations allow continuous classifier fine-tuning, as demonstrated on finite alphabets, Gaussian data, and handwritten digits.

title: Slow and rapid mixing in $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory
abstract: The Ising model under Glauber dynamics on the torus is known to exhibit a phase transition in its mixing time. The mixing is exponentially slow when $β>β_c$ and logarithmically fast when $β<β_c$. In this paper, we generalize the slow-mixing result to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory when $β$ is large enough. This is a higher-dimensional analogue of the Ising model, with spins on $k$-cells. Specifically, on the torus of any dimension $m \ge k+2$, we prove explicit exponential lower bounds on the mixing time of Glauber dynamics when $β$ is sufficiently large. More precisely, we prove that the result holds for a broader class of dynamics, allowing more than one $k$-cell to change its value at each step of the algorithm. Finally, we show that there are distinct slow and rapid mixing regimes, as for sufficiently small $β$ the Dobrushin condition is satisfied for Glauber dynamics under the heat-bath rule, which implies logarithmic mixing.

title: Weighted $H^p$--$L^q$ estimates for fractional operators with multiple kernels under a strengthened Hörmander condition
abstract: We study a scale of strengthened fractional Hörmander conditions, indexed by $δ\ge0$ and adapted to the Hardy spaces $H^p$, $0<p<1$, which was recently considered by Han and Wu [Y.~Han, H.~Wu, \emph{The weighted $H^p$ estimates for commutators of fractional integrals}, Potential Anal. \textbf{59} (2023), 1827--1850] for fractional integrals with a single kernel. We show that these conditions form a strictly decreasing scale in $δ$, and we compute the exact range of $δ$ for a natural family of homogeneous kernels. We then apply them to the integral operators \[ T_αf(x)=\int_{\RR^{n}}k_1(x-A_1y)\cdots k_m(x-A_my)\, f(y)\,dy, \] where $A_1,\dots,A_m$ are invertible matrices and $\frac n{q_1}+\dots+\frac n{q_m}=n-α$, $0<α<n$. Assuming that each kernel $k_i$ satisfies an $L^{p_i}$ size condition of order $n-n/q_i$ and the Hörmander condition of order $δ=n(\frac1p-1)$, we obtain, for $\max\{\frac n{n+1},\frac n{n+α}\}<p<1$ and $1/q=1/p-α/n$, the $H^{p}_{w^p}(\RR^{n})-L^{q}_{w^q}(\RR^{n})$ boundedness of $T_α$ for weights $w$ such that $w^{a}\in\mathcal A_1$, where $\frac1a=\frac1q-\sum_i\frac1{p_i}$, and $w(A_ix)\le c\,w(x)$ a.e. For a single kernel, this relaxes the smoothness and weight conditions of a recent result of Han and Wu. No homogeneity is assumed on the kernels; the case $k_i(x)=Ω_i(x)|x|^{-n/q_i}$ with $Ω_i$ homogeneous of degree zero is included. Finally, we show that the strengthened condition cannot be replaced by the classical fractional Hörmander condition.

title: On two-dimensional affine Springer fibres
abstract: We extend results of Spaltenstein on irreducible components of two-dimensional usual Springer fibres in reductive groups of simply lace type to the case of two-dimensional affine Springer fibres associated to loop groups. One of our methods is to relate these affine Springer fibres with certain subsets of the affine Weyl group.

title: Dual-Mode Extremum Seeking for a Class of Unknown Controlled Diffusions
abstract: A dual-mode extremum-seeking controller is developed for unknown nonlinear systems with affine control inputs driven by persistent Brownian process noise. The controller uses a single measured cost, without state estimation or differentiation of the measurement. Bounded cosine feedback generates, through Lie-bracket averaging, a proportional--integral (PI) action: the proportional action stabilizes a feasible minimum of the cost on the time scale of the plant, and the integral action adapts a bias toward the unknown input that regulates the plant at that minimum. The averaged closed loop is a PI-regulated diffusion that retains the process noise, and its stability condition does not require knowledge of the control direction. Under a regional Lyapunov condition on the averaged dynamics, an exact periodic response of the noise-free closed loop is constructed and serves as the center of a Lyapunov function with bounds uniform in the excitation frequency. Exit-probability estimates show that, for small noise and large excitation frequency, trajectories reach a prescribed neighborhood of the optimum and remain there for times exponential in the inverse noise variance, with exponentially small failure probability. Under an additional stochastic contraction condition, the closed loop is approximated uniformly in time, in mean square before common exit, by its averaged diffusion driven by the same Brownian motion, with an error that decreases with the excitation frequency. The regional regulation conditions are verified for a planar hydrodynamic trap with an unknown stagnation-point offset and actuator sign. Simulations illustrate intensity-only confinement of a Brownian particle, integral compensation of the holding input, and axial-strip exit statistics.

title: Odd-degree cycles and rationality of Peskine sixfolds of discriminant 24
abstract: Benedetti and Faenzi conjectured that, for a general trivector $σ\in\mathcal D^{1,6,10}$, the Peskine sixfold $X_1^σ$ is rational if the Brauer class $β$ on the associated K3 surface vanishes. We prove this implication for every $σ$ in a nonempty Zariski open subset $U\subset\mathcal D^{1,6,10}$. When $β=0$, we construct a line on the generic fiber of the Peskine fibration after a cubic field extension and use odd-degree descent to obtain a line over the original function field. We extend criteria for rationality to smooth complete intersections of an arbitrary number of quadrics under suitable hypotheses. Finally, we describe the derived category of the generic fiber of the Peskine fibration in terms of a twisted nodal curve of arithmetic genus two.

title: Discrete Hyperbolic Cosecant Distributions
abstract: We introduce three families of discrete hyperbolic cosecant probability distributions, supported either bilaterally on $\mathbb{Z}$ or unilaterally on $\mathbb{N}_0$, inspired by series evaluations of Srinivasa Ramanujan. We determine their exact normalization constants in terms of singular values of complete elliptic integrals and the Gaußian constant $G=\varpi/π$ with the lemniscate constant $Γ^2(1/4)/(2\sqrt{2π})$ by explicitly calculating some series, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{κ\in \mathbb{Z}} 2κ\operatorname{cosech}(κπ) = G^2 + \frac{1}π. $$ Furthermore, by connecting these distributions to Fourier transforms of powers of the hyperbolic secant and applying the Poisson summation formula, we obtain closed-form evaluations for even moments and hyperbolic secant lattice sums, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathrm{sech}^4(k π) = \frac{2}{3} \left(G^4 + G^2 + \frac{1}π\right). $$ This machinery proves conjectures on lattice sums arising in electrostatics proposed by Vigren and Dieckmann (Symmetry, 2020).

title: The conductors of fibered Burnside rings
abstract: We give an explicit formula for the conductors of the primitive idempotents of fibered Burnside algebras of finite rank. This formula generalizes previous results for Burnside rings, monomial representation rings, and cyclic fibers, removing the coprimality condition required in the latter case. We also derive some consequences for cyclic fiber groups and $p$-groups.

title: A proof of the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture on entropy maximization for cube projections
abstract: We complete the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture: among the one-dimensional projections of the uniform measure on a cube, differential entropy is maximized precisely in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. Pang proved the conjecture in every dimension at least $150$. We prove the remaining dimensions using polynomial entropy bounds in dimensions three through six and exact certificates for derivatives of the logarithm of the diagonal projection density. The proof uses integer arithmetic and certified one-dimensional integration. We also derive quantitative stability estimates and determine the optimal asymptotic coefficient of a linear stability bound. The source code and the outputs of all finite verifications accompany the paper.

title: Self-adjoint boundary conditions for equation-free multiscale modelling
abstract: Equation-free modelling is a computation multiscale modelling scheme for the simulation of complex dynamical systems. Efficient computations are achieved by solving the given microscale model in small, well-separated `patches' spread across the space-time domain, with each patch providing a data point for the macroscale simulation. Patch coupling bridges the unsimulated space between patches and supports the macroscale dynamics. Accurate simulations require coupling conditions that preserve underlying symmetries of the microscale equation. Failing to preserve such symmetries may result in an unphysical macroscale simulation that does not satisfy required conservation laws. Here we develop equation-free modelling that preserves self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models defined by a compact self-adjoint operator on a bounded domain with fixed boundary conditions. This new design for equation-free modelling greatly increases the range of systems for which equation-free modelling is applicable.

title: Two-Sided Projection-Based Model Reduction of Parametric Generalized Algebraic Riccati Equations via Grassmann-Manifold Optimization
abstract: Parametric generalized algebraic Riccati equations arise in many-query problems in optimal control, state estimation, and filtering, where repeated full-order solutions may become computationally prohibitive for large-scale systems. In this paper, within a projection-based model reduction framework, we propose a two-sided projection approach that constructs reduced bases by minimizing the aggregate relative two-sided projection error of Riccati solution snapshots. Under suitable dissipativity assumptions, the resulting Galerkin-projected PGARE admits a unique symmetric positive semidefinite stabilizing solution. For error assessment, we employ an existing residual-based a posteriori error estimator for the full-order Riccati residual. A projection-based error decomposition developed in this work provides the theoretical motivation for the proposed basis construction. To accommodate clustered solution manifolds, we extend the framework to localized model reduction by combining parameter-space proximity and solution-space correlation for clustering, with classifier-based online basis selection. Numerical experiments on parameterized heat-conduction problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed global and localized approaches in terms of approximation accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Stabilizing Parabolic Vector Bundles
abstract: For an irreducible parabolic flat vector bundle of rank $r < 2\sqrt{g}$ on a genus $g$ curve, we prove that an analytically general isomonodromic deformation is stable. This refines Landesman-Litt's semistability result for bundles of rank $< 2\sqrt{g+1}$. The proof applies the non-generically globally generated (non-GGG) lemma to establish infinitesimal obstructions to extending destabilizing subbundles of semistable bundles.

title: Fundamental group and $Q$-curvature on open four-manifolds
abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a complete, connected, and non-compact four-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature and nonnegative $Q$-curvature. If $g$ is not Ricci-flat, we show that both the fundamental group $π_1(M)$ and the integral of $Q$-curvature are finite, satisfying $$|π_1(M)|\int_MQ_g dμ_g\leq 8π^2$$ with the equality holding if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to $(\mathbb{R}^4, e^{2u}|\mathrm{d}x|^2)$ with vanishing isoperimetric ratio.

title: Nondoubling Calderón-Zygmund theory across geometries
abstract: We develop a Calderón--Zygmund theory without the doubling property, a metric or a martingale structure. Our measure spaces carry an exhausting family of admissible sets with recursive child partitions. A stopping-time construction gives a decomposition of an integrable function, with a bounded good part and bad terms that cancel on the parents of the stopping sets. We introduce the corresponding atomic Hardy and BMO spaces, establish their duality and interpolation properties, and prove weak-type $(1,1)$ and Hardy-space bounds for singular integral operators under a Hörmander condition and a size estimate between each stopping set and its parent. We apply this framework to arbitrary flow trees, whose associated flow measures need not be either locally or globally doubling. As a result, we obtain endpoint bounds for Riesz transforms and spectral multipliers satisfying a scale-invariant Sobolev condition of order greater than $3/2$ in this setting.

title: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
abstract: We show that a single Legendrian surgery on the canonical contact structure of the unit cotangent bundle $ST^*K$ of the Klein bottle $K$ produces a planar contact $3$--manifold $(Y,ξ)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings. The fillings are obtained from the disk cotangent bundle $DT^*K$ by attaching a single Weinstein $2$--handle along the images of one Legendrian knot under the powers of a contactomorphism of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, no positive power of which extends over $DT^*K$. The construction takes place in a planar open book of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, and $(Y,ξ)$ is contactomorphic to Baykur's recent example of a planar contact $3$--manifold with infinitely many Stein fillings. Since $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$ has a unique minimal symplectic filling up to homeomorphism, finiteness of fillings is not preserved under Legendrian surgery, even for planar contact $3$--manifolds. The same construction gives the planar contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings found earlier by the author.

title: Pole rigidity in root-optimal rational approximation of the exponential on infinite sectors
abstract: The optimal root convergence factor for uniform rational approximation of the exponential on an infinite sector is classical. We prove that, for every fixed infinite sector of opening less than $π$, the normalized pole-counting measures of any reduced root-optimal sequence, after scaling the poles by degree, converge weakly to a uniquely determined probability measure supported on a compact analytic arc outside the sector. For the half-line, the corresponding pole law was previously announced by Stahl and Schmelzer; our new result covers sectors of positive opening. The proof rules out boundary pole accumulation and controls an exponentially small Hermite residual through reflection and noncancellation, without assuming interpolation or orthogonality. We explicitly construct the equilibrium measure and its supporting arc in terms of a zero of a Ferrers function, and relate this parameterization to the Gonchar--Rakhmanov theta equation. We also obtain a degree-independent comparison for simultaneous approximation of finitely many $\varphi$-functions with a common denominator. Numerical pole distributions support the theoretical law.

title: New constructions of optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for quasi-block monotone Ferrers diagrams
abstract: Constant dimension subspace codes (CDCs) have become an important object in coding theory due to their applications in random network coding. The paper is devoted to constructing optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for block Ferrers diagrams, which play a crucial role in the multilevel construction of CDCs. Let \(\mathbb{F}_q\) be the finite field with \(q\) elements of characteristic \(p\), \(P\) be a power of \(p\), and \(e\) be a positive integer. Let \(L=\mathbb F_{q^{eP}}\) and \(σ\) be the Frobenius \(\mathbb F_q\)-automorphism of \(L\), set \(N=σ^e-\mathrm{id}\). Based on the multiplicative property of the kernel filtration of the nilpotent map \(N\), we construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for block monotone diagrams. Specifically, considering \(n \times l\) Ferrers diagrams, we prove that optimal codes always exist for block monotone diagrams when \(n = eP\). Furthermore, by employing puncturing on columns, we prove that optimal codes also always exist for block strictly monotone diagrams, removing the restriction \(n = eP\). Consequently, optimal codes always exist for block upper triangular diagrams, specifically for maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD)-constructible block diagram pairs, which generalizes the corresponding results in \cite{neri2024,calderini2026}, in which the rank distance or the characteristic is restricted. Furthermore, by employing both puncturing and shortening on columns, we prove that optimal codes always exist for quasi-block strictly monotone diagrams, thereby generalizing the corresponding results in \cite{pratihar2023, zhang2019}. The optimal codes constructed in this paper will potentially be beneficial to the further construction of CDCs.

title: Classification of critical points of heat kernels on flat tori and Riemann theta functions
abstract: For any two-dimensional flat torus $E_τ:=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathbb Zτ)$ and any $t>0$, we prove that the heat kernel $p_τ(z,t)$ has either four or six critical points on $z\in E_τ$ (i.e., including four trivial critical points and at most one pair of nontrivial critical points). This is interestingly consistent with Lin-Wang's remarkable result (Ann. Math. 2010) for the Green function. The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given.

title: Delay Closure of Observable Dynamics for the Heat Equation
abstract: We study finite-delay representations of point observables, which are solution values at selected spatial locations, for spatially discretized heat equations. We show that the observables satisfy closed dynamical systems whose evolution depends only on their own history, without requiring solution values elsewhere in the domain. Using semigroup properties, we analyze low-rank approximate closures that can use substantially fewer delay terms than the exact representation. We consider two computational approaches: direct least-squares fitting of delay coefficients from observable trajectories and shift-invert Krylov approximation of the semigroup using preconditioned linear solves. Numerical experiments for constant- and variable-coefficient heat equations in one, two, and three dimensions illustrate the effects of memory length and sensor information on prediction. The results are consistent with the theoretical analysis.

title: Averaged-Cost Control with Shared Feedback under Model Uncertainty
abstract: This paper studies the shared-feedback design problem for finite-horizon averaged-cost control under model uncertainty represented by a joint law over the model parameter and initial state. One feedback map is shared across all realizations and uses only time and the current state as online inputs. We develop two methods: the nonlinear adjoint method combines forward closed-loop solves, backward adjoints, and joint-law policy gradients, while the linear moment method gives exact cost and gradient formulas for a homogeneous linear-quadratic design model by propagating conditional second moments. Numerical studies compare averaged and nominal designs for time-dependent neural feedback and static linear feedback in nonlinear Van der Pol and Stuart-Landau systems; the static gains are designed from oscillator linearizations and evaluated on the original nonlinear systems. Averaged design has lower cost in most comparisons.

title: On p-adic modularity of abelian threefolds with imaginary multiplication and rational p-isogeny
abstract: We prove $p$-adic modularity of a certain class of abelian threefolds over $\mathbf{Q}$ (with imaginary multiplication and rational $p$-isogeny), including the Jacobians of some genus 3 curves known as Picard curves. More precisely, we study a deformation problem for residual 3-dimensional totally reducible Galois pseudorepresentations over an imaginary quadratic field which are ordinary at primes over $p$ and conjugate self-dual. We show that under certain conditions the universal pseudodeformation ring in any weight (including the non-classical low weight corresponding to an abelian threefold) is isomorphic to a specialization of the ordinary Hida Hecke algebra on $U(2,1)$. The conditions that we assume are essentially class group conditions as well as weak regularity of the Hecke algebras in sufficiently high classical weights.

title: Gravitational and Maxwell--Proca-Type Structures in a Variational Metric-Affine Framework
abstract:
We study Einstein's nonsymmetric metric-affine Lagrangian density with a generally nonsymmetric metric and an affine connection treated as independent variational variables. The resulting connection equation belongs to the classical Einstein--Hlavatý--Tonnelat framework, while the unrestricted metric Euler--Lagrange equation is analyzed without a divergence constraint on the antisymmetric metric density.
  Its symmetric part takes the form of Einstein-type gravitational equations with geometrically induced source terms and reduces to the vacuum Einstein equations in the torsion-free limit. The antisymmetric part becomes a geometric constitutive relation based on the irreducible decomposition of torsion. Its contracted four-divergence yields a general vector-field equation with geometric source and response terms. Under a trace--axial reduction, $Q=0$ gives a source-free Maxwell-type equation, whereas constant nonzero $Q$ gives a Proca-type equation.
  Independently, a trace of the generalized Bianchi identities yields the homogeneous Maxwell-type pair associated with the torsion trace, while the connection equation implies a Lorenz-type condition. Thus gravitational, constitutive, Maxwell--Proca-type, and Lorenz-type structures arise as compatible consequences of one metric-affine variational system. The antisymmetric dynamical level is generated by the contracted four-divergence of its constitutive level. No independent electromagnetic or matter field is introduced.

title: Delaunay Combinatorics of the Moduli and Teichmüller Space of Closed Genus-Two Riemann Surfaces
abstract: Every closed Riemann surface of genus two is hyperelliptic, so it is determined by six branch points on the sphere, which become cone points of angle pi in the quotient orbifold metric. The Delaunay decomposition of these cone points, dual to the Voronoi diagram of the Weierstrass points, gives a trivalent graph with eight vertices, twelve edges and six faces. We classify these graphs. When the dual triangulation is simple there are exactly two types, dual to the octahedron and to a stacked triangulation, with orientation-preserving automorphism groups of orders 24 and 2, and we determine the Whitehead-move (diagonal-flip) orbit connecting them. Allowing bigons, the orbit closes at exactly twenty types. Iterated edge contraction from the two simple types gives a seven-level hierarchy of 2, 6, 22, 32, 22, 5 and 1 types, ending at two vertices joined by six parallel edges; closing under both contraction and expansion gives all 280 maps on the sphere with six vertices and no vertex of degree one. The rank of the linear cone-angle system of each type equals the real dimension 6 of the Teichmüller space. We realize both simple types by explicit hyperbolic cone spheres, in closed form for the octahedral type, build the corresponding genus-two surfaces by cutting and doubling, and show that the boundary x_e = 0 of the angle system is exactly the concyclicity of four branch points. The classification, the automorphism groups and the flip orbit are formally verified in Lean 4, and every enumeration is reproduced by an independent program, which also determines which types are realized by Delaunay decompositions.

title: Decompositions of the diagonal of complete intersections in products of projective spaces
abstract: We study rationality of very general complete intersections in products of projective spaces. By constructing specific reference varieties and apply specialization method in the form of relative torsion orders, we extend the quintic constructions by Hotchkiss and the quartic constructions by Böhning, Graf von Bothmer, Pirutka and Zhang to very general complete intersections in products in every characteristic. In particular, we prove that very general quartic hypersurfaces of positive dimension admit no decomposition of the diagonal in every characteristic.

title: Proper implies improper for the chromatic symmetric function
abstract: Stanley's question of whether the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees has been unanswered for over thirty years. It has now been checked for trees with at most 29 vertices, and for several classes of trees. There is the perception that answering the question might be easier for the class of ``proper'' trees, i.e. trees where every vertex is either a leaf or adjacent to a leaf. In this paper, we show that an affirmative answer for a subclass of proper trees, which we call ``$k$-weighted'', is equivalent to an affirmative answer for all trees. In addition, we show that in the class of $k$-weighted trees, the coefficients carry redundant information. In fact we give a closed formula for obtaining the redundant coefficients from other coefficients.

title: Irreducible Projective Polynomials
abstract: Suppose $q=p^{s_1}$ and $σ=p^{s_2}$ for a prime $p$ and $s_1,s_2\in\mathbb{N}.$ In this paper, we characterize for which values of $p, d, s_1, s_2, \ell$ there exists an irreducible polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of the form \begin{align*} x^\frac{σ^d-1}{\ell}+\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}a_j x^\frac{σ^j-1}{\ell} \end{align*} for fixed $d,\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ where $\ell\mid (σ-1).$ In particular, we enumerate irreducible polynomials of this form.

title: Field algebras associated with non-symmetric lattices
abstract: Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields. We associate to every finite-rank lattice $L$ equipped with an arbitrary bilinear form a canonical field algebra $V_L$, generalizing the Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras. We then study potential definitions of commutants in this setting and analyze when they are realized as subfield algebras. Finally, we realize these constructions geometrically by looking at the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending previous results from Dominic Joyce.

title: Support recovery of diffusion models under the manifold hypothesis
abstract: We study diffusion models under the manifold hypothesis with possibly large score estimation and discretization errors, and show that while they may not exactly recover the data distribution, they will exactly recover the support (or data manifold). In continuous time, we use a Lyapunov function to show that even if the relative score estimation error is fixed (and not necessarily vanishing), then the rate at which the process approaches the support is $O(\sqrt{(T-t)|\log(T-t)|})$ as $t \to T$, where $T$ is the final time. In discrete time, we use geometric time steps with a fixed (non-vanishing) ratio and show that with a fixed (also not small) relative score estimation error, the process approaches the data manifold exponentially with the number of iterations. The proof relies on controlling a Gaussian measure of a neighborhood of the cut-locus of the data manifold, using a polynomial approximation argument combined with quantitative semi-algebraic estimates.

title: A Las Vegas algorithm for satisfiable SAT formulas, with an application to timetabling
abstract: Many scheduling problems need many different feasible timetables, and a view of how much freedom each event has. We study a Las Vegas algorithm that samples satisfying assignments of a Boolean formula one variable at a time: it draws each value from an estimate of its conditional probability, propagates, and restarts on a contradiction. Every output is a checked solution and comes with the exact probability of producing it. We prove that a run succeeds with probability at least $2^{-K}$, where $K$ is the expected Kullback--Leibler divergence between the true and estimated conditional probabilities along the run of a uniform solution. We also bound the distance of the outputs from uniform from the samples alone; it is a divergence in the opposite direction to $K$, so a sampler can succeed more often while being farther from uniform. On generated timetabling instances counted exactly, belief propagation on the timetabling problem brings $K$ to at most about one bit, and the estimated counts are within 2% of the exact ones.
