On a real university instance of the International Timetabling Competition 2019, rerunning only the failed runs delivered all 72 requested timetables with each of two estimators. Belief propagation succeeds in 31% of runs. Steered by a Markov chain that carries a nearly feasible timetable, it succeeds in 65% of runs, with outputs at least 300 bits from uniform. There the importance weights are too uneven to estimate the number of timetables, and we certify a lower bound instead. For random 3-SAT, an estimator whose $K$ grows logarithmically would give a polynomial-time Las Vegas algorithm beyond the densities at which any algorithm is proved to succeed; we conjecture that one exists below the satisfiability threshold.

title: A Note on the Cosupport of Balmer-Favi Idempotents
abstract: Let $g_x$ be the Balmer-Favi idempotent at a point $x$ of the spectrum of a rigidly-compactly generated tensor triangulated category. We study the equality $\operatorname{Cosupp}(g_x)=\operatorname{gen}(x)$ by expressing $g_x$ as a local dual. We prove the equality for the derived category of a Noetherian scheme and for the stable module category of a finite group scheme over a field of positive characteristic. For $E(n)$-local spectra we express the maps between distinct monochromatic layers of the sphere in terms of the chromatic fracture square. The height-two splitting gives the equality through height two at every prime. For a Noetherian local ring we characterize the Gorenstein property by the form of its closed-point idempotent.

title: On stretched Kostka polynomials
abstract: Stretched Kostka polynomials are defined by $f_{λ,μ}(N) := K_{Nλ,Nμ}$, where $K_{λ,μ}$ denotes the corresponding Kostka number. In 2004, King-Tollu-Toumazet conjectured that, for every integer $k$, there are only finitely many polynomials $f_{λ,μ}(N)$ such that $f_{λ,μ}(1)=k$. For $k=3$, KTT also conjectured that there are exactly two such polynomials. We prove both conjectures via Ehrhart theory, by counting lattice points in families of rational polytopes with a fixed set of normals.

title: Quadratic Embedding Constants of Block Graphs and Characterization of Cactus-like Graphs
abstract: A (finite or infinite) connected graph is called \textit{cactus-like} if every pair of distinct maximal cliques has at most one vertex in common and its clique graph is a tree. Equivalently, a cactus-like graph is a block graph whose clique graph is a tree. We prove that a finite connected graph $G$ with at least two vertices is cactus-like if and only if its quadratic embedding constant satisfies $\mathrm{QEC}(G)<-1/2$. Moreover, we establish upper and lower bounds for $\mathrm{QEC}(G)$ in terms of the clique degree of a block graph $G$. For the proofs, we develop a method for constructing a conditionally negative definite kernel on a block graph by concatenating local kernels along geodesics in the block graph. Concrete examples include free products of complete graphs and trees.

title: Leafwise thermalization near vacuum for the inhomogeneous Landau equation with very soft and Coulomb potentials
abstract:
We study the inhomogeneous Landau equation with very soft and Coulomb potentials, $γ\in[-3,-2]$, for data near vacuum. Unlike for $γ>-2$, the collisions along a free trajectory have a divergent time integral, so the dynamics is not a perturbation of free transport. It is instead organized along \emph{leaves}, the velocity distributions in the variable $z=x-tv$: on each leaf the solution follows a homogeneous Landau flow with a leaf-dependent collision rate, first far from equilibrium and then near a Maxwellian whose parameters approximately solve a compressible Euler system with the free-expansion prefactor $t^{-2}$.
  For data of size $ε$, analytic in velocity and Gaussian in space, we prove global existence of classical solutions, relaxation of every leaf (not uniform in $x/t$), and convergence of the leaf parameters at rate $t^{-1}$. The solution scatters in $L^1$ to the free transport of a thermalized profile that generally remains at a fixed relative distance from the data. The $L^1$ distance to the scattering state decays like $(1+ε\log t)^{-(p-3)/p}$ at $γ=-2$ and $(1+εt^{|γ|-2})^{-(p-3)/p}$ for $γ<-2$, where $\langle v\rangle^{-p}$ is the velocity decay of the data; these rates are sharp when the spatial profiles stay away from Maxwellians. Each leaf relaxes on its own clock: as a power of $t$ proportional to its collision rate at $γ=-2$, and as a stretched exponential of its clock for $γ<-2$. We also prove the near-Maxwellian and homogeneous results we need beyond the literature, including at $γ=-2$.

title: Joint Channel Estimation, Data Detection, and Phase Noise Tracking in Massive MIMO Systems
abstract: Communication over multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems is degraded by phase noise (PN) arising from imperfect local oscillators, with PN becoming more severe at higher carrier frequencies. Existing methods either rely on linearized Kalman-filter approaches or apply variational Bayes (VB) only to individual stages, such as data detection under a static phase prior, or channel estimation alone, leaving no unified framework that tracks an evolving PN process consistently across pilot and data transmission. This paper develops such a framework for uplink massive MIMO. Specifically, we first propose VB-Tracking, which employs von Mises priors and coordinate-ascent VB inference to jointly estimate the channel and track the transmit and receive PN trajectories during the pilot phase without linearization. We then propose VB-Detecting for joint data detection and phase tracking by absorbing the transmit PN into a composite transmit variable. Using a sequentially propagated von Mises predictive prior, the composite variable admits an exact closed-form posterior. Finally, we propose VB-Refining, which periodically re-estimates the channel during data transmission using the soft posterior moments of reliably detected transmit symbols as virtual pilots. We show that VB-Detecting scales linearly in the number of users, receive antennas, constellation size, and iterations. Simulations against EKF-EP, EKF-ZF, and JED baselines show that VB-Tracking, VB-Detecting, and VB-Refining together achieve lower channel NMSE and symbol error rate, with the performance gap widening at high SNR and under severe PN.

title: Surrogate Symbols in Wireless Communications
abstract: Co-channel interference (CCI), caused by the inevitable aggressive channel reuse in dense deployments, remains a critical bottleneck for current and future wireless communication systems. In this paper, we address this bottleneck in an N-co-channel wireless communications network of single-antenna transmitters and receivers. The limiting case of this problem leads to a novel "thought experiment": If each receiver's own desired channel link is simultaneously completely blocked, can a Maximum Likelihood Detection at each receiver still recover its transmitted symbol? In the traditional way of thinking, the answer is no: The receiver obtains nothing but co-channel interference (CCI) plus thermal noise, and a receiver-side phase rotation cannot help, since there is no desired signal to align. Given only the channel matrix H -- and no knowledge of the transmitted symbols -- can the transmitters' phases be chosen so that the received signal becomes "almost" the desired symbol at every receiver? We show that the answer is yes. We first develop the underlying framework for the general case (nonzero own-channel link case), turning classical co-channel systems into a novel discrete phase-optimization problem, "Game of Phases: Surrogate Symbol Optimization", and present two algorithms, "Minimum Phased-Interference Power algorithm (MiPIP)" and "Maximum Phased-Interference Support (MaPRIS)". We then show that the MaPRIS resolves the thought experiment: it converts hostile CCI into an "almost" desired symbol even when the own desired channel link is zero, yielding the counter-intuitive result that higher CCI variance yields higher SINR. Extensive simulation results confirm the findings. The gain promised by the proposed algorithms comes on top of any other CCI reduction techniques as our framework here is based on a bottom-line baseband model.

title: Compromise Optimization over Incompatible Efficient Sets Using a Minimax Distance Approach with Polyhedral Characterization and an Application to Fisheries Management
abstract: The efficient sets associated with different decision-makers may have an empty intersection, even when their objectives are linear and the common feasible region is a compact polytope. In this paper, we consider a compromise criterion that minimizes the largest weighted distance from a feasible decision to the respective efficient sets of the decision-makers. First, we establish the existence of an optimal compromise and show that the formulation recovers the common efficient set whenever it is nonempty. We then derive a lower bound based on the separation of efficient sets and obtain an exact formulation in terms of finitely many linear programs by exploiting their polyhedral structure. Next, we examine the effect of approximating the efficient sets and establish a stability bound expressed in terms of the Hausdorff distance. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of the proposed approach through a numerical study of harvest allocation between two interconnected fishing zones.

title: The Walsh spectrum of the Dobbertin APN function
abstract: APN functions yield the best resistance to differential attacks when used as a building block of a block cipher. APN functions induced by monomials over finite fields have received particular interest both for their simplicity and their unique properties. A key property of APN functions is their linearity, which has been determined for all known APN monomials outside of the Dobbertin APN monomials. In this paper, we close this gap and determine the complete Walsh spectrum and in particular the linearity of the Dobbertin APN monomial, answering a problem that has been open for more than 20 years. Using known connections, our result also yields the asymptotically largest Sidon sets in elementary abelian $2$-groups constructed so far as well as binary linear codes of minimum distance $5$ that are almost optimal.

title: Spectral Conditioning of Weighted Multivariate Vandermonde Operators via Radial Beurling--Selberg Approximation
abstract: We establish explicit eigenvalue bounds for Gram matrices of weighted multivariate Vandermonde operators with separated nodes on a torus. The squared magnitudes of the weights are samples of a nonnegative radial spectral energy density whose profile has bounded variation, finite energy, and finite weighted variation cost; compact support is not required. The estimate holds in every dimension and depends on the periodic Euclidean separation and the weighted variation integral. For compactly supported profiles, our analysis combines a signed layer decomposition with the ball approximants of Holt and Vaaler; the noncompactly supported case follows by truncation. Combining the resulting radial envelopes with a bandlimited sampling identity based on Poisson summation yields the spectral bounds by eliminating off-diagonal interactions and nonzero diagonal aliases. The result covers nonmonotone profiles and discontinuous radial low-pass filters, and it is complemented by a global elementary upper bound on the Holt--Vaaler cost that exhibits two radial regimes.

title: Weak and Strong Moments of Log-Concave Measures
abstract: Let $X\in\mathbb{R}^d$ be a log-concave random vector, and let $N$ be a seminorm on $\mathbb{R}^d$. For $p\ge 1$, we show that $\|N(X)\|_p$ is at most $\mathbb{E} N(X)+C s_p$, where $s_p$ is the supremum of $\|u(X)\|_p$ over all linear functionals $u$ satisfying $|u(x)|\le N(x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. A choice for $C$ is $2+5e/2$. This bound implies Latała's conjecture on weak and strong moments.

title: The cop number of the flower snarks, and the generalized Petersen graphs with cop number two
abstract:
We study two questions of Morris, Runte and Skelton (Australas. J. Combin. 83 (2022)) on the game of Cops and Robbers.
  First, we show that the flower snark $J_n$ has cop number $3$ for every $n\geq 5$, and that $J_3$ has cop number $2$. The upper bound comes from a three-cop strategy, which we call the rolling wall. It works on every connected graph whose vertices can be arranged in a cycle of columns, each dominated by a single vertex. Because only one cop moves on each turn, the same strategy also shows that the lazy cop number of $J_n$ is $3$ for $n\geq 5$.
  Second, we prove the conjecture of Morris, Runte and Skelton that the only generalized Petersen graphs with cop number $2$ are $\mathrm{GP}(n,1)$ and the four graphs $\mathrm{GP}(6,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(8,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(9,3)$ and $\mathrm{GP}(12,3)$. The new ingredient is an explicit robber strategy showing that two cops do not suffice on $\mathrm{GP}(3k,k)$ and $\mathrm{GP}(4k,k)$ for $k\geq 4$.
  The theorem on flower snarks and all of the new lower bounds have been formally verified in the Lean 4 proof assistant.

title: Determinants of amphichiral knots of braid index at most three
abstract: We show that an odd number n is the determinant of an amphichiral knot of braid index at most three if and only if both n and n + 4 are sums of two squares. The proof rests on the known description of amphichiral knots of braid index three as closures of alternating 3-braid words with a rotation or reflection symmetry (Birman--Menasco, Stoimenov, Jung). Determinant formulas for closed 3-braids are also known (e.g. through the reduced Burau representation at t = -1); what is added here is their evaluation on the two symmetric families, which gives the condition on n + 4, and an explicit construction for the converse. For amphichiral knots of braid index three this describes which determinants occur, which bears on the determinant part of a question of Jung. We did not find the statement in the literature we searched. As a consequence, for an odd n with n + 4 not a sum of two squares, every amphichiral knot with determinant n has braid index at least five; we test this on 4,999 amphichiral knots of Burton's census with up to 19 crossings whose determinant satisfies this hypothesis.

title: Rank-One Sutured Instanton Homology Detects Homology Products
abstract: We prove that a balanced sutured manifold $(M,γ)$ satisfying $\dim_{\mathbb C} SHI(M,γ)=1$ is an integral homology product; that is, $H_*(M,R_-(γ);\mathbb Z)=H_*(M,R_+(γ);\mathbb Z)=0$. Consequently, for every taut balanced sutured manifold $(M,γ)$, $SHI(M,γ)\cong\mathbb C$ if and only if $(M,γ)$ is a product sutured manifold. The proof uses the enhanced Euler characteristic of $SHI$ and a specialization formula for sutured torsion.

title: Minimality of the Double Kite among Strict Two-Pole Configurations of Unit Triangles
abstract: A strict unit-triangle configuration is a finite connected family of closed equilateral unit triangles in which distinct triangles are disjoint or meet at a common vertex, and no vertex belongs to more than two triangles. A vertex belonging to exactly one triangle is a pole. We prove that every strict configuration with one or two poles contains at least fourteen triangles, a sharp bound for two poles attained by the double kite and the reverse double kite. A strict four-regular configuration whose contact graph has an edge cut of size at most two contains at least twenty-eight triangles. A decomposition into three strict two-pole components requires forty-two triangles; both known ring constructions attain the bound. The proof reduces minimal counterexamples to two-connected contact graphs, applies area bounds to complementary unit-sided polygons, and excludes the remaining cases by exact angle certificates. The supplement contains 13,668 stored marked records, 233 exclusion certificates, a standard-library verifier, and independent checks of the complete enumeration.

title: Martingale and signed diffusive optimal transport: geodesics and gradient flows
abstract: In signed diffusive transport, a path of probability densities $ρ_t$ on the circle and a momentum $m_t$ satisfy $\partial_tρ=\partial_{xx}m$, and the cost of the path is the action $\int_0^1\int m^2/(2ρ)\,dx\,dt$. The diffusivity $m/ρ$ is an unknown of this variational problem and can take either sign. On the real line, the constraint $m\ge0$ gives the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem of Huesmann and Trevisan. We study geodesics and minimizing movements, which discretize gradient flows. For signed geodesics, we prove the $Γ$-convergence of the time-discrete problems for all probability endpoints, and of the fully discrete Fourier-grid problems as the space and time meshes tend to zero independently, without a positive lower bound on the densities. For a modified Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme on the torus, we prove convergence along subsequences to a weak solution of a fourth-order equation, the Derrida-Lebowitz-Speer-Spohn equation for the entropy in dimension one, under the assumption that the densities of the scheme stay above a positive constant on every finite time interval. In dimension one, the normalized minimum values of a discretization with nonnegative momentum and of a discretization by martingale couplings with a fourth-moment cost converge to the same martingale transport cost, and we identify the limit of the minimizing movements with nonnegative momentum for potential energies with bounded second and third derivatives. We compute geodesics and modified JKO trajectories by Douglas-Rachford splitting and by an interior-point method, and bound the optimization errors of selected solutions by dual lower bounds evaluated in interval arithmetic. The computed geodesics approach zero density near the points where the diffusivity changes sign, and along computed trajectories of the modified JKO scheme the density minimum can fall below its initial value.

title: Interpolation, Factorization, and Approximation in the Numerical Radius Unit Ball
abstract:
We initiate a systematic study of Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and function theory for matrix-valued holomorphic functions on the unit disk taking values in the numerical radius unit ball - a class we term as $ν$-Schur functions.
  In contrast to the operator-norm setting, where commutatnt lifting reduces interpolation to the positivity of a single Pick matrix, we show that a natural one-parameter familty of Pick-type matrices arising from Ando's characterization is necessary but not sufficient for solvability. We overcome this obstruction by establishing two necessary and sufficient solvability criteria. The first is constructive, resting on a factorization of $ν$-Schur function $F=PGQ$ into a classical Schur function $G$ and bounded holomorphic matrix functions $P, Q$ coupled by a boundary condition. This yields an accompanying Choi-Li-type dilation representation. The second is dual and geometric, characterizing solvability via a Nehari-type distance from a cononical model-space interpolant to a subspace determined by the interpolation data.
  Finally, we introduce $ν$-inner functions - $ν$-Schur functions whose non-tangential boundary values lie almost everywhere in the set of extremal numerical contractions - and prove that every non-extremal problem admits a $ν$-inner solution. As a consequence, we obtain a numerical-radius Caratheodory approximation theorem: $ν$-inner functions are dense in the $ν$-Schur class under the compact-open topology.

title: Pólya inequalities on thin planar networks
abstract: We construct thin planar domains on which the Dirichlet and the Neumann Pólya inequalities both hold strictly. For the neighborhoods of a given finite connected embedded polygonal graph (branches and cycles are allowed) there is a single radius threshold below which both inequalities hold for every eigenvalue index. We also show that every nonempty bounded connected open set in the plane can be approximated, in measure and in the Hausdorff distance, by smooth simply connected domains satisfying both inequalities. Along the same sequence, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue tends to infinity, while each Neumann eigenvalue of fixed positive index tends to zero. In the special case of rectangular frames our estimates lead to explicit sufficient conditions, with no restriction on the aspect ratio.

title: Classification of ${\rm GL}_1(D)\times {\rm GL}_{n-1}(D)$-distinguished representations
abstract:
Let $D$ be a quaternion division algebra over a non-Archimedean
  local field $F$ of characteristic zero.
  We prove the conjecture of Dagar, Sharma, and Verma classifying irreducible smooth
  representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(D)$ distinguished by
  $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(D)$ for $n>2$.
  These are precisely the trivial representation and the
  irreducible normalized parabolic inductions
  $\one_{n-2}\timesτ$, where $τ$ is an infinite-dimensional
  irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(D)$ distinguished
  by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_1(D)$.
  The proof combines a choice of cuspidal inducing factor
  with orbit conditions and multisegment methods.

title: The Contact Process with Temporary Immunity on $\mathbb{Z}$
abstract: We develop a regeneration scheme for the one-dimensional contact process with temporary immunity, also known as the spatial SIRS process, a non-attractive interacting particle system. The key ingredient is a one-sided space-time shielding mechanism, constructed from infinite infection paths of an auxiliary process. These paths separate the evolution of the infection front from the configuration and graphical history left behind, allowing us to construct regeneration times without relying on attractiveness. The same shielding mechanism also provides coupling arguments for processes started from different initial configurations. Using this approach, we establish a law of large numbers and a functional central limit theorem for the right edge, existence and uniqueness of an invariant law for the process seen from the edge, and complete convergence. We also prove survival from every nonempty finite infected set for sufficiently large immunity-loss rates and derive an explicit extinction criterion.

title: Stability of Self-Similar Expansions for Self-Gravitating Hyperelastic Bodies
abstract: We consider the three-dimensional elastodynamics system with nonlocal gravitational coupling and nonlinear traction-free boundary conditions, modeling an isolated self-gravitating hyperelastic body, where the strain-energy function is assumed to be objective, isotropic, and homogeneous of degree $-1$. We prove nonlinear stability of a self-similarly expanding separable solution, recently constructed by the authors [JangLeslie2025], under radial perturbations satisfying the codimension-one constraint of zero total energy. Using a self-similar reformulation analogous to that developed for the mass-critical Euler--Poisson system in [HadzicJang2018CPAM], we recast the perturbed equation as a scalar nonlinear five-dimensional radial wave equation and the nonlinear traction-free boundary condition as a homogeneous Neumann condition. A key is to identify a quasilinear form of the leading-order spatial operator that is compatible with this boundary condition and yields coercive energy estimates. Our energy estimates capture the stabilizing effect of the background expansion and yield global existence and nonlinear codimension-one stability in self-similar variables.

title: A proof of Schmeisser's conjecture
abstract:
In 1977, Schmeisser proposed a strengthening of Sendov's conjecture: if all zeros of a polynomial $p$ of degree $n\ge2$ lie in the closed unit disk, then for every point $ξ$ in the convex hull of the zeros of $p$, there exists a critical point $ζ$ of $p$ such that $
  |ξ-ζ|\le 1.$ We prove this conjecture in every degree. The proof combines a covering of the convex hull by diameter disks, inequalities for reflected polynomials, and quantitative estimates for centred products, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted verification in a finite range of degrees.

title: Regularity of Solutions to Non-Local Equations on Homogeneous Groups
abstract: We prove a Harnack inequality and Hölder continuity of solutions to non-linear nonlocal equations on homogeneous groups. In addition, we show basic properties of the involved Sobolev spaces, which are crucial for the analysis of such operators.

title: Zero area of quartic Fibonacci Julia sets
abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the Julia set of the degree-four Fibonacci renormalization 2-periodic point has zero planar Lebesgue measure. As a corollary, the degree four Fibonacci polynomial $z^4+c_{\mathrm{Fib}}$ has zero measure Julia set.

title: Level Set Method; partial regularity in ${\mathbf R}^3$
abstract: In the level set method, all level sets of a function move by mean curvature. The function is then a solution of a degenerate parabolic equation, the level set equation. Since the beginning of the 1990s it has been known that solutions are Lipschitz and, in general, not $C^2$. We show that, along a level set that is initially a smooth closed surface in ${\mathbf R}^3$, the Hessian of the solution is bounded up to its first singular time. In fact, at each non-generic singularity the Hessian tends to zero, at a rate given by its instability. Using these bounds, we show in the sequel that, surprisingly, at the singular time the solution is twice differentiable and has a backward time derivative at every point of the level set, whatever the singularity, and identify both the Hessian and time derivative.

title: Link Spectra of Lorenz-like Templates and the Horseshoe
abstract:
We give a complete classification of the inclusion relations between the link spectrum of the horseshoe template $L(0,1)$ and those of the nonnegative Lorenz-like templates $L(0,a)$. For a template $T$, its link spectrum $\mathscr L(T)$ consists of the link types carried by $T$, allowing parallel strands along its strips. For integers $a\geq0$, the spectra of $L(0,a)$ and $L(0,1)$ are comparable under inclusion if and only if $a\notin\{0,2\}$. More precisely, \[ \mathscr L(L(0,a))=\mathscr L(L(0,1)) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=1, \] while \[ L(0,a)\prec L(0,1) \qquad (a\geq3). \] For $a=0$ and $a=2$, the two spectra are incomparable.
  The main new containment is \[ L(0,2n)\preceq L(0,1)\qquad(n\geq2), \] which goes beyond the classical parity-preserving nesting relations. A key ingredient is a braid-theoretic criterion: every $T$-link \[ T((r_1,s_1),\ldots,(r_k,s_k)) \] with $s_k\geq2r_k$ is a horseshoe link. This gives a large explicit family belonging to both the Lorenz and horseshoe spectra.
  In the reverse direction, we construct a horseshoe link outside the Lorenz spectrum. For each integer $m\geq6$, we obtain infinitely many horseshoe links of braid index $m$ excluded from every other nonnegative $L(0,a)$. These examples give infinitely many links with any prescribed number of components at least three. In the other direction, for each positive number of components, we give infinitely many links carried by both $L(0,0)$ and $L(0,2)$ and excluded from the horseshoe spectrum.

title: An $(\infty,1)$-category of conically smooth stratified bordisms
abstract:
To study derived defect topological quantum field theories, we construct an $(\infty,1)$-category of stratified bordisms and sketch its $(\infty,d)$-dimensional analogue.
  In the first chapters we develop a method for constructing symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories, inspired by Segal spaces but better suited to geometric inputs, which we call interval Segal spaces. Using this framework, we construct the $(\infty,1)$-category of $d$-dimensional smooth manifolds via smooth $\infty$-sheaves thereof, in an attempt to address fibrancy issues present in prior work on this subject. We further equip this category with a symmetric monoidal structure, compute its homotopy 1-category, and extend the construction to manifolds endowed with tangential structures, obtaining the interval Segal space of $d$-dimensional bordisms with tangential structure.
  To model the stratifications supporting topological defects, we work with conically smooth stratified spaces, a suitably smooth framework for conical stratifications.
  We define stratified topological manifolds as stratified $\mathcal{B}$-manifolds for a suitable $(\infty,1)$-category of basics $\mathcal{B}$. Using these, we construct an interval Segal space whose objects are compact closed stratified topological $(d-1)$-manifolds and whose 1-morphisms are stratified $d$-dimensional bordisms, and we endow it with a symmetric monoidal structure. We also use tangential structures on conically smooth stratified spaces to formulate a notion of defect labels, aiming toward bordisms with labeled defects in the style of Carqueville et al.
  Finally, we sketch a higher-dimensional generalization of the interval category to a category of $d$-cubes for $d>1$, conjecturally presenting $(\infty,d)$-categories, and outline how stratified factorization homology may be used to produce derived stratified defect TQFTs.

title: Cotorsion pairs in $η$-extensions with applications to $θ$-extension rings and tensor rings
abstract: Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category with enough projective and injective objects, and let $\mathcal B\ltimes_ηF$ be an $η$-extension of $\mathcal B$ with $η$ associative. Given a cotorsion pair $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ in $\mathcal B$, we show that the cotorsion pair $(Δ(\mathcal X),Δ(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ exists for arbitrary associative $η$, removing the square-zero assumption $F^2=0$ from Hu's construction. When $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ is hereditary, the heredity of $(Δ(\mathcal X),Δ(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ is characterized by the first left derived functor of a canonical defect functor $δ$. We also remark that Hu's construction and hereditary result for the cotorsion pair $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ remain valid without the nilpotence assumption on $η$. Under nilpotence hypotheses, we establish a completeness criterion for $(Δ(\mathcal X),Δ(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ using the Beligiannis radical functor $\mathfrak r$. And we also provide a completeness criterion for $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ if $\mathcal B\ltimes_ηF$ has enough injective objects. We give sufficient conditions for their coincidence. Dual results are obtained for $ζ$-coextensions. Finally, we specialize the theory to $θ$-extension rings and tensor rings, where the abstract conditions admit explicit module-theoretic descriptions.

title: Smoothing of the Coupled KdV System on \mathbb{T}
abstract:
We study the nonlinear smoothing properties of the Coupled KdV system posed on the torus. This system arises as a particular case of the four-parameter family of Boussinesq systems studied by Bona, Chen and Saut, corresponding to the choice $η^{2}=\frac{2}{3}$, $b=d=0$ and $a=c=\frac{1}{6}$. Although the similarities with the periodic KdV equation and the favorable resonance structure of the Majda-Biello system for the coupling parameter $α=-1$ might suggest that smoothing can be established by a relatively straightforward adaptation of existing techniques, the nonlinear interactions in the Coupled KdV system introduce additional difficulties. In particular, certain mixed interactions lead to degeneracies in the associated resonance functions, resulting in a loss of frequency decay that restricts the attainable smoothing gain. By combining normal-form reductions, duality arguments and Bourgain-space estimates, we establish a smoothing gain of any order $
a< \min \{1,\frac{2}{3}(2s+1)\} $
for $s>-\frac{1}{2}$. Our result demonstrates that the interplay between nonlinear interactions and resonance structures plays a decisive role in determining the smoothing properties of coupled dispersive systems.

title: First-order convergence of finite-difference approximations to the minimum action for diffusions with multiplicative noise
abstract: We prove first-order convergence of finite-difference approximations to the Freidlin--Wentzell minimum action for diffusions with multiplicative noise, which answers the question of the sharp rate left open in [Hong, Jin, Sheng, \emph{IMA J. Numer. Anal.} 45 (2025), 1501--1536]. As shown in that work, a bound on the action controls only the $L^2$ norm of the velocity, which leads to a half-order estimate for the difference between the discrete and continuous actions. To improve it, we use the discrete Euler--Lagrange equation to derive mesh-independent $L^\infty$ bounds on the velocity of piecewise affine interpolants of stationary discrete paths with bounded action. For the case of a unique continuous minimizer, we identify the leading coefficient of the error between the discrete and continuous minimum actions on uniform grids, and a scalar example shows that the first-order error bound is sharp. We also prove strong $H^1(0,T;\mathbb R^d)$ subsequential convergence of interpolated discrete minimizers. Numerical experiments for a two-protein genetic toggle switch confirm first-order convergence of the discrete action for transitions in both directions.

title: The governing equation for probability density of transition path time
abstract: Transition path time is the time it takes a system to move from the initial state (State A) to a final state (State B) without recrossing back to State A in between. The transition path time is probabilistic in nature, and considerable research has been devoted to studying its distribution. In this paper, we derive a governing integral equation that expresses the density of the transition path time in terms of the probability density of the first passage time, which is well understood. An efficient numerical method is provided to solve this governing equation. Several numerical examples are presented to validate the governing equation and to compare the densities of the transition path time and the first passage time.

title: Absence of binding for the helium anion
abstract: We study the helium anion in the nonrelativistic Coulomb model with an infinitely massive nucleus and spin-$\frac12$ electrons. We prove the absence of binding, with $E^{\mathrm{F}}(3,2)=E^{\mathrm{F}}(2,2)$ and no three-electron ground state. A decomposition relative to the helium ground state and completion of the square reduce the problem to a one-dimensional variational inequality.

title: The Bilinear Hilbert Transform Along the Primes
Structural latent dimension: deterministic geometry and local Fisher structure
abstract: We study the \emph{structural dimension} of a second-order object: the minimum latent dimension that remains necessary relative to a declared class of competing dependence. Building on minimum-rank factor analysis and low-rank-plus-sparse decomposition, we use distances to lower-dimensional classes to describe inference near structural ambiguity. General distance and tangent-cone facts yield confidence statements and local margins. For rank-zero competitors with bounded residual degree, we derive exact maximum-weight $b$-matching formulas, support-slack tangent cones and sparse-spike angles; a shared residual support across a field can produce separation absent pointwise. We give positive-semidefinite brackets, a dimension-free Gaussian likelihood expansion, an exact quotient by the tangent of a low-rank background, and a detection floor from the margin. Equal-angle configurations with different branch multiplicities motivate static and spectral detection conjectures. Joint low-rank/residual profiling and the sharp composite information boundaries remain open.

title: Homotopy Classification of Pointed Self-Maps of $\mathbb{RP}^3\#\mathbb{RP}^3$
abstract: We classify pointed self-maps of $M=\mathbb{RP}^{3}\#\mathbb{RP}^{3}$ up to pointed homotopy. Using the universal cover $S^2\times\mathbb R$, we reduce the problem to paths in the sphere mapping space with even or odd endpoint conditions. The evaluation fibration, Whitehead products, and a double-coset calculation determine the resulting secondary invariants. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism split into four families, each in bijection with $\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. Every other realizable endomorphism sends both standard generators to reflections. For each such endomorphism, the realizable multipliers on $π_2(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ are precisely the odd integers $d$, and the classes with fixed multiplier are in bijection with $\mathbb Z/|d|\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. We compute an explicit composition law on the double-reflection submonoid and determine the pointed self-homotopy equivalences. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism form a subset $\mathcal{T}$ that is preserved by composition on either side with arbitrary pointed homotopy classes and satisfies $\mathcal{T}^2=\{0\}$, where $0$ is the constant class. For each fixed triple $(m,k,d)$ in the double-reflection case, the $|d|$ classes induce identical homomorphisms on every homotopy group. Thus the secondary invariant detects distinctions invisible to these induced homomorphisms.

title: Multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for Banach space valued holomorphic functions
abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study a generalized notion of multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for holomorphic functions defined on the unit ball of the finite-dimensional Minkowski sequence space with values in complex Banach spaces. We first prove that the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius is positive for every non-null bounded linear operator whose norm is sufficiently small relative to the scaling parameter. We then determine the exact asymptotic behavior of the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces of finite cotype and we obtain analogous bounds for spaces without finite cotype. Finally, for concave Banach lattices and summing operators, we prove lower bounds that involve a logarithmic factor. These results connect classical scalar Bohr phenomena with operator-valued and Banach space valued settings, and highlight how the geometry of the spaces and the mapping properties of the operator influence coefficient estimates and their dependence on dimension. Several examples illustrate the consistency of our results with the classical Bohr radius and the sharp Defant--Frerick asymptotics.

title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for Riesz capacity in all dimensions
abstract: We prove the Brunn--Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n-1<p<n$, extending the known endpoint $p=n-1$. For sets of positive capacity, equality holds if and only if they are convex and positively homothetic. The inequality remains conjectural for $n-2<p<n-1$, when $n\ge2$. Known isodiametric counterexamples rule out a general extension to negative $p$, even for convex planar sets.

title: Independent Sets in $C_4$-Free Planar Graphs: Sharp Claw-Free Bounds and Structural Reductions
abstract: For every claw-free $C_4$-free planar graph, we prove the sharp weighted bound $α_w(G)\ge (10/31)\sum_v w(v)$, equivalently $χ_f(G)\le31/10$. The proof uses a line-graph representation and the matching polytope; the exceptional small roots are excluded analytically by planar duality and degree-four neighborhood analysis in triangulations. We also prove that, in every $2$-connected $C_4$-free graph of minimum degree at least four, an independent selection of claw centers leaves a compatible subgraph of noncenters with fractional chromatic number at most three; planarity is not required. We apply these results to the conjecture $α(G)\ge5|V(G)|/16$. A minimum-order counterexample without degree-three vertices has at least forty-nine vertices. When all degree-three components of a minimum counterexample are triangle trees, we derive exact boundary states and a joint matching formula. We identify the remaining deficiency estimate and the additional component types that must be addressed to extend this approach. The general conjecture remains open.

title: Veech dichotomy for specific covering surface over Veech surface
abstract: It is known that Veech dichotomy, which states that minimal directions are uniquely ergodic, holds for Veech surface and covering surface branched at a single non-periodic connection point of Veech surface. We give a sufficient condition for Veech dichotomy holds for a finite translation cover of a Veech surface, and applies it on branched cover of square-tiled surfaces to construct examples that satisfy Veech dichotomy but aren't Veech surfaces.

title: Splitting and Mixed Deformations of Toric Generalized Kähler Potentials
abstract: We study splitting phenomena for extremal toric generalized Kähler structures on products of compact toric manifolds. We prove that every extremal symplectic potential splits when the skew-symmetric parameter $B$ is block diagonal, without any restriction on $A$. We also construct two types of non-splitting examples on $\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$: an explicit constant-generalized-scalar-curvature structure with a splitting potential but a non-product generalized Kähler structure, and a deformation family of constant-generalized-scalar-curvature structures with genuinely non-splitting potentials.

title: On the false discovery rate of one-sided p-values under Gaussian dependence
abstract: We study the false discovery rate (FDR) of the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure for $K$ hypotheses at nominal level $q$ under Gaussian dependence of one-sided p-values. We ask whether the global null is least favorable after optimizing over correlation matrices. We show that the global null attains the worst-case FDR for $K\le3$ at every level. In dimension eight, an explicit mixed-null construction has FDR $21q/20$ for $0<q<1/2$. It exceeds the global-null maximum for all sufficiently small $q$, by a uniform extension of the known fixed-matrix small-level Simes bound. For $0<q<1/2$, we identify eight as the first inflation dimension in the monotone rank-one class and prove that $21q/20$ is its exact eight-dimensional maximum. In the same level range, the sharp multiplicative bound over all dimensions in this class is twice the omega constant $w = W(1)$, where $W$ is the Lambert $W$ function. This bound is approached as the dimension increases. We also give scale conditions for stability around the independence benchmark $m_0q/K$, where $m_0$ is the number of true nulls, and obtain a dimension-free upper bound of $q+q^2/2+O(q^3)$ at small levels under the global null with nonpositive correlations.

title: Large caps in $\mathbb{F}_3^9$ and $\mathbb{F}_3^{11}$
abstract: We construct sets of $1104$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^9$ and $5744$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^{11}$, each containing no three distinct collinear points. A reflection lift sends the Calderbank--Fishburn $236$-cap to a cap with three parallel layers of sizes $512,80,512$; both outer layers are linearly equivalent to the FunSearch $512$-cap. A coordinate substitution in Hill's $112$-cap uses replacement sets of sizes $80,32,32$ for the three values of one scalar coordinate. Assigning the $80$-point set to a noncentral $45$-point section gives $5744$, gaining $240$ points over the $5504$ construction obtained from a central $40$-point section.

title: Chang's Omitting Types Theorem in Lukasiewicz Logic
abstract: We prove Chang-style omitting types theorems for standard first-order Lukasiewicz logic. Starting from a prescribed model $M$, we obtain an extension that omits higher-complexity types while preserving lower-level types already realized in $M$. If $T$ is a $Π_{n+2}$-theory, every model of $T$ has an exact extension that preserves its realized $Σ_{n+1}$-types and omits every $Σ_{n+2}$-type not generated by a $Σ_{n+1}$-type. An iterated construction also omits infinity-universal types, whose unbounded quantifier complexity cannot eventually be generated by the corresponding lower-complexity fragments of a single type. The main tool is a refinement of Robinson's infinite forcing sensitive to the quantifier complexity of formulas.

title: On the Cauchy problem for $σ$-evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients via upper decay indicators
abstract: In this paper, the first main goal is to investigate the Cauchy problem for the linear $σ$-evolution equation $$u_{tt}+a^2(t)(-Δ)^σu+b(t)u_t+m^2(t)u=0, $$ where propagation speed, damping term and mass are time-dependent functions. Under suitable assumptions on the interaction among these coefficients, we not only derive decay estimates for the solution and its derivatives in terms of the effective parabolic time scale $\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(s,t):=\int_s^t a^2(τ)/b(τ) dτ$, but also conclude the additional decay induced by the mass term and the upper decay indicators of the initial data. Especially, one can recognize that the time-derivative estimate for solutions exhibits a competition between $m^2(t)$ and $a^2(t)\left(1+\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(0,t)\right)^{-1}$. For the corresponding semi-linear problem with the nonlinear term $|u|^p$, we also establish global (in time) existence of small data solutions fulfilling decay estimates, coming from the mass factor $\exp\left(-\int_0^t m^2(τ)/b(τ)dτ\right)$, under the same assumptions on these coefficients.

title: Edgeworth expansion on sums of Wiener chaos
abstract: In this paper, we study Edgeworth expansions for random variables belonging to a fixed finite sum of Wiener chaoses. Building on the work of Mansanarez, Poly and Swan (arXiv:2510.14002) for a single Wiener chaos, we investigate the extension of their approach to functionals $F$ living in a finite sum of Wiener chaoses $\mathcal{W}_{\leq d}$. Within the Malliavin--Stein framework, we bound the total variation distance between the law of $F$ and its Edgeworth approximation of order $2dm$ by $(\sum_{p,q}^d \operatorname{Var}Γ(F_p,F_q))^{m/2}(\operatorname{Var}Γ(F,\operatorname{L}^{-1}F))^{1/2}$, where $F_p$ denotes the projection of $F$ onto the $p$-th Wiener chaos. The presence of several chaotic components introduces additional interactions, since these components are orthogonal but generally dependent. Since our proof relies on the integration-by-parts formalism and the spectral properties of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator, this result extends naturally to the broader framework of Markov chaoses.

title: Quantum periods and threefold flips
abstract:
We study regularized quantum periods under birational contractions involving threefold flips. Let $g:X \dashrightarrow X'$ be a birational map between Fano threefolds with terminal quotient singularities which contracts exactly one prime divisor $E$ and extracts no divisor. We prove that
  $$
  \lim_{r \rightarrow +\infty}\widehat{G}_{X,rE}(t) =\widehat{G}_{X'}(t).
  $$
  The proof uses logarithmically smooth degenerations and positive discrepancies on good resolutions. Compatibility with orbifold invariants is proved using successive quotient-point extractions and the two-component orbifold degeneration formula.
  We also define stationary descendant invariants of projective terminal Fano threefolds by good resolutions and prove compatibility with a given projective $\mathbb{Q}$-smoothing. The period comparison extends to projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal Fano endpoints under the same hypothesis on the birational map. Its proof compares the endpoints on a common resolution.

title: An Explicit Version of Serre's Open Image Theorem for Galois Number Fields
abstract: In 1971, Serre showed that the mod $p$ Galois representation associated to a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field is surjective for all but finitely many primes $p$. That is, there exists a constant $c(E,K)$, for $E$ a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field $K$, such that $ρ_{E,p}:\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)\to \mathrm{Aut}(E[p])$ is surjective for all primes $p>c(E,K)$. We give a bound for this constant using an effective version of the Faltings isogeny theorem for specific number fields. We show that, for $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ with $|D|<50$ and $K$ a formally real number field, given a non-CM elliptic curve $E$ over $K$ we have $c(E,K)\le 2C_1(K)\log N_{K/\mathbb Q}\operatorname{rad}\left( 2\mathcal O_K\mathfrak N_{E}\right )+2 C_2(K)$, where $\mathfrak N_E$ denotes the conductor ideal of $E$, and the constants $C_1(K)$ and $C_2(K)$ can be described explicitly. We also show that for primes greater than this bound, the image cannot be contained in the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup. This works for any Galois number field. Our proof assumes the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH).

title: Fundamental Limits of Statistical Watermarking for LLMs with Fixed and Optimizable Common Randomness
abstract: Watermarking has emerged as an important technique for distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written text. However, most existing work is primarily empirical, relies on ad hoc watermarking designs, and lacks a fundamental understanding of the performance limits. In this paper, we propose a unified theoretical framework for statistical watermarking of large language models (LLMs), casting the problem as an independence test between generated text and common randomness and jointly designing the watermarking embedder and the detector. Our objective is to maximize detection power while controlling the worst-case false positive rate (FPR) and limiting distortion to text quality. A central focus of our framework is the design of the common randomness, which plays a critical role in both watermark embedding and detection. We characterize the fundamental limits of statistical watermarking under both fixed and optimizable common randomness. Our results show that optimizing the common randomness does not improve the fundamental limits: the best achievable performance is the same as that with fixed common randomness. Nevertheless, common randomness design remains highly important because it can substantially simplify detector design. In particular, with optimizable common randomness, a fixed, deterministic, and model-agnostic detector can achieve optimal performance. We further study a practical setting with fixed uniform common randomness and a fixed deterministic detector, and characterize its performance gap relative to the optimizable case, thereby demonstrating the practical value of optimizable common randomness.

title: Lipschitz bounds and gradient continuity for the Trudinger equation
abstract: We establish local spatial Lipschitz and gradient Hölder estimates for general nonnegative weak solutions to Trudinger's equation $\partial_t u^{p-1}=Δ_pu$, $p>1$. The estimates are uniform across the zero set. The proofs combine Bernstein-type estimates for power transformations, smooth approximation, and comparison with exponential barriers near the zero set.

title: Determinateness in a classical theory of nonclassical truth
abstract: Recent theories that take determinateness as primitive are either nonclassical theories of nonclassical truth, like Field's INT, or classical theories of classical truth, like Fujimoto and Halbach's CD and CD^+. This paper develops a third option: a classical theory of nonclassical truth. The theory, KFDcs, extends the Kripke-Feferman theory KFcs with a primitive determinateness predicate. Unlike CD^+, KFDcs keeps the iteration of truth unrestricted and gives up its completeness. With or without a consistency axiom, KFD is proof-theoretically equivalent to the theory \widehat{ID}_2 of twice iterated fixed points, with ordinal {\varphi}({\varphi}({\varepsilon}_0, 0)0), thus stronger than CD^+. It is also shown that replacing full induction with internal induction yields ordinal {\varphi}({\varphi}(ω, 0)0), and restricting internal induction to total formulae yields {\varphi}({\varepsilon_0},0), the ordinal of KF.

title: Weak-type $(p,p)$ inequalities for Riesz transforms
abstract: For $1\le p\le2$, we obtain the sharp weak-type $(p,p)$ inequality for each classical Riesz transform on real-valued functions on $\mathbb R^n$, with the same optimal constant as for the Hilbert transform. The proof combines the Bellman function method of \cite{BHV} with Janakiraman's sharp strip potential \cite{Janakiraman}.

title: A note on distributive lattices with a commutative generalized implication
abstract: We study distributive lattices with an ideal-valued generalized implication satisfying a commutativity identity. This class extends commutative weak Heyting algebras by allowing implication values to be non-principal ideals. We characterize its intersection with several known classes of gi-lattices, study gi-deductive systems and their relationship with gi-filters and gi-congruences, and extend the relational characterization of commutativity to this setting. The resulting correspondence yields a Priestley-style duality by restricting the established duality for gi-lattices.

title: Homomorphisms between Weyl modules for $\mathrm{GL}_3$ in characteristic $2$
abstract: We classify the homomorphism spaces between Weyl modules for the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_3$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$. We prove that these spaces have dimension at most one and give an explicit recursive procedure that determines when they are nonzero and constructs generators in terms of semistandard tableaux. As a consequence, we determine the dimensions of certain homomorphism spaces between Specht modules in characteristic $2$.

title: Local asymptotic normality for Cox-Ingersoll-Ross drift parameters under high-frequency sampling and the strict Feller condition
abstract: For the ergodic Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) diffusion with known diffusion scale and a fixed initial value, we prove local asymptotic normality (LAN) of the exactly sampled experiment for the drift parameters whenever the Feller index exceeds $1$, assuming only a vanishing mesh and a diverging observation horizon. This improves the previously known condition that the index exceed $(11+\sqrt{89})/2$. The proof cuts off the continuous score near $0$, recovers the remainder by exact conditional centering on each sampling interval, and transfers LAN by a conditional-likelihood argument.

title: Generic finiteness of rotating relative equilibria in the planar $N$-vortex problem
abstract: For every $N\ge2$, we prove that Zariski-generic nonzero real circulations, with any prescribed signs, admit at most $N^{2N}$ labeled, collision-free rotating relative equilibria modulo translations, rotations in $SO(2)$, and positive scaling. The excluded parameters lie in an explicit finite union of quadratic hypersurfaces. The proof combines a logarithmic-residue obstruction to positive-dimensional complex solution sets with Bézout degree bounds.

title: A Proof of The Twin-Star Hypothesis in Dimension Five
abstract: It was recently shown that the question of whether the determinant-like map \(\det^{S^2}\) is unique up to multiplication by a scalar is equivalent to a combinatorial conjecture regarding cycle-free \(d\)-partitions of the complete graph \(K_{2d}\), known as the twin-star hypothesis. This hypothesis asserts that every cycle-free \(d\)-partition of \(K_{2d}\) is weakly equivalent to one that contains a component isomorphic to the twin-star graph \(TS_d\). This hypothesis was previously established for \(d\le4\). In the present paper, we prove it for \(d=5\). Consequently, the associated determinant-like map \(\det^{S^2}\) is unique up to a scalar in dimension \(5\).

title: Hilbert-Kunz Multiplicity and Smirnov's conjecture
abstract:
In this paper, we study Smirnov's conjecture: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring of characteristic $p>0$ and dimension $d$. Let $I$ be an $\mathfrak{m}$-primary ideal. If $R$ is weakly $F$-regular, analytically unramified and Cohen-Macaulay, then $\displaystyle L_1(I)=e(I)-e_{\mathrm{HK}}(I)$ if and only if $I$ is stable. Here, $e(I)$ and $e_{\mathrm{HK}}(I)$ denote the Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity and the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity of $R$ with respect to $I$, respectively. Moreover, $\displaystyle L_1(I)=\lim_{q\to\infty}\frac{e_1(I^{[q]})}{q^d},$ where $q=p^e$ and $e_1(I^{[q]})$ denotes the first Hilbert coefficient of $R$ with respect to the $q$th Frobenius power of $I$.
  We prove the conjecture when $R$ is either excellent and strongly $F$-regular, or excellent of dimension $3$.

title: On $z_{2M}(21,4)$: the Hole Extensions of the Chen--Chen Configuration Are Reducible, and the Extremal Configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ Are Not Unique
abstract: The second order extended Zarankiewicz number $z_{2M}(m,n)$ of Qi and Yu allows a secondary half of a $2$-edge to be shared, while the $1$-edge graph stays $C_4$-free and extremal and $1$-edges and main halves stay exclusive. Whether $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ is open. Since deleting a $2$-edge removes exactly one displayed square, $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ if and only if there is no irreducible admissible configuration with exactly $56$ displayed squares, and by the cell count of Qi and Yu and the heredity of irreducibility such a configuration without empty cells is an extremal $55$-square configuration of $z_2(21,4)$ plus one $2$-edge at its hole. For the extremal configuration of Chen and Chen we show, by certificates verified in exact rational arithmetic, that all $56$ such extensions have SOS rank at most $55$: $32$ by product relations and $24$ by contraction certificates of Xu--Yan type. We also show, with computer-assisted certificates and an exhaustive isomorphism search, that the extremal configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ fall into at least six isomorphism classes; Chen and Chen leave the structural classification of extremal augmented graphs open. Finally we prove a six-to-four reduction. For irreducible configurations whose $1$-edge graph is $C_4$-free with $m+\binom n2$ edges it bounds the multiplicity of a shared half by $n(n-1)$ ($12$ at $21\times4$), and it applies directly to an explicit number of the extensions of any extremal configuration of $z_2(21,4)$, eight for that of Chen and Chen, bringing each to at most $54$ squares, in agreement with the certificates. The cell count, the heredity lemma, the rows lemma, the six-to-four identity and a $2\times2$ example are checked in Isabelle/HOL; the remaining arguments are written proofs.

title: From Objective Compromise to Structure-Enabled Intelligence: Reshaping the Scientific Paradigm of AI
abstract: Mainstream artificial intelligence systems, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), are fundamentally constructed upon the Optimization-Driven (OD) paradigm. This paradigm can be characterized as an ill-posed optimization problem within a high-dimensional parameter space. When confronted with real-world scenarios characterized by noise and conflicting constraints, the logic of global error minimization inherently induces a strong smoothing effect. Consequently, this yields statistical compromise solutions that flatten local features, making it arduous to overcome the inherent bottleneck of Out-of-Distribution (OOD) generalization. Existing AI models generate outputs purely based on statistical probabilities. They lack the capacity to autonomously discern truth from falsehood or establish causal logic, thereby lacking genuine cognitive intelligence. To address the ontological limitations of the OD paradigm, this paper proposes a novel paradigm termed \textit{Structure-Enabled Intelligence}. This approach abandons the conventional path of relying solely on computing power scaling and data fitting to achieve emergent intelligence. Instead, it embeds mathematical structures and physical mechanisms as underlying priors into the algorithmic architecture, constraining the model's solving process with structured scientific rules. Through this paradigm shift from ``data-driven objective fitting'' to ``mechanism-structure dominance,'' the proposed approach fundamentally mitigates the issue of statistical compromise, enhances the model's extrapolation and generalization capabilities, and simultaneously reshapes human-AI synergy by upholding human subjectivity in scientific cognition.

title: On the Waldschmidt constant of monomial ideals
abstract: We investigate a conjecture proposed by Cooper et al. in 2017 regarding a lower bound for the Waldschmidt constant of monomial ideals. We first show that this conjecture does not hold in general by explicitly computing the Waldschmidt constant for a family of monomial ideals. Also, we identify a class of monomial ideals for which this conjecture holds by proving a containment between symbolic and ordinary powers. For a monomial ideal, we provide a new lower bound for the Waldschmidt constant, which modifies the conjectured lower bound under a certain condition.

title: Representability of Galois extensions
abstract: We study faithful Galois extensions in a presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathscr{C}$ by a dualizable $\mathbb{E}_1$-group $G$. We prove that these extensions correspond to colimit-preserving symmetric monoidal functors from $\mathrm{An}^{\mathrm{B}G}$ to $\mathscr{C}$. Under suitable assumptions, we use this correspondence to construct a Galois pro-anima that classifies Galois extensions in $\mathscr{C}$. This generalizes the étale fundamental groupoid of commutative rings and Mathew's weak Galois groupoid.

title: Horrocks-Mumford sheaves on toric varieties
abstract: Previous work of the authors introduced the class of Horrocks-Mumford sheaves over normal algebraic k-varieties, the most prominent example being the classical Horrocks-Mumford bundle on projective four-space. For a smooth semiprojective toric variety, we derive an explicit description of these sheaves in terms of finitely generated graded modules over the Cox ring which we use for an algorithmic treatment. In particular, we discuss some explicit examples, their indecomposability and local freeness.

title: Lower bounds for the Kolmogorov widths of global attractors of dissipative systems
abstract: We introduce the notion of a strengthening set in a Hilbert space and prove an exponential lower bound for its Kolmogorov widths. For compact sets containing the origin, the strengthening property is equivalent to the existence of such a bound. As an application, we obtain an exact formula for the widths of the global attractor of a diagonal dissipative system.

title: Singular Birth-Death model
abstract: We introduce and study a one-dimensional singular birth-death model constructed from Itô's Brownian excursion measure. In this model, particles are born at the origin at infinite rate, evolve as Brownian excursions away from the origin, and are killed upon returning to the origin. Although the number of particles alive at any fixed deterministic time is almost surely finite, we prove that the set of exceptional times at which infinitely many particles are alive is almost surely dense and has Hausdorff dimension $1/2$. We further investigate the spatial structure of the particle system at such exceptional times. In particular, we identify the critical near-origin profile of the infinite particle cloud, which is governed by a scale of order $\log\log(1/|x|)^{-1}$ as $x\downarrow0$. Finally, we establish laws of large numbers and central limit theorems for two natural observables of the system: the $α$-power sum of the positions of all alive particles and the top particle position.

title: Distance-$2$ isolation of connected graphs
abstract:
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a set of graphs and $F$ is a copy of a graph in $\mathcal{F}$, then we call $F$ an $\mathcal{F}$-graph. Let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex graph. For a subset $D$ of the vertex set $V(G)$, let $N^2[D]$ denote the second closed neighbourhood of $D$. Let $ι_2(G, \mathcal{F})$ denote the size of a smallest subset $D$ of $V(G)$ such that $N^2[D]$ intersects the $\mathcal{F}$-graphs contained by $G$ (equivalently, $G - N^2[G]$ contains no $\mathcal{F}$-graph). For $k \geq 0$, let $\mathcal{E}_k$ denote the set of connected graphs that have at least $k$ edges (and at least one vertex if $k = 0$). By a well-known result of Meir and Moon, $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_0) \leq n/3$ if $n \geq 3$. We show that $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_1) \leq n/4$ if $n 
eq 2$, $n 
eq 3$ and $G$ is not a $7$-cycle. Hua and Liu recently showed that if $G$ is not a $4$-vertex path or a $4$-cycle or a $9$-cycle, then there exists a subset $D$ of $V(G)$ such that $|D| \leq n/5$ and each component of $G-N^2[D]$ has a universal vertex. We strengthen this result by showing that $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_2) \leq n/5$ if $n 
eq 3$, $n 
eq 4$ and $G$ is not an $8$-cycle or one of five $9$-vertex graphs. It follows that $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_3) \leq n/5$ if $G$ is not a $3$-cycle or a $4$-vertex graph or a $9$-cycle. This also implies the result of Hua and Liu, and that if $\mathcal{C}$ is the set of cycles, then $ι_2(G, \mathcal{C}) \leq n/5$ unless $G$ is a $3$-cycle or a $4$-vertex graph containing a cycle. All these bounds are sharp.

title: An ancient diophantine problem of Brahmagupta
abstract: In the seventh century CE, Brahmagupta gave a parametric solution to the problem of finding two numbers $x$ and $y$ such that $x+y, x-y$ and $xy+1$ are all squares. We describe a method for generating infinitely many rational parametric solutions of the problem and another method for generating parametric solutions of the problem in terms of univariate polynomials with integer coefficients. The complete solution of the problem still remains elusive.

title: Uniqueness and Nondegeneracy of Positive Bounded Solutions for Semilinear Dirichlet Problems in Exterior-Star Domains
abstract: We prove the uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive bounded solutions for the Dirichlet problem $$-Δu=f(u)\,\ \ \text{in}\ \ Ω, \ \ u=0\,\ \ \text{on}\ \ \partialΩ,$$ where $f$ is a positive reaction and $Ω\subsetneq\mathbb{R}^d$ is a uniformly $C^{2,γ}$ domain with a star-shaped complement. Our uniqueness result gives a positive answer to Open Question 1 of [H. Berestycki and C. Graham, ARMA, 2026].

title: The Common-Color Spectrum of Endpoint Set-Coloring Ramsey Numbers
abstract:
The set-coloring Ramsey number $R(n;r,s,t)$ is the least $N$ such that every assignment of an $s$-element subset of $[r]=\{1,\ldots,r\}$ to each edge of $K_N$ contains a $K_n$ whose edge labels have at least $t$ common colors. Motivated by the work of Erdős and Szemerédi on $R(n;r,r-1,1)$, we write $R(n;r,r-1,t)=\exp\bigl(nf_{r,n}(t)\bigr)$ and study $f(t):=f_{r,n}(t)$ as $t$ ranges from $1$ to $r-1$.
  For fixed integers $r\ge2$ and $1\le t<r$, we prove that, as $n\to\infty$, \(
  \frac12\log\frac{r}{r-t}+o(1)
  \le f(t)
  \le \frac{r}{r-t}\log\frac{r}{r-t}
  +C+O_{r,t}\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \) where $C>0$ is an absolute constant. Comparisons between different numbers of colors show that the rates $\liminf_{n\to\infty}f_{r,n}(t)$ and $\limsup_{n\to\infty}f_{r,n}(t)$, defined for fixed $r$ and $t$, each have a limit as $r\to\infty$ and $\frac{t}{r}\toα\in(0,1)$ from above. The resulting two functions of $α$ are finite, positive, nondecreasing, and right-continuous. Writing $Δ_t=f(t+1)-f(t)$, we further prove that, as $r\to\infty$, uniformly for $n\ge r^2$, at least $\frac{(1-o(1))\log r}{\log\log r}$ indices $1\le t<\frac{r}{2}$ satisfy $Δ_t\ge\frac{1-o(1)}{2r}$. For $r,n\ge3$ and $2\le h\le r-1$, the final $h-1$ increments account for at least $1-\frac{1}{\left\lceil h/2\right\rceil}$ of the total increase $f(r-1)-f(1)$. For each fixed $r\ge4$, the last increment has a positive lower limit as $n\to\infty$. Moreover, for $r,n\ge3$, it exceeds the sum of all preceding increments whenever $r$ is even or $n=3$.

title: Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers from rainbow Turán numbers and beyond
abstract: The Hadwiger-Debrunner number $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)$ is defined as the maximum piercing number over all finite families of compact convex sets in $\mathbb R^d$ in which among every $p$ sets, some $q$ have non-empty intersection. We develop three complementary constructions that improve lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers. For any fixed $q>d\ge 2$, a randomly sparsified family of hyperplanes, analyzed using hypergraph containers, yields $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)\ge p^{(d+q-2)/(q-1)+o(1)}$ as $p\rightarrow\infty$. To deduce further bounds, we establish a transfer argument from upper bounds on the sizes of sufficiently general-positioned subsets of high-dimensional integer grids to lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers. Two methodologies are adopted to derive the former: one connects rainbow Turán theory and general-positioned grid sets, and the other uses full spark linear reduction of tuples with bounded-size preimages. As a combinatorial ingredient, we describe the rainbow Turán behavior under suspension operations, which may be of independent interest.

title: DLR variational principle for the one-dimensional log-gas and another proof of existence of Sine-beta
abstract:
We show that every stationary solution of the Dobrushin--Lanford--Ruelle (DLR) equations for the one-dimensional log-gas with a quantitative control on its number variance minimizes the free energy functional. This yields a DLR variational principle for this continuous long-range system.
  Moreover, we show that any limit point of the finite-volume log-gases is stationary and satisfies this condition. This allows us to give a new, physical proof of the existence of a microscopic limit for the Gaussian Beta Ensembles, known as the Sine-beta point process.

title: Many faces of integer semidefinite programming
abstract: We first establish several properties of integer positive semidefinite matrices, extending known results for binary and ternary positive semidefinite matrices. We then show how to reformulate an integer quadratic program (IQP) as an equivalent integer semidefinite program (ISDP). We distinguish three cases, namely IQPs with two, three, or more than three distinct integer values, and provide several ISDPs for each case. Each reformulation yields either a binary ISDP, a ternary ISDP, or a rescaled version of one of these. The results show that ternary SDP formulations for problems with three distinct integer values provide SDP relaxations with fewer constraints and, in the case of equally spaced integers, also smaller matrix variables than binary-based SDP relaxations. For quadratic problems whose variables can take more than three distinct integer values, one can choose among three formulations based on the size of their matrix variables, the number of constraints, and the strength of the resulting SDP relaxations. We also show how to reformulate a mixed-integer QP as a mixed-integer SDP.

title: On the Power-Law Duality in Wigner-Yang Quantum Mechanics
abstract: In this work we first revisit the Hooke-Newton duality and its generalisation to arbitrary power laws in classical and quantum mechanics. We then consider Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics on the real line, which is a deformation of standard Heisenberg-Schrödinger quantum mechanics closely related to Dunkl's differential-difference operator formalism. We consider the corresponding eigenvalue problem for the harmonic potential and a Coulomb-like potential. We observe that the Hooke-Newton duality is also applicable to these deformed quantum systems allowing us to solve the eigenvalue problem of one by mapping it onto the other system. This approach is then generalised to arbitrary power-law potentials in Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics. Whereas in standard quantum mechanics the classical re-scaling of angular momenta has to be applied to Langer-modified quantum angular momenta, Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics requires a rescaling of deformation parameters similar to the Langer-type modification but involving the reflection operator. The energy coupling-constant exchange, however, remains the same in all three cases, classical mechanics, quantum mechanics and Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics.

title: Log Hodge-de Rham degeneration beyond the toroidal case
abstract:
Let $φ\colon X \to S$ be a flat and proper one-parameter degeneration of algebraic varieties with a single degenerate fiber $X_0$. If $φ\colon (X|X_0) \to (S|0)$ is log smooth and saturated, the log Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence is known to degenerate at the page $E_1$. Adding to that some further well-known related properties, we say that the log de Rham complex $Ω^{\bullet,\mathrm{log}}_{X/S}$ is cohomologically flat as a filtered complex, short cffc. Furthermore, if $φ\colon (X|X_0) \to (S|0)$ has only toroidal log singularities, it is known that the reflexive log de Rham complex $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc. A major motivation to study this property is that in the Calabi-Yau case, $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ being cffc implies that a certain logarithmic deformation functor for $φ_0\colon X_0^\partial \to S_0^\dagger$ is unobstructed.
  In this article, we develop a computational criterion to determine, under very mild assumptions on $φ\colon X \to S$, whether the reflexive log de Rham complex $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc. Applying this criterion, we found many explicit examples of degenerations of surfaces where $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc, even though the log singularities are worse than toroidal. We did not find any new examples of degenerations of threefolds such that $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc.

title: Orbital graph structure of alternating full groups and simple torsion amenable groups of exponential growth
abstract:
We develop a framework for constructing simple alternating full groups A(G, X), associated with finite fragmentations of minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions, with controlled orbital-graph codings and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. We also prove that positive entropy of a naturally labeled admissible orbital line forces exponential word growth of the acting group.
  As an application, we construct continuum many pairwise abstractly nonisomorphic, finitely generated, infinite, simple, torsion, amenable groups of exponential word growth. They arise as alternating full groups of fragmented minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions with linearly repetitive generic regular orbital graphs and purely non-Hausdorff singularities.
  Under the same minimality, expansivity, linear repetitivity and singularity assumptions, if every finite clopen coding is determined by a bounded fragmentation window, the alternating full group has intermediate word growth.

title: Second-Order Threshold and Value Asymptotics in Multiple-Stopping Secretary Problems
abstract: We study the classical secretary problem with a fixed number of selection opportunities. We derive explicit corrections to the limiting thresholds and to the optimal success probability. A cancellation identity removes the influence of later threshold rounding from the first correction, while a Poisson representation explains its probabilistic meaning. Every bounded rounding of the limiting thresholds shares the first value correction. We obtain integer rounding laws, eventual threshold identities along continued-fraction convergents, and joint rounding frequencies. Rigorous rational bounds show that the first eleven corrections are positive and the twelfth is negative, producing the first shifted convergent identity.

title: Equilibrium measures for anisotropic exponential interaction energies with applications to transformers
abstract: We study the minimization of anisotropic exponential interaction energies over probability measures on the sphere, motivated by mean-field models of self-attention in transformer architectures. For every symmetric positive definite interaction matrix, we relate the minimizer to a corresponding anisotropic Brownian motion and use the Feynman--Kac formula and elliptic regularity theory to show that it admits a smooth, strictly positive density on the sphere. We further show that it is the only stationary measure with full support for the dynamics considered. We use the stochastic viewpoint to derive an algorithm for sampling from the minimizer. In dimension two, we also propose a numerical scheme for approximating its density based on a Mathieu series expansion.

title: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} in 2004 conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$.

title: Spaces with maximal monotone convex subdifferentials
abstract: We characterize the real Hausdorff locally convex spaces on which every proper lower semicontinuous convex function has a maximal monotone convex subdifferential. Equivalent conditions are given in terms of the portability of closed convex sets and identities involving upper envelopes. Among normed spaces, this property is equivalent to completeness; among Fréchet spaces, it is equivalent to normability. We also prove that the property is preserved under products with finite-dimensional spaces.

title: Fixed-space indices and symmetry breaking in variational problems
abstract:
We establish a quantitative criterion for variational bifurcation with prescribed exact stabilizers under finite group actions. Combining scalar spectral flow on fixed spaces with overgroup nullities, we bound the number of bifurcation parameters when the restricted singular set is finite. The theorem allows strongly indefinite Fredholm Hessians and singular ambient endpoints, without parameter differentiability or regular crossings. Finite Morse index reduces the inputs to indices and nullities; extensions cover varying form domains and regular matrix Sturm--Liouville systems.
  For a Newtonian nine-body family containing a reported counterexample to Moeckel's stability conjecture, we prove analytically that two nonconjugate exact reflection types bifurcate at a common central mass, displacing the central body. Positivity excludes larger stabilizers, while a scalar Schur complement synchronizes the bifurcations, independently of the reported stability assertion.

title: Galerkin methods for unconventional superconductors with long-range interactions on 3D lattices
abstract: We develop an analysis and a B-spline Galerkin method for the matrix-valued Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) gap equation of unconventional superconductors with general long-range interaction kernels on arbitrary Bravais lattices. We define the BCS free energy functional on lattices, show that it is bounded from below, and characterise solutions of the gap equation as its stationary points. For non-repulsive kernels, we prove that fixed-point iteration never increases the free energy and drives the residual to zero. The algebraically decaying tails of the interaction are described by Epstein zeta functions, so the method applies to any power-law exponent $ν>0$, including exponents at or below the lattice dimension such as dipolar interactions in three-dimensional lattices. In the B-spline Galerkin basis, the singular convolutions correspond to block-circulant matrices whose eigenvalues are lattice sums, applied without quadrature at FFT cost.
