A closed-form evaluation of the nonsubfield distribution remains open.

title: Sharp fill-in inequalities and rigidity for spin initial data sets
abstract: We prove sharp fill-in inequalities for compact spin initial data sets satisfying the dominant energy condition. The inequalities relate the spacetime mean curvature of the boundary to its hyperspherical radius and stable one-systole. Equality characterizes spacelike graphs of constant boundary height over round Euclidean balls and, in the systolic case after passing to the universal cover, over products of a round disk with Euclidean space. We also prove rigidity under comparison with strictly convex Euclidean domains, using normalized boundary metrics. The proofs use a modified Dirac operator with a chiral boundary condition.

title: Nonsmooth Convex and Strongly Convex Optimization from Noisy Comparisons
abstract: We study nonsmooth convex and strongly convex optimization problems using only noisy pairwise comparisons: each query specifies two points and returns a single binary response indicating which point has the smaller function value, subject to noise. We distinguish two observation models: Stochastic Order Oracles, which compare two evaluations of the same random loss, and Preference Oracles, whose conditional response mean is a transfer function of the objective difference. For Stochastic Order Oracles, we prove that no comparison-based algorithm can guarantee vanishing expected suboptimality in general, even when sample losses are convex and Lipschitz and the mean objective is strongly convex. Under a normalized probit calibration, we recover convergence and establish matching upper and lower rates for convex and strongly convex objectives. For Preference Oracles with a linear response model, the binary response $O \in \{\pm1\}$ satisfies $\E[O\mid y,z]=λ(f(y)-f(z))$, with $λ>0$. In dimension $d$, we obtain an upper bound of $\widetilde (d^{3/2}/(λ\sqrt N))$ and establish, to our knowledge, the first minimax lower bound of $Ω(d/(λ\sqrt N))$, matching the optimal budget $N$ exponent, for both convex and strongly convex nonsmooth objectives. Beyond exact linearity, we analyze a simple projected comparison method for nonlinear transfer functions and establish convergence rates that depend on how accurately these functions can be approximated by a linear model near zero. Our analysis requires neither oddness nor twice differentiability of the transfer function.

title: The Deepest Pairs of Points Are Not as Deep as Conjectured
abstract: Given any finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, Neumann-Lara and Urrutia \cite{NLUr88} proved in 1988 that there is always a pair such that every circle through the two points encloses a positive fraction of all points. While Edelsbrunner et al.\ \cite{EHSS89} showed that the fraction is at least $\sfrac{1}{2} - \sfrac{1}{\sqrt{12}} = 0.211\ldots$, Urrutia \cite{Urr02} conjectured that the constant $\sfrac{1}{4} = 0.25$ in the upper bound proved by Hayward, Rappaport and Wenger \cite{HRW89} is best possible. We disprove this conjecture by lowering the constant to $\sfrac{3}{14} = 0.214\ldots$. The new bound also disproves a related conjecture by Ramos and Viaña \cite{RaVi09} on finite sets in convex position in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Finally, we generalize the latter extremal question to finite sets in possibly non-convex position, for which we prove the first linear lower bound, with constant $\sfrac{(2-\sqrt{2})}{6} = 0.097\ldots$.

title: Characterisation of first passage locations for two-dimensional lattice random walks
abstract: Consider a diagonal random walk $(X_n,Y_n)$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with transition probabilities depending only on the second coordinate. We characterise the distributions of first passage locations, $X(τ_a)$, where $τ_a$ is the first time $Y_n$ reaches level $a$. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for a given distribution to be realised as a rescaled first passage location from some starting level. The proof extends Bondesson's method for one-dimensional first passage times. It combines a transformation of generating functions based on Pick functions with a construction using barriers. We also study maximal representations of generating functions of first passage locations and show that analogous converse results for standard and honeycomb random walks require additional restrictions.

title: Quantum Gromov--Hausdorff Convergence of Spectral Truncations for Amenable Discrete Quantum Groups with Modified Rapid Decay
abstract: Let $G$ be an amenable discrete quantum group with the modified rapid decay property relative to a proper central length $\ell$. We construct a modularly corrected commutator seminorm on $C_r^*(G)$ and prove its right invariance. Averaging over the coproduct yields a regular bi-invariant Lip-norm. For the spectral projections $P_R=χ_{[0,R]}(D_\ell)$, we equip the finite-dimensional operator systems $A_R=P_RC_r^*(G)P_R$ with the Lip-norms induced by the compressed left and right coactions. We prove quantum Gromov--Hausdorff convergence and obtain an explicit approximation estimate. These spectral compressions are length-filtered Peter--Weyl truncations of the compact dual. The resulting regular bi-invariant Lip-norm also places the family within Leimbach's operator Gromov--Hausdorff convergence theorem. The construction applies to non-unimodular discrete quantum groups, including discrete duals of standard deformations of compact semisimple Lie groups.

title: Schatten isometries of Grassmann spaces
abstract:
We characterize all (not necessarily surjective) Schatten $p$-isometries of the Grassmann space of rank $k$ projections on a complex Hilbert space for every $p\in(0,\infty]$. We prove that every such isometry is induced by a linear or conjugate-linear isometry of the underlying Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, with the additional possibility of composition with orthocomplementation when $\dim \mathcal H = 2k > 2$.
  Our result generalizes Wigner's theorem, which plays a central role in the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics. It also extends previous results on Schatten $p$-isometries of Grassmann spaces, including characterizations of surjective isometries by Gehér and Šemrl for $p=\infty$ and by Qian et al. for $0<p<\infty$ and that of not necessarily surjective isometries by Gehér for $p=2$.

title: Frege's logic in Grundgesetze is nonclassical
abstract: I show that the axioms and rules of inference about the horizontal in the subsystem of Grundgesetze without value-ranges fail to capture its intended interpretation. That is, I build a nonstandard model in which $-a$ is the true iff $a$ is not the false, thereby confirming a conjecture made by Landini that $a \to (-a) = a$ is not provable in this subsystem. This motivates our main result, namely, soundness and completeness proofs for the first-order fragment without value-ranges with respect to a new nonclassical semantics of boolean truncation. Simply put, the widespread assumption that Grundgesetze's first-order logic is classical first-order logic is mistaken.

title: Uniqueness of limit cycle{s} in a class of classical trinomial Liénard systems
abstract:
This paper studies the number of limit cycles of the polynomial Liénard system
  $\dot x=y-F(x)$, $\dot y=-x$, where
  $F(x)=a_1x^{2N}+a_2x^{2m+1}+x^{2n+1}$,
  with integers \(N,m,n\) satisfying $2\le N\le m<n$, $a_1\ne0$ and $a_2\neq 0$.
  It is proved that this system has exactly one limit cycle and that
  every periodic orbit is hyperbolic and attracting
  for $a_2<0$; this system has
  no limit cycles for $a_2>0$. The uniqueness proof compares the widths and relative midpoints of the two scalar
  arcs obtained in potential coordinates.
  This result gives a positive answer to Conjecture 1.4 of
  Cen et al. (Sci. China Math., 2026).

title: Saturation and Semi-Saturation Numbers of Joins with Complete Graphs
abstract: For a nonempty family $\mathcal F$ of graphs, a graph is $\mathcal F$-semi-saturated if adding any missing edge creates a copy of some member of $\mathcal F$ containing the added edge, and is $\mathcal F$-saturated if it is also $\mathcal F$-free. The minimum numbers of edges in such graphs of order $n$ are denoted by $\operatorname{ssat}(n,\mathcal F)$ and $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal F)$, respectively. We study these parameters for families of graphs obtained by taking the join of a fixed complete graph with each member of a given graph family. Assume that every member of $\mathcal F$ has at least $8$ vertices, minimum degree at least two, and no triangle containing two vertices of degree two. We give explicit sufficient conditions under which $\operatorname{sat}(n,K_t\vee\mathcal F) =\binom{t}{2}+t(n-t)+\operatorname{sat}(n-t,\mathcal F),$ and characterize all extremal graphs. For the family $\mathcal C_{\ge r}=\{C_\ell:\ell\ge r\}$ of subdivisions of $C_r$, this identity holds for fixed $t\ge1$ and $r\ge4t^2+8t+29$ and all sufficiently large $n$. For $K_t\vee C_k$ with $k\ge2t^2+3t+4$, we establish the corresponding identity for saturation when $n\ge2(k+t-2)^3$ and for semi-saturation when $n\ge56k^3+t-1$.

title: Word complexity cutoffs for mixing properties of subshifts
abstract:
Investigating word complexity cutoffs for partial and light mixing in subshifts, we construct partially mixing rank-one subshifts whose word complexity functions $p(q)$ satisfy $
\liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q<2+ε$
for any prescribed $ε>0$ and, conversely, we prove that every lightly mixing rank-one subshift satisfies $
\liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q>2, $
establishing $2$ as the optimal limiting threshold in the rank-one setting. More quantitatively, we show that every $α$-partially mixing rank-one subshift satisfies $
\liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q\geq 2+\fracα{(1+α)}. $
Our constructions are a combination of staircase and Chacon-like rank-one stages; we introduce the independently interesting notion of mixing spans and meshes to establish partial mixing while retaining low word complexity.

title: Routing Information and Stationary Limits in Many-Server Load Balancing
abstract: We study how routing information determines stationary congestion in many-server systems with Poisson arrivals and homogeneous exponential servers. We consider policies that prioritize idle servers and select a queue stochastically no longer than a uniformly sampled queue. In nondegenerate slowdown, where spare capacity is fixed, we identify population laws from the fraction of queues with waiting jobs at each population level. We establish these laws for one-job priority, join-idle-queue, and idle-first sampling. One-job priority attains the join-the-shortest-queue population law and mean delays; further queue information can improve limiting delays in convex order without changing their means. In the super-Halfin-Whitt and Halfin-Whitt regimes, every such policy has the same stationary limits. Our estimates bound idleness-weighted occupancy tails in terms of ordinary tails, uniformly over queue-length thresholds and policies. They also yield process convergence and limit interchange for initial laws uniformly dominated by stationarity, with convergent scaled initial states.

title: Asymptotic Order of the Minimum Number of Graph-Saturating Edges
abstract: Given an $H$-free graph $G$, a non-edge $e$ of $G$ is called $H$-saturating if $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$. The function $f_H(n,m)$ denotes the minimum number of $H$-saturating non-edges over all $n$-vertex $H$-free graphs with exactly $m$ edges. In this paper, we give a complete classification of the asymptotic behavior of $f_H(n,\operatorname{ex}(n,R)+1)$ for any fixed graph $H$ satisfying $χ(H)>χ$ and $χ(H-e)>χ$ for every $e\in E(H)$, where $χ\ge 2$ and $R$ is an arbitrary fixed edge-critical graph with $χ(R)=χ+1$. We show that this quantity is of quadratic order, asymptotic to $\frac{2n}χ$, or zero, according to the existence and structure of $χ$-critical two-edge sets of $H$. In particular, we resolve the conjecture proposed by He et al. ({\it J. Combin. Theory Ser. B} 159 (2023), 42-60).

title: On Semi-interval and Para-interval Graphs
abstract: Bau and Johnson introduced semi-interval graphs and asked whether one of the two extremal sets can always be replaced by a single vertex. A negative answer to this question is given by a tree which has no such representation. It is also shown that a finite connected graph with at least two vertices is a semi-interval graph if and only if it is bipartite. Para-interval graphs, for which one extremal set consists of a single vertex, are characterized by necessary and sufficient conditions on their distance matrices. A characterization of para-interval trees is obtained, and a relation between para-interval graphs and shortest-path interval graphs is established by identifying the vertices of an extremal set. Finally, leveled graphs and the corresponding Hasse diagrams of finite partially ordered sets are considered.

title: On Minima of 3D Lennard-Jones Lattice Energy and FCC-Tetragonal-Simple Hexagonal Phase Transitions
abstract: Denote the Epstein zeta function by \begin{equation}\label{eq:Epstein} E(L,s):=\sum_{v\in L\setminus\{0\}}|v|^{-2s}, \;\;\hbox{where}\;\;L\;\;\hbox{is a lattice}; \qquad s>\frac32. \end{equation} We consider the three-dimensional Lennard--Jones lattice energy, which has the form \[ \mathcal E(L)=\frac12E(L,6)-E(L,3). \] We completely classify the minimizers at every covolume $|L|$, and we prove that as the covolume increases, the minimizing phase changes from the FCC to the body-centered tetragonal and then to the simple-hexagonal lattice. Thereby, we give a positive answer to an open problem raised by Blanc--Lewin [EMS Survey Series 2015, Section~2.5,~(27), pp.~268--269] and Bétermin--Petrache [JMP 2017, Question~1.15], and we prove and clarify the conjecture of Bétermin--Šamaj--Travěnec [SAM 2023].

title: Adaptive Precision Cholesky with Error Guarantees
abstract: Modern accelerators increasingly support low-precision formats such as 8-bit floats and integers to speed up machine learning. We show that a Cholesky factorization in which both GEMM and TRSM are implemented using the fixed-point Ozaki 1 scheme satisfies the same backward error bounds as the standard floating-point Cholesky factorization, and that the same holds for a Cholesky factorization computed using a low-precision MicroScaled GEMM. We then use our error analyses to construct an adaptive precision Cholesky factorization that exploits low-precision formats while respecting a prescribed element-wise error bound, as long as the factorization succeeds. We test it in two settings. First, we use it to choose the number of Ozaki 1 slices at each iteration, with SYRK/GEMM and TRSM emulated in INT8 fixed-point arithmetic to attain double-precision accuracy. Second, we use it to build a low-precision Cholesky preconditioner for the conjugate gradient method (PCG), in which SYRK/GEMM take low-precision inputs and accumulate in high precision, with the input format selected adaptively for each panel; if the factorization breaks down, diagonal perturbation still yields a valid preconditioner, at the cost of the error bound guarantees. On an NVIDIA GH200, the adaptive Ozaki 1-based factorization is up to 29% faster than a right-looking Cholesky using a fixed slice count of 7, and up to 69% faster than one using cuBLAS' Automatic Dynamic Precision (ADP), while maintaining the same error guarantees. For PCG, FP8 factorizations with diagonal perturbation form effective preconditioners on the 13 tested SuiteSparse matrices, reducing the number of PCG iterations by up to $12\times$ over CG on the same matrix diagonally scaled by powers of two. For synthetic matrices with arithmetic spectra, and geometric spectra with $κ\le 10^4$, FP8 preconditioners also reduce the number of CG iterations.

title: $\ell^p$-Busemann space and the coarse Novikov conjecture
abstract: We introduce the notion of an \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space, which is a complete Busemann convex geodesic metric space whose tangent cones admit uniformly controlled homogeneous bi-Lipschitz embeddings into \(\ell^p\)-spaces. An \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space is called admissible if it contains dense sequences of closed convex subsets isometric to certain Finsler manifolds. We then prove that the rational coarse Novikov conjecture holds for proper metric spaces with bounded geometry that admit coarse embeddings into admissible \(\ell^p\)-Busemann spaces.

title: Equivariant homomorphisms and Mordell--Weil groups of twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes
abstract: Let $X'\to X$ be a Galois cover of smooth projective varieties over a field $k$ with group $G$, and let $G$ act on an abelian variety $A$ over $k$. We prove an exact sequence relating the Mordell--Weil group of the twist of $A$ by $k(X')/k(X)$ to the group of $G$-equivariant homomorphisms from the Albanese variety of $X'$ to $A$; the remaining obstruction is killed by $|G|$. This corrects structure theorems in two earlier papers of the author and in a corrigendum to the first, where the equivariance condition was omitted. For the twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes considered in those papers, we determine the rank and the torsion subgroup. Over number fields we describe the rank through the Galois action on endomorphisms and prove a specialization result. When $F(x,y)=0$ is the dual of the Fermat cubic, the Mordell curves $y^2=x^3+16F(a,b)$ have rank at least $3$ over $\mathbb Q$ for all $(a,b)\in {\mathbb Q}^2$ outside a thin set.

title: Bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence of finite plane-to-plane germs
abstract: We show that the bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence of finite holomorphic map germs $(\mathbb{C}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^2,0)$ admits continuous moduli, already among finitely determined polynomial germs of corank one and degree five. The moduli come from a new invariant of finite germs: for two tangent branches of the critical set whose images are tangent, the limit of the ratio of the norms of the images of nearby points is preserved by bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence. For germs $(F,H)$ with quasihomogeneous components the invariant is computed from the height functions of $F$ and $H$: it is given by the moduli of the values of the height function of the component of lower weighted degree at the roots of a weighted Wronskian. As a first application we obtain a continuous invariant for the germs $(Y^3+3tYX^4+X^6,\,X^N)$, $N\ge7$, built from the Henry--Parusiński family.

title: Spectral coincidence and generalized Hua inversion in rings and Banach algebras
abstract: For additively coupled elements with invertible sum and selected commuting outer inverses, we study coincidence of the core idempotents and inversion of the Hua element. Intertwining forces coincidence for finite-Drazin data in unital rings and for generalized-Drazin data in complex unital Banach algebras. Under coincidence, the output splits into an invertible core and a complementary parallel sum, called the residue, yielding exact criteria for inverse existence and success of the prescribed candidate. Explicit ring examples show that strict generalized-Drazin input inverses need not force coincidence under intertwining, and that a common core with a Harte-quasinilpotent residue need not give a strict output inverse. For rings finite as modules over a commutative central subring with the same identity, we prove intertwining transfer and automatic bicommutation for commuting outer inverses with Harte-quasinilpotent remainders, without Noetherianity. This gives input-core coincidence under intertwining. If the central subring is Noetherian, every Harte-quasinilpotent element also has separated left and right powers. For common-core data in the finite-central class, the candidate is a strict output inverse exactly when the residual parallel sum is Harte-quasinilpotent. In the Banach setting, uniform input spectral gaps characterize continuity of the core and candidate along convergent input pairs, with intertwining and quasinilpotent input remainders at every term and at the limit. The output gap is equivalent when the residues of the sequence and limit are also quasinilpotent. Exact defect identities give local estimates on augmented inverse data. At an exactly intertwined base with invertible coefficient operators, we determine the feasible first-order defect space and its sharp norm constant, with a norm-specific matrix calibration.

title: Associahedra are 8-colourable
abstract: Determining the chromatic number of associahedra is a long-standing open problem. Tan [arXiv:2611.05323] recently proved that associahedra are 12-colourable, which is the first constant upper bound. This paper adapts Tan's argument to show that associahedra are 8-colourable.

title: Ramsey Numbers of Most Even-Linked Double Stars
abstract: For $n \geq m$, the linked double star $S_c(n, m)$ is the graph formed by taking two disjoint stars $K_{1, n}$ and $K_{1, m}$ and linking their centers with a path on $c$ vertices. In this paper, we investigate the Ramsey numbers of even-linked double stars, that is, where $c = 2p$ for some $p \in \mathbb{N}$. Determining the Ramsey numbers of the $p = 1$ case (classical double stars) is a longstanding open question; the $p = 2$ case was resolved by Burr and Erdős in 1976, and Liu and Chen made progress for general even-linked double stars in 2026. We extend Burr and Erdős' formula for $p = 2$, proving that the Ramsey number of $S_{2p}(n, m)$ is given by \[r(S_{2p}(n, m)) = \max(2n + 2p - 1, n + 2m + 3p - 1),\]when $m \geq p -2 \geq 0$. Our upper bound argument hinges upon the existence (or nonexistence) of an object that we call a polarized pair. We also establish a matching lower bound that applies for all $n, m, p \geq 2$, and as such, we conjecture that this formula applies for all even-linked double stars where $p \geq 2$.

title: The $E_6$-Grassmannian, its minuscule Coxeter matroids, and the lines on a cubic surface
abstract: We study the minuscule Coxeter matroids of type $E_6$, whose ground set is the set of 27 lines on a smooth cubic surface. We characterize them by a tritangent exchange property and classify them into 230 orbits under the Weyl group. Every nonempty matroidal stratum of the $E_6$-Grassmannian is an open subscheme of a torus, and all orbits but one are realizable over every infinite field. Finally, we compute the tropical $E_6$-Grassmannian and its 60 classes of toric degenerations. This is an extended abstract for a forthcoming paper.

title: Positivity and Boundedness of Solutions to the Guyon-Lekeufack Volatility Model with General Kernels
abstract: We study nonnegativity of the volatility in the continuous-time Guyon-Lekeufack model, in which volatility is an affine function of the convolution of past returns with a kernel $K_1$ and the square root of the integral of past squared returns weighted by a kernel $K_2$. We show that, when volatility is nonnegative and $K_1$ admits a resolvent of the first kind, uniform boundedness of integrals of $K_2$ with respect to this resolvent yields a deterministic upper bound for the asset price, which is then a bounded martingale on every finite time interval. This result is the counterpart of the strict local martingality criterion for negative volatility in Guyon, Jeannin and Jourdain (2026, Corollary 2.6(ii)). We also derive such bounds for popular stochastic volatility models when the Brownian motions driving the asset price and volatility have correlation $-1$. We give sufficient conditions for nonnegative volatility with a completely monotone return convolution kernel $K_1$, and necessary conditions when $K_1$ and $K_2$ are respectively $M$- and $N$-exponential kernels. For $M=1$, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition.

title: A New Record for the Katz-Tao Sum-Difference Exponent
abstract: We prove the record bound $C_{3b}\le 209357544569848128/114631769327023765=1.8263483657186\ldots$ for the Katz-Tao sum-difference exponent, valid in every abelian group without $2$-torsion. Using only Shannon inequalities, conditional copies and Katz-Tao's original directions, whose classical single-grid argument gives $11/6$, we break $11/6$, obtaining $2762/1509$ and $152/83$. For every abelian group we prove the universal bound $C_{\mathrm{all}}=10304335425987192362/5641833174538280329=1.8264161855212\ldots$, which is below the previous record for the real Katz-Tao constant. In the AlphaEvolve study (arXiv:2511.02864v3), the search for extremal distributions improved this constant's lower bound in the eighth decimal place and left its upper bound at $11/6$. Our upper bounds are proofs discovered by CASPAC, the computational mathematics engine of the CASP research system, and certified by independent exact checkers. The proofs use stacked entropy certificates; we supply the complete rational identities, proofs of every auxiliary inequality, and exact verification over the stated group classes.

title: Far-field prediction of algebraic curves via generalized asymptotes
abstract: The asymptotic behavior of algebraic curves is classically described by means of linear asymptotes. However, many infinite branches exhibit a non-linear behavior that cannot be represented accurately by straight lines. In this paper we propose a computational framework for far-field prediction of algebraic curves based on generalized asymptotes. Starting from the asymptotic expansion of a real branch at infinity, we retain its non-decaying terms in order to construct an algebraic surrogate, which is then used as an adaptive far-field model outside a sufficiently large compact region. We introduce explicit discrepancy indicators and a switching radius that determine when the exact branch may be replaced by its generalized asymptotic predictor. The framework recovers the classical linear asymptote whenever the latter exists, while remaining effective for branches with polynomial or Puiseux-type dominant behavior. In the implicit setting, we prove algebraicity and compatibility properties of the predictor and derive asymptotic error estimates from the first neglected term of the expansion. A residual certificate distinguishes guaranteed finite-tail replacement from asymptotic radius estimates. Tangential tails, slow decay, and a smooth transition rule clarify the limitations of truncation. Reproducible finite-window tests compare the predictors with fitted polynomial baselines; these tests are not a benchmark of a complete plotting system.

title: Exact multiplicity for a Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem with a step weight
abstract: The DEG1 challenge asks whether positive solutions of a super-exponential Minkowski-curvature equation are unique for step weights with a single sign change and negative mean. In this paper, we give a Neumann counterexample by studying $\left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' + λa_{μ,h}(t)(e^{u^2}-1)=0$ with $u'(0)=u'(2h)=0$, where $a_{μ,h}=1$ on $(0,h)$ and $a_{μ,h}=-μ$ on $(h,2h)$, with $μ>1$. Using the shooting method, we prove that the positive solution curve has exactly two nondegenerate folds for $(λ,h)$ in a nonempty open region. As $μ$ increases through the corresponding critical values, the number of positive solutions is successively $1$, $2$, $3$, $2$, and $1$.

title: Antisymmetry Breaking for Critical Poincaré-Sobolev Extremals in the Three Dimensional Ball
abstract: We study extremal functions for Poincaré-Sobolev inequalities in the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$. At the critical exponent $q=6$, we prove that no minimizer is antisymmetric with respect to any hyperplane through the origin. We obtain a positive gap between the general and antisymmetric optimal constants. Continuity of these constants yields antisymmetry breaking for exponents sufficiently close to $6$. We introduce two critical indices to describe the onset of antisymmetry breaking and prove that global minimizers are antisymmetric at both indices.

title: Instability of non-minimal critical points of Newton's equation with real analytic potentials
abstract:
We prove that any non-minimal critical point of a real analytic potential on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space possesses a nonconstant zero-energy Newton trajectory that converges to the equilibrium as \(t\to+\infty\). By time reversibility, this yields forward Lyapunov instability. We do not assume the critical point is isolated.
  The proof constructs angular minima via quadratic regularization, matching the regularization coefficient to the leading inertial term. A free forcing coefficient allows continuation past bounded accumulations of correction orders. For polynomial potentials, this produces a complete Hahn-series solution, and differential algebraicity gives a common Puiseux denominator. A fixed-denominator continuation estimate together with a finite Taylor transfer extends the construction to analytic potentials. The realization theorem for the resulting invariant formal phase curve then yields a genuine trajectory. We also exhibit an isolated polynomial singularity for which an exact Euler-field identity admits no relatively differentiable solution on the negative set of the potential.

title: Uniquely balanced polyhedral complexes are highly connected
abstract: We establish higher connectivity of polyhedral complexes admitting a unique positive balanced top cycle. Our main result shows that, after quotienting by common lineality, every skeleton satisfies the corresponding higher connectivity property. The proof bounds the number of connected components surviving facet deletions by the dimension of the top-cycle space using homological and linear-algebraic arguments. As applications, we prove higher connectivity for all skeleta of arbitrary pointed polyhedral structures on tropical linear spaces of valuated matroids and Bergman fans including nonrealizable cases. These results answer questions raised by Maclagan and Yu.

title: Enhancing Exploration in Ensemble Kalman Inversion via Covariance Inflation and Projected Dropout
abstract: Ensemble Kalman inversion (EKI) is a derivative-free and parallelizable method for parameter estimation in Bayesian inverse problems involving expensive forward models. It adapts Kalman filtering by repeatedly assimilating the observation data through an artificial dynamical system with identity state evolution and the parameter-to-observation map as its observation operator. However, its performance can be limited by ensemble collapse and confinement to the affine span of the initial ensemble. We propose an exploration-enhanced EKI framework that combines multiplicative covariance inflation with a projected-dropout correction of the ensemble mean. Inflation helps maintain ensemble spread, while projected dropout enables the mean to explore directions beyond the initial affine span. For linear inverse problems, we provide a discrete-time, finite-ensemble analysis of the resulting method and prove the least-squares objective converges exponentially to its minimum in expectation. Within the initial ensemble subspace, the contraction factor is independent of the conditioning of the inverse problem, and the limiting ensemble covariance provides a low-rank representation of the posterior covariance. Experiments on ill-conditioned linear systems, 100-dimensional nonlinear benchmarks, and a PDE-constrained barotropic flow inverse problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Fourier Ratio Bounds and Sensitivity to Sensor Placement
abstract: We study how the regularity of a continuous function controls the Fourier ratio of its sampled values, and how errors in sensor placement affect recovery from incomplete measurements. For a periodic function on the square sampled on an $N$ by $N$ grid, we show that Hölder regularity $C^{0,γ}$ with $0<γ<1$ leads to a bound of order $N^{1-γ}$, that Lipschitz regularity leads to the critical bound $\sqrt{1+\log N}$, and that fractional Sobolev regularity $W^{s,p}$ with $0<s<1$ and $sp>2$ leads to a bound of order $N^{1-s}$, where both polynomial exponents are sharp. A common translation of the grid removes the hypothesis on the sampled mass needed on a fixed grid and yields an estimate in terms of the $L^2$ norm of the gradient, and with two derivatives the bound is independent of the grid size. We extend the energy argument behind these results to compact Riemannian manifolds and prove that the critical square-root logarithm is necessary on every compact surface. Finally, we treat separate sensor displacements as measurement error and combine the analytic bounds with random sampling to obtain stable recovery of the sampled vector on the square and of bandlimited functions on compact manifolds, where the number of samples depends on the suprema of the chosen eigenfunctions.

title: Behavior of the Caputo time fractional equations as the order $α\rightarrow 0^+$: the resolvent limit and its stochastic interpretation
abstract: We study the behavior, as the fractional order $α\rightarrow0^+$, of the Caputo time derivative and of the solutions of $D_t^αu=Au$ in a Banach space. The solutions converge for every $t>0$ to the time-independent resolvent value $(1-A)^{-1}φ$. A single bounded fractional resolvent family already forces the sectoriality of $A$ and yields operator-norm convergence with rate $O(α)$ and a full expansion in powers of $α$. The engine is an expansion of the Mittag-Leffler function in its order, $E_α(z)=(1-z)^{-1}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}c_kα^k\mathrm{Li}_{-k}(z)+O(α^{K+1})$ on sectors away from $[1,\infty)$, the corresponding qualitative limit going back to Mittag-Leffler's summability of the geometric series. We also develop stochastic interpretations using inverse $α$-stable subordinators, and establish connections with probabilistic potential theory, the Feynman--Kac formula, and degenerate elliptic equations.

title: Explicit geometric integrators for Langevin equations with superquadratic potentials
abstract: We propose a new class of explicit methods for Langevin equations with a superquadratic potential that simultaneously preserve the conformal symplecticity and ergodicity as well as achieving high-order convergence. The construction is based on a mollified potential approach, in which the original potential is truncated to quadratic growth at infinity and globally mollified to control the superquadratic behavior while maintaining the underlying properties of the original dynamics. By appropriately choosing the cut-off radius, the far-field quadratic coefficient, and the step size, we obtain the coercivity of the mollified potential and derive its derivative estimates. These estimates allow us to prove uniform-in-time weak convergence for the proposed (including higher-order) explicit conformal symplectic numerical methods. Since the mollified potential is identical to the original one in a ball whose radius grows as the step size decreases, the computational cost of the new methods is essentially the same as that of the usual schemes (e.g., BAOAB) applied to the original potential. Numerical experiments are provided to illustrate the theoretical results.

title: Exact Redundancy under Average and Almost-Sure Distortion Constraints
abstract: We characterize the exact redundancy of lossy source coding under average and almost-sure distortion constraints. For general source and output alphabets, we establish the asymptotic redundancy coefficients under suitable regularity conditions. Under the average distortion constraint, the coefficient is half of the minimum probability that an output reveals information about the source, among all rate-distortion optimal channels. Under the almost-sure distortion constraint, the coefficient is either $1/2$ or $1$, depending on whether the $D$-tilted information is constant or not. Both converse results follow from a common change-of-measure inequality. Finally, we verify the required conditions under both distortion requirements always hold for finite alphabets.

title: Finite sums of weighted composition operators on the Fock space
abstract: We study finite sums of weighted composition operators on the classical Fock space. We show that no cancellation phenomenon occurs when the composition symbols are pairwise distinct: such a sum is bounded, compact, or belongs to the Schatten class S_p, 0<p<\infty, if and only if each summand has the corresponding property. We also obtain two-sided essential norm estimates and quantitative Schatten norm comparisons for fixed distinct nonconstant symbols. As an application, we obtain corresponding boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class results for finite sums of generalized Volterra-type integral operators.

title: A new formula for Moore-Penrose inverses of rank-deficient Toeplitz matrices
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new formula for the Moore-Penrose inverses of the rank-deficient Toeplitz matrices, based on the quasi-direct decompositions of Toeplitz matrices. Numerical examples are presented to verify the validity and the efficiency of our method.

title: Strong Standard Completeness of a Hypersequent Calculus for Cyclic Involutive Residuated Lattices
abstract: We present a hypersequent calculus $H_R$ for cyclic involutive residuated lattices and prove strong standard completeness for arbitrary theories in a fixed countable propositional language. Standard models are chains on $[0,1]$; neither commutativity nor equality of the monoid unit and the dualizing constant is assumed. The chain semantics is the class $K_R$ defined by unit cyclicity and all ordered finite-history conditions. Every countable member of $K_R$ embeds into a standard chain preserving the entire signature. The construction combines central-support reconstruction, gap insertion and relative contraction. A relative comparison construction supplies the required chain countermodels. We also prove admissibility of the unrestricted density rule for theoremhood and effective elimination from finite proofs without additional assumption leaves. Elimination uses terminating enumeration of density-free proofs; ordinary Cut is retained, and no complexity bound is claimed. Further constructions give bounded standard embeddings for nontrivial countable chains of involutive uninorm logic and pseudo-uninorm logic with weak commutativity. Using ordinary chain completeness for arbitrary theories, these yield strong standard completeness for both logics. A companion Lean~4 development formalizes the main results, with its scope and external inputs stated explicitly.

title: Variance Stable Gaussian Smoothing Estimator for Arbitrary High-order Derivatives
abstract: Computing high-order partial derivatives in high dimensions by automatic differentiation can be costly in both computation and memory. Stein's identity offers an alternative through Gaussian smoothing, but the variance of the resulting estimators can diverge as the step size tends to zero, even with antithetic sampling. We propose a variance stabilization technique that extends antithetic sampling from a reflection pair to $n$ equally spaced points on a circle in the complex plane. Under local analyticity, we prove that, when $n$ is at least the derivative order, the bias is of order $O(σ^n)$ and the variance remains bounded as the smoothing step size $σ$ tends to zero. Numerical experiments support these predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the estimator in physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for polyharmonic and Cahn--Hilliard equations. The technique mitigates the bias-variance trade-off in smoothing-based derivative estimation and is useful for PINNs solving high-order partial differential equations.

title: The maximum length of a Hamiltonian path in the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$
abstract: Label the $mn$ vertices of the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$ bijectively by $1, \dots, mn$ and read the labels in increasing order; this produces a Hamiltonian path whose length in the Manhattan metric is denoted $M(P_m \times P_n)$. McNeil conjectured, on the basis of computer evidence, that $M(P_n \times P_n) = n^3 - 3$ for even $n$ and $n^3 - n - 1$ for odd $n$. Fried recently determined $M(P_m \times P_n)$ up to an additive error of one. We determine it exactly, which settles McNeil's conjecture. The proof rests on the cut-counting bound for multisets. Fried states that bound for multiplicities at least two; we give a form valid for every multiplicity, with a correction term that is invisible in the planar case but not in higher dimensions.

title: Borel $(2n+1)$-coloring for bounded degree function graphs
abstract: Let $G=(X,E)$ be a Borel graph generated by $n$-many bounded-to-one Borel functions. We show that $G$ admits a Borel proper $(2n+1)$-coloring, which answers a problem of Kechris, Solecki and Todorčević.

title: Distance-Certified Polyak-type Stepsizes for Subgradient Methods under Hölder Growth
abstract: In this paper, we consider nonsmooth convex optimization under a H{ö}lder growth condition, with quadratic growth and weak sharp minima as two important special cases. Existing subgradient methods often employ predetermined decaying stepsize schedules, whereas the classical Polyak stepsize selects its stepsize adaptively but requires knowledge of the optimal value. We introduce a new distance-certified subgradient method (\DCSG) that follows a one-step optimization principle analogous to that underlying the Polyak stepsize, without requiring the optimal value. Specifically, \DCSG{} maintains a valid upper certificate for the current squared distance to the solution set. The method selects each stepsize by minimizing the worst-case upper bound on the next squared distance over all distances consistent with this certificate. We show that the resulting minimax problem admits a closed-form solution, yielding an explicit adaptive stepsize update. Under uniformly bounded subgradients, \DCSG{} improves upon the convergence rate of the classical subgradient method and matches the state-of-the-art rates for Lipschitz convex optimization under H{ö}lder growth. In particular, it achieves linear convergence under sharp growth. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of \DCSG.

title: Gaussian mass inequalities for lattices
abstract: The Gaussian mass of a lattice is the evaluation of its theta series at a real nome and is relevant to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel. The ratio of the Gaussian mass of stable lattices to the Gaussian mass of the integer lattice was conjectured to be $\le 1$ (Regev et al., 2024). Kominers proved this bound recently for lattices obtained by Construction~A from binary self-dual codes. Building on Kominers' bound, we establish corresponding inequalities on average for Construction~$A_4$ lattices obtained from free self-dual quaternary codes and for Construction~$A_6$ lattices obtained from self-dual senary codes. We also prove the strict Gaussian-mass inequality for extremal unimodular lattices of both Type~II and Type~I. The Type~I result uses the Rains--Sloane definition of extremality. Its proof combines a universal theta truncation with an exact inversion of the shadow coefficients, and a Gaussian inequality for translated lattices. In addition, we obtain an averaging bound over the genus of Type~II lattices, and extend the binary Construction~A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus, with further quaternary results under conditions on the residue code.

title: On the continuity of the geometric side of the twisted trace formula
abstract: We establish the continuous extension of the geometric side of the twisted trace formula to a natural space of test functions, which are not necessarily compactly supported, for reductive algebraic groups. The continuity of the geometric side of the (untwisted) Arthur trace formula was established by Finis--Lapid. Subsequently, Parab generalized their result to the twisted trace formula under a certain restriction on the truncation parameter and an additional assumption. In this paper, we remove his restriction and assumption, and prove the continuous extension for the twisted trace formula. We also give a revised form of Parab's decay estimate for the geometric side.

title: Thouless's bandwidth conjecture: a proof by elliptic periods
abstract: We prove Thouless's bandwidth conjecture for the critical rational Harper operator: the denominator times the total bandwidth tends to $32G/π$, uniformly in the reduced numerator, where $G$ is Catalan's constant. We identify a universal limit of the normalized even coarea density. Positive real part and evenness give an integrable endpoint bound, so the local law determines the bandwidth. An exact finite-matrix formula reduces the local law to one normalized period for each fixed odd numerator. Explicit boundary polynomials, point blowups, and intersections determine a compact genus-one family. Nodal-annulus calculations fix its period equation and hence the universal density. An exact rational Fourier identity and uniform closed-path bounds extend the result to all reduced numerators and both denominator parities. The singular matrix limit, including its subtraction and normalization, is proved separately in detail.

title: Lau's Fixed Point Problem for Elementary Amenable Groups and Finite Left Amenable Semigroups
abstract: Lau's fixed point conjecture is proved for elementary amenable groups. More generally, a weak$^*$-continuous nonexpansive representation of such a group on a nonempty weak$^*$-closed nonexpansive retract of a weak$^*$-compact convex subset $C$ of a dual Banach space has a nonempty common fixed point set that is a nonexpansive retract of $C$. For finite left amenable semigroups, continuity and weak$^*$-closedness of the retract are unnecessary. The argument also leads to a new class of amenable groups with the same retraction property, which contains all elementary amenable groups and may be strictly larger. This class may provide a useful framework for further research on Lau's conjecture. Bruck's theorem is also extended from abelian to elementary amenable group actions on nonexpansive retracts of weakly compact convex sets with the fixed point and conditional fixed point properties, without weak continuity, thus partially answering a longstanding question of Bruck. Several consequences of the theorem are recorded.

title: Invariance of Arens module actions on the norm dual of a Riesz-normed f-algebra
abstract: Let $A$ be an f-algebra and let $V$ be an order ideal of its order dual $A^{\sim}$ that separates the points of $A$. In a comment accompanying a theorem of Huijsmans and de Pagter (J. Funct. Anal. 59 (1984), 41--64), it is stated that the proof of that theorem can easily be adapted to show that the order continuous dual $V_n^{\sim}$ of $V$ is an f-algebra under the Arens multiplication. We show that this statement is false. The Arens multiplication on $V_n^{\sim}$ requires two invariance conditions on $V$, with respect to the module actions of $A$ and of $V_n^{\sim}$, which do not follow from the stated hypotheses and can fail already in the most natural case, where $A$ carries a Riesz norm and $V=A^$ is the norm dual of $A$. We prove that the first condition holds if and only if $A$ is bounded, and that the second holds whenever the Riesz norm is submultiplicative (which forces $A$ to be bounded); in that case $(A^)_n^{\sim}$ is indeed an f-algebra. We then construct a bounded f-algebra of finitely supported real sequences, equipped with a non-submultiplicative Riesz norm, for which the second condition fails, so that the Arens multiplication on $(A^*)_n^{\sim}$ is not even defined. The comment has also been used in the literature to derive a further result, which is false as well. This clarifies the exact scope of the comment.

title: Spectral action in Betti metaplectic Langlands
abstract:
We construct the spectral action in the context of Betti metaplectic Langlands theory. More precisely, we prove that the category of twisted sheaves on $\text{Bun}_G$ with nilpotent singular support admits a canonical action by the symmetric monoidal category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted $H$-local systems, where $H$ is the metaplectic dual group. This confirms the Betti version of the conjecture of Gaitsgory--Lysenko, originally formulated in the de Rham setting under the name ``metaplectic vanishing conjecture".
  Given a symmetric monoidal category with suitable symmetry, we develop a categorical framework by introducing a notion of twisted factorization homology and studying its categorical action. We show that the category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted local systems can be realized as a twisted factorization homology. Using metaplectic factorizable Satake we further prove that the metaplectic Hecke action naturally fits into our categorical framework. Combining these results, we obtain the desired spectral action.

title: Isolated Singularities Not Resolved by Iterated Nash Blowups
abstract: Castillo, Duarte, Leyton-Álvarez, and Liendo asked whether iterating ordinary Nash blowups in characteristic zero or normalized Nash blowups in arbitrary characteristic can fail to resolve isolated singularities arXiv:2511.17862. We answer this question affirmatively with two constructions of isolated singularities, one nonnormal and one normal, both giving counterexamples to normalized Nash iteration in every characteristic.

title: Counting integral points of fixed degree and given height over function fields
abstract: Let $k$ be a finite extension of the rational function field in one variable over a finite field, and let $\mathcal{O}_k$ be its ring of integers. Let $\overline{k}$ be an algebraic closure of $k$. For integers $e \geq 2$ and $n \geq 1$, we study the number of points in the affine space $\overline{k}^n$ whose coordinates are integral over $\mathcal{O}_k$, have absolute logarithmic Weil height equal to $m \geq 0$, and generate an extension of degree $e$ over $k$. More precisely, we derive an asymptotic formula for this quantity as $m \rightarrow \infty$ whenever $n > e$, except in the cases $(n,e)\in \{(3,2),(4,3),(5,4)\}$. When $k$ is the rational function field, however, we use Weierstrass semigroups to obtain asymptotic formulas for the cases $(n,e)\in \{(1,2),(2,2),(3,2)\}$, thereby completing the picture in the setting $e=2$. As an application, we also derive asymptotic estimates for the number of certain decomposable forms with coefficients in $\mathcal{O}_k$.

title: A Negative Answer to a Variant of the Lins-de Melo-Pugh Conjecture
abstract: We study the polynomial Liénard system $$\dot x=y-(a_1x^{2m+1}+a_2x^{2n+1}+x^{2N}),\qquad \dot y=-x,$$ where $0\leq m< n<N$ are integers and $a_1a_2<0$. The supremum of the numbers of limit cycles in this family is at least two for every integer $N\geq3$ and at least three for $N=5$. These results disprove Conjectures 1.5 and 1.6 of Cen et al. [Sci. China Math. 69 (2026)].

title: First-order smoothed exact-penalty methods for equality-constrained regularized nonconvex optimization
abstract: We consider regularized nonconvex optimization over a closed convex set $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, which involves a convex nonsmooth regularizer $r$ in the objective and $n$ smooth equality constraints. To find a near-KKT point of the problem, we propose a prox-linear first-order method, named as SEPi-Prox, based on a smoothed exact-penalty formulation. At each outer iteration of SEPi-Prox, a strongly convex prox-linear subproblem is formed and solved inexactly to a sufficient accuracy. Under a local non-singularity condition that is weaker than some other commonly used regularity conditions or constraint qualifications, SEPi-Prox finds an $ε$-KKT point within $O(ε^{-2})$ first-order oracle calls, matching the lower bound for unconstrained smooth nonconvex optimization. We employ Nesterov's accelerated proximal-gradient method (APG) and a dual cutting-plane method (DCP) for the prox-linear subproblems. Let $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{FO}}$ and $\mathcal{C}_r$ denote the numbers of arithmetic operations of evaluating one first-order oracle and one proximal mapping of $r$ over $\mathcal{X}$, respectively. Then SEPi-Prox requires $\widetilde{O}(\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{FO}}ε^{-2} + (dn + \mathcal{C}_r)ε^{-5/2})$ and $\widetilde{O}((\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{FO}} + dn^2 + n\mathcal{C}_r + n^{3.373})ε^{-2})$ total arithmetic operations to produce an $ε$-KKT point, respectively by using APG and DCP as the subsolver. The latter result is preferable when $n$ is small and nearly matches the optimal dependence on $ε$. Numerical experiments on instances of the multi-class Neyman-Pearson classification demonstrate the efficiency of SEPi-Prox with both subsolvers.

title: Character variety of the punctured sphere and the determinantal variety
abstract: We show that the SL(2;C) character variety of the n-punctured sphere is described via the determinantal variety defined by an n x n symmetric matrix of rank at most 4 whose entries are the traces of simple closed curves on the surface. This result generalizes the Fricke-Klein-Vogt relations to arbitrary n, and we determine the structure of the kernel of the associated matrix.

title: Geomagnetic Q-Response Inversion as a Calderón-Type Inverse Boundary Value Problem
abstract: Whether electrical conductivity can be uniquely determined from magnetic measurements alone is a fundamental question in geomagnetic induction sounding. For a spherical conductor in the magnetoquasistatic model, we establish an equivalence between the complete Q-response and a restricted magnetic boundary operator, connecting geomagnetic induction to Calderon-type inverse boundary value theory. For axisymmetric conductivities, we derive exact representations of the zero-frequency zonal response derivatives as conductivity-weighted spatial moments. These formulas give an explicit interpretation of individual response derivatives, and completeness of the moment family yields conductivity uniqueness. For layered axisymmetric models with known shell interfaces and piecewise-constant radial dependence, we further establish uniqueness at a single nonzero frequency. Finite-dimensional subclasses also admit uniqueness and stability estimates from finitely many response coefficients at sufficiently low nonzero frequencies. These results identify complementary mechanisms for conductivity recovery from magnetic-only observations, while uniqueness for general three-dimensional scalar conductivities from ideal magnetic-only Q-response data remains unresolved.

title: Calabi flow in the controlled Kähler cone
abstract: We prove that the geometric limit of a global Calabi flow in a real class of the controlled Kähler cone is independent of the initial metric. Under cohomological K-polystability, the limit is a smooth cscK metric in the original class and complex structure. We also establish varying-class closedness and an equivariant continuity method. We apply this method to construct a smoothly varying family of cscK metrics throughout an explicit interval of symmetric real Kähler classes on the blow-up of the projective plane at four points in general position.

title: Weighted bisections of triangle-free subcubic graphs
abstract: We prove a conjecture of Gerke, Gutin, Yeo, and Zhou: for every finite triangle-free subcubic graph other than the claw and every nonnegative edge weighting, there is a bisection whose weight is at least $11/15$ of the total edge weight. This bound is best possible, as shown by the Petersen graph. The proof uses matching-based local distributions, weighted induction, and convex separation to establish the edgewise cut guarantees while maintaining global balance.

title: Scaling Fourier Inequalities for Locally Compact Quantum Groups
abstract: In this paper, we study Fourier and convolution inequalities on locally compact quantum groups in the presence of the scaling group. For $1\le p\le 2$, we investigate a family of scaling Fourier transforms and the associated norms $H_{p,θ}(\mathbb G)$, and we show that $H_{p,θ}(\mathbb G)<1$ for the real quantum $az+b$ group and $0<θ<1$, $1<p<2$. We also investigate scaling convolution for locally compact quantum groups and, by extending the ordinary convolution, obtain the corresponding scaling Young inequality in four different regions. In Young Region~II, under $1<p,s<2$ and $2\leq r<\infty$, we construct sequences proving norm one at every effective vertex and prove strict inequality at every other effective point.

title: Counterexamples to Ecker's Conjecture
abstract: Analogous to Perelman's W-entropy defined for Ricci flow, K. Ecker defined a functional W for the mean curvature flow in R^{n+1} and the region it encloses, and made the conjecture that this functional is monotonically increasing in time. In this paper, we give a negative answer to Ecker's conjecture.

title: Optimal first order global regularity for fractional harmonic maps into spheres
abstract: This paper is a continuation of our previous work on global regularity theory for the sphere-valued fractional harmonic maps which was initialized by several authors such as Millot-Pegon-Schikorra and Millot-Sire. By adapting the powerful quantitative stratification approach developed by Naber-Valtorta on harmonic mappings, we establish a corresponding stratification theory for fractional harmonic maps, from which an optimal first order global regularity theory and the rectifiable structure of singular sets follow.

title: An improved lower bound for piercing the chessboard by lines
abstract: Let $p_n$ be the least number of lines meeting the interior of every cell of an $n\times n$ board. We prove that $\liminf_{n\to\infty}p_n/n\ge0.7520517>\frac34$. The previous bound was $0.7$. The proof is computer-assisted. It identifies a non-negative polynomial on the unit square and bounds its integral along every line.

title: Stability of the tangent bundle on del Pezzo surfaces
abstract: In this article, we study the Bridgeland stability of the tangent bundle on del Pezzo surfaces. We obtain a complete description of the region where the tangent bundle is (un)stable with respect to the standard Bridgeland stability conditions associated to the anticanonical polarization.

title: Relax-and-Sparsify Approximation Algorithms for Sparse Ridge Regression
abstract: This paper studies sparse ridge regression in the low-rank, high-dimensional setting that often arises when data collection is expensive. By exploiting the low-rank structure, we develop approximation algorithms within a relax-and-sparsify framework: solve a convex relaxation and then sparsify its solution to satisfy the original sparsity constraint. Specifically, we establish a tight rank-dependent sparsity bound for the convex relaxation by decomposing its support into two parts. This decomposition in turn motivates two approximation strategies, parameter reduction and binary redistribution, each exploiting a different part. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that the binary redistribution algorithms outperform the benchmarks in most instances.

title: A simplified temporal logic completeness proof
abstract: A temporal logic discussed in the author's book "Logics of Time and Computation" is given a simpler proof of semantic completeness, eliminating some flaws in the original.

title: On the number of elite primes
abstract: A prime $p$ is elite if all sufficiently large Fermat numbers $F_n=2^{2^n}+1$ are quadratic nonresidues modulo $p$. Let $E(x)$ be the number of elite primes up to $x$. The best published bounds are $E(x)\ll x/(\log x)^{3/2}$ unconditionally and $E(x)\ll x^{5/6}$ under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), both due to Just. Just and Pollack remarked, without a written proof, that sorting primes by the exact power of $2$ dividing $p-1$ should give $x/(\log x)^{2-\varepsilon}$ and $x^{3/4+\varepsilon}$. We give complete proofs of slightly sharper statements: $E(x)\le(16+o(1))x\log\log x/(\log x)^2$ unconditionally, and $E(x)\ll x^{3/4}(\log x)^{1/2}$ under GRH. We also recall, with short proofs, known facts about the period of $(F_n\bmod p)$ that go back to Aigner: every elite prime $p$ satisfies the defining condition from the index $v_2(\operatorname{ord}_p 2)$ onwards, and the period is even unless $p\in\{3,5\}$. Finally, we show under GRH that, when the moduli involved are at most $x^{1/3}$, the set of primes bounded by the sieve argument has size $\asymp x\log\log x/(\log x)^2$. This indicates that the remaining factor $\log\log x$ cannot be removed by this method alone. All theorems of the paper have been formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant, with the Brun--Titchmarsh inequality and two standard consequences of GRH as explicit hypotheses.

title: Symbolic Powers and Asymptotic Invariants of Invariant Ideals in Determinantal Rings
abstract: Let $A$ be the coordinate ring of a bounded-rank locus of generic, symmetric, alternating, or Hankel matrices. Thus $A$ is the quotient of a polynomial ring by a generic determinantal, symmetric determinantal, generic Pfaffian, or Hankel determinantal ideal. In each case there is a nested family of rank primes ${\mathfrak p}_1\supset {\mathfrak p}_2\supset\cdots\supset{\mathfrak p}_q$ and a standard-monomial basis whose shapes are diagrams with parts at most $q$. We isolate the common properties of these four straightening theories and use them to give a uniform treatment of products $D_σ={\mathfrak p}_{σ_1}\cdots{\mathfrak p}_{σ_s}$ in the quotient ring $A$, extending analogous results over suitable polynomial rings. In all four cases the shape $σ$ must have parts of size at most $q$. We determine their primary decompositions and associated primes in the rank-$q$ quotient, compute all symbolic powers with respect to the full set of associated primes, and prove that their symbolic Rees algebras are finitely generated. In the generic, symmetric, and alternating cases the respective symbolic Rees algebras are also normal, and Cohen--Macaulay. We also determine the asymptotic resurgence $\widehatρ$ and Waldschmidt constants of these ideals and prove they are related by $\widehatρ(D_σ)=α(D_σ)/\widehatα(D_σ)$.

title: The Dedekind-MacNeille Completion as a Functor
abstract: We study the Dedekind-MacNeille completion through representable functors on the wide subcategory $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$ of posets and lower cut-continuous (closed) maps. On this category the completion is contravariantly functorial and naturally isomorphic to $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}}(-,[1])^{\mathrm{op}}$, via $A\mapstoχ_A$ and its inverse $f\mapsto f^{-1}(\{0\})$. The naturality of this identification makes the Yoneda lemma applicable: uniqueness of the representing object and the endomorphism monoid of the completion follow formally. We also show that $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$ is full in $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$, that $\mathbf{CLat}_\wedge$ is equivalent to a full subcategory of $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and that the covariant adjunction refines to a $2$-adjunction whose idempotent monad has Eilenberg--Moore algebras equivalent to $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$.

title: Certified Algorithms for Gaussian Location Mixture NPMLEs via Discretized Gradient Flows
abstract: We study the computation of approximate nonparametric maximum likelihood estimators (NPMLEs) for Gaussian location mixtures in arbitrary dimension $d\ge 1$ via the Fisher-Rao gradient flow. We provide a certified algorithm based on an entropic proximal discretization of the flow which, given a sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$, returns an absolutely continuous mixing measure $\tildeμ$ admitting an exact finite-dimensional representation and satisfying $\hat L_n-L_n(f_{\tildeμ})\le\varepsilon$. For almost every dataset $X_1,\cdots, X_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying $n>2(d+1)(m+1)^2$, where $m$ is the number of support points of the NPMLE, the algorithm requires $O(n\varepsilon^{-1}\log^{d+2}(1/\varepsilon))$ time. En route, we also establish results on the well-posedness and convergence properties of the continuous-time Fisher--Rao flow. In particular, initializing the flow at the uniform probability measure on a ball containing the convex hull of the observations, we show that $\hat L_n-L_n(f_{μ_t})=O(\log t/t)$. We also establish that, for almost every dataset satisfying the same condition on $n$ as above, the set of global maxima of the optimal score is the same as the support of the NPMLE, and the Hessian of the optimal score is nondegenerate at these points, extending a result of (Polyanskiy-Sellke, 2025) to higher dimensions.

title: The Erdős similarity problem for polynomials and analytic maps
abstract: In this paper, we study the Erdős similarity problem by replacing affine copies with images of polynomial maps or analytic maps. This is inspired by a connection between a partial converse of Szemerédi's theorem and the Erdős similarity problem and its variants, as well as a version of polynomial Szemerédi's theorem by Bergelson and Leibman. In particular, we strengthen several known results in the literature. We show that a large class of sequence are not polynomially universal in this sense. First, for sequences satisfying suitable gap hypotheses, an explicit Cantor-type witness is constructed. Second, for sets satisfying certain growth conditions, a random Cantor-type witness is constructed, extending work of Kolountzakis. This also extends certain results in recent work of Cuéllar-Iosevich-Kulkarni-Aravena-Yavicoli to the polynomial setting. Finally, we show for arbitrary sequences $A$ with zero as an accumulation point that the $(d+3)$-fold sumset $(d+3)A$ is not polynomially universal when restricted to polynomials of degree at most $d$; this complements classical work of Bourgain.

title: Cyclic Hasse diagrams of manifolds and noncommutative path cohomology
abstract: Let $M$ be a connected oriented closed manifold of dimension $d\geq 2$, equipped with a regular CW structure, and let $P$ be its face poset. We consider the cyclic Hasse diagram $G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, obtained from the directed Hasse diagram $G_P$ by adding an arrow from each maximal cell to every $0$-cell of $M$. Over an arbitrary field $\mathbb K$, we completely describe the path cohomology algebra $PH^*(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$ in terms of the $\mathbb K$-Betti numbers of $M$. In particular, this algebra is not graded commutative whenever the dimension of $H^*(M)$ over $\mathbb K$ is at least 4. This disproves Grigor'yan's conjecture on graded commutativity. Moreover, as $M$ ranges over connected oriented closed surfaces, the even subalgebras $PH^{\mathrm{even}}(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$, regarded as ungraded associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras, satisfy no common algebraic identity beyond those satisfied by all associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras. These results distinguish GLMY path cohomology from classical cohomology, whose cup product is graded commutative and whose even subalgebra is commutative. As an application, we construct a digraph $G$ for which the Künneth formula for the categorical product $G\times G$ fails, answering a question of Pinto negatively and disproving another conjecture of Grigor'yan.

title: Lengths and Counting of Palindromic Prefixes of Standard Sturmian Words
abstract: Every standard Sturmian word $c_\mathbf{d}$ is determined by a directive sequence $\mathbf{d}=(d_i)_{i\ge 1}$ of positive integers, and its palindromic prefixes are obtained by iterated palindromic closure. We describe the lengths of these prefixes by the numbers $j\,\ell_{i-1}+\ell_{i-2}-2$, where $\ell_n$ is the length of the $n$-th standard word and $1\le j\le d_i$, and we show that each nonzero length is attained by exactly one pair $(i,j)\neq(1,1)$. For a purely periodic directive sequence of period $k$ we then prove that the number $π_\mathbf{d}(N)$ of nonempty palindromic prefixes of length at most $N$ satisfies \[ π_\mathbf{d}(N)\sim\frac{d_1+\cdots+d_k}{\logλ_\mathbf{d}}\,\log N, \] where $λ_\mathbf{d}$ is the largest eigenvalue of the matrix $M(d_1)\cdots M(d_k)$. For the Fibonacci word this gives $π_\mathbf{d}(N)\sim\log N/\log\varphi$, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$.

title: Feasibility certificates for DeePC: A set invariance approach
abstract: DeePC is posed on a window of past inputs and outputs, so its feasible set is a set of histories and is not available in closed form. We write the DeePC solution as an implicit ReLU network whose weights are built from Hankel matrices and whose activation patterns are the critical regions of the underlying quadratic program. This gives, directly from the Hankel matrices, the feasible set of DeePC as a polyhedral projection, its explicit piecewise-affine control law, and an exact linear model of the history window. We compute three invariant sets of histories: the maximal positively invariant set of the unsaturated linear branch, the region of recursive feasibility of DeePC without terminal ingredients, and the maximal control invariant set of admissible histories. We show these sets are nested and provide numerical examples.

title: The Maxwell Bethe-Sommerfeld problem I: Thin-layer induction and results for planar TE modes
abstract: We present a framework for constructing a single medium that supports infinitely many complete spectral gaps for periodic divergence-form operators, which arise from the transverse electric (TE) polarization of Maxwell's equations. The construction proceeds by inductively inserting a seed medium with a prescribed spectral gap into a thin layer of the unit cell. As a result, we obtain densely many counterexamples to the Bethe-Sommerfeld Conjecture (BSC) for divergence-form operators. Moreover, we prove that the thin-layer construction controls the gap topology: by carefully selecting the seed medium, one can realize a single operator with any prescribed configuration of gap Chern numbers. This is the first of two papers that contains all the fundamental ingredients for the thin-layer induction. In the second paper, we will apply this framework to disprove the BSC for the full three-dimensional Maxwell operator.

title: Radar Waveform Design via Convex Semidefinite Relaxation
abstract: The ambiguity function (AF) of a radar waveform describes its ability to resolve targets in range and Doppler. Designing a waveform that attains a prescribed AF magnitude is a phase retrieval problem with four trivial ambiguities, and a time- or band-limited pulse is determined up to these ambiguities by at most three times as many AF samples as it has time samples or frequencies. Existing solvers for the narrowband AF, however, are non-convex: they cannot guarantee that they reach the global minimizer, which is unique only up to the trivial ambiguities, so the recovered pulse depends on the starting point. This letter addresses this gap by lifting the problem to positive semidefinite matrices supported on the pulse band, where each AF sample becomes the magnitude of a linear functional. In the lifted space, recovery is formulated as a convex program, and a dual certificate provides a sufficient condition for exactness. The proposed algorithm, wavex, combines an initialization by relaxed reflections, convex semidefinite surrogate steps, and a local polish. Numerical experiments show that wavex accurately recovers band-limited pulses from complete AFs and from AFs with most of their samples removed, provided the remaining samples determine the pulse, and that its accuracy degrades gracefully as the noise increases. wavex is built on the open-source library invexapi, and the code that reproduces every result is available at https://github.com/samuelpinilla/waveX.

title: Higher-Order Isometric Liftings of Convex and Concave Operators
abstract: We study higher-order isometric liftings of bounded operators on Hilbert spaces under convexity and concavity assumptions. First, we prove that every $m$-convex operator $T$ satisfying $\sup_{n\geq 1}n^{-(m-1)}\|T^n\|^2<\infty$ admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting whose complementary diagonal entry is an expansive $(m-1)$-isometric weighted shift. Next, we show that every $m$-concave operator admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting with an expansive $m$-isometric weighted-shift component, without imposing an additional growth assumption. We also establish an alternation between convexity and concavity under polynomial growth conditions and give examples illustrating limitations of converse implications.

title: Arc connected continua and the double commutant property
abstract: Let $K$ be a compact metrizable space. For $f\in C(K)$ let $M_f$ be the largest lower semicontinuous map with $k\in M_f(k)\subseteq f^{-1}(f(k))$. We say that $K$ has the double commutant property if for every $f\in C(K)$ every continuous function that is constant on all sets $M_f(k)$ is constant on the fibres of $f$; this is exactly the condition that the double commutant of every multiplication operator on $C(K)$ is the closed algebra generated by the operator and the identity. We show that an arc connected continuum has this property if the points having an open locally connected neighbourhood are dense, and we extend this to some continua that are not arc connected. We then develop new techniques that work when such points are not dense, or do not exist at all, and prove that several well-known continua have the property: the Cantor comb, the Cantor fan and, more generally, the cone over every compact metrizable space, every smooth fan with a closed set of end points, and the Cantor grid $(C\times[0,1])\cup([0,1]\times C)$. The property passes to open images. Examples show that the hypotheses cannot be weakened in several directions. For individual functions we show that, on a continuum all of whose arc components are dense, every function that is constant on no arc satisfies the double commutant condition, and that on every smooth dendroid and every fan the functions satisfying it are dense.

title: Higher-dimensional homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic materials
abstract: Quasiperiodic geometrical arrangements, which exhibit long-range order in the absence of periodicity, have attracted interest in the design of composites and mechanical metamaterials. In this context, direct numerical simulations explicitly resolving the quasiperiodic microstructure become prohibitively expensive for macroscopic problems, motivating the development of homogenized continuum models. However, the absence of a periodic unit cell in physical space hinders the use of conventional homogenization methods. In the present work, we exploit higher-dimensional periodic representations to perform computational homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic composites. Thereby, effective properties are obtained from unit-cell problems solved using the fast Fourier transform in higher-dimensional spaces. Using two-dimensional Penrose tilings and three-dimensional Ammann--Kramer--Neri tilings as paradigmatic examples, we describe the distribution of heterogeneous material properties in the corresponding higher-dimensional unit cells, compute effective elasticity tensors, and assess convergence of fully resolved finite patches to the homogenized limits. We provide open-source implementations of all numerical models.

title: Quadrature-Induced Local Minima in Structure-Preserving Lotka-Volterra Control
abstract: Harvest quadrature can change a discrete optimal control problem even when the state scheme stays fixed. We study this effect for a positivity-preserving Lotka--Volterra scheme. The difference appears in a model with harvesting alone: rewarding the scheme's removal flux gives a strictly convex reduced cost, whereas using prey density at the start of each step overestimates harvest and can create negative curvature and a strict local minimum that is not global. Rational root isolation certifies the two-step global minimizers. With diffusion in one space dimension, nonnegative bounded $H^1$ initial data and positive diffusivities, the costs, weighted gradients and Hessians differ by $O(τ)$ uniformly in the spatial mesh, where $τ$ is the time step. A uniform positive lower bound on the reduced Hessian gives the same order for the distance between nearby controls. A large enough effort penalty gives unique global discrete minimizers. We also prove positivity, exact population balance and a common variational limit, and derive exact discrete adjoints and Hessian actions. Numerical tests trace changes in curvature and stationary controls across parameters and grids, with costs evaluated on a common reference using adaptive time stepping. The construction extends to weighted production--destruction systems, giving exact harvest accounting and smooth derivatives on fixed grids.

title: Gordan-Rankin-Cohen brackets on $1|n$-dimensional superstrings with a contact structure for $n\leq 6$
abstract:
The binary projectively $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant differential operators between spaces of weighted densities on the 1-dimensional manifold are called Gordan transvectants or Rankin-Cohen (GRC) brackets. For the two contact series (with an even and an odd ``time'' variable) on the supercircle or superstring of dimension $1|2$, we describe analogs of GRC brackets. We have discovered many new operators. For $\mathfrak{osp}(2|2)\subset\mathfrak{k}(1|2)$, the space of invariant binary operators of every given order is $2$-dimensional for all weights of the densities, not only for the weights considered so far. For $\mathfrak{pe}(2)\subset\mathfrak{m}(1)$, there are three independent binary operators of order $2$, not two. While classifying them, we correct an earlier result on the unary operators: the order-$2$ Bol operator over $\mathfrak{m}(1)$ is only one member of a $1$-parameter family invariant for all weights, which corrects Theorem 5.1 of arXiv:2110.10504.
  We correct earlier findings in the $1|3$-dimensional case and consider $\mathfrak{osp}_a(4|2)$-invariant (GRC) brackets in $1|4$-dimensional case, where the order-$2$ bracket is independent of the parameter $a$ and is invariant under the whole of $\mathfrak{k}(1|4)$. In the $1|5$-dimensional case, the analogs of Bol operators are odd, of order $5+2k$, where $k=0,1,2,\dots$, and so is the first GRC bracket of odd order, which is of order $5$. We also settle the exceptional case $\mathfrak{as}\subset\mathfrak{kas}\subset\mathfrak{k}(1|6)$.

title: An abstract observability criterion via translation hulls, with applications to transport systems
abstract: We establish an observability criterion for translation-covariant families of operators on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$. Under continuity of the observed cell energies, a common summable localization bound, and reconstruction up to a locally collectively compact error, observability is equivalent to the absence of nonzero uniformly local invisible states on every configuration in the full translation hull. For one-dimensional transport systems satisfying the Kalman rank condition, this yields localized observability in the intrinsic Kalman--Jordan energy space for arbitrary real Jordan structure and nonzero speeds. For unions of observed intervals with a uniform positive lower length bound, the sharp condition is that the slowest characteristic travels farther than the gap supremum. Observability fails at equality even when this supremum is not attained. Duality gives exact controllability in the dual energy space. We also obtain sharp criteria for translating observation regions and scalar transport with an integrable convolution kernel. The reconstruction hypothesis is also necessary for observability.
