An anisotropic heat-flux example shows that it applies beyond coercive multiplication-plus-compact Gramian decompositions.

title: Test of p-rationality of a number field--pari/gp programs
abstract: We give a new computational approach of p-rationality of a number field k, when the method using ray class groups is out of reach in a reasonable time when the degree of k and p are too large. The method is based for a part on the utilisation of the Logp-function that we have defined in the 80's. The general pari/gp program makes no assumptions about k and p. For quadratic fields, we give other programs giving more information (surprisingly these programs, with many instructions, are much faster).

title: Property A and the identification of the maximal and reduced uniform Roe algebras
abstract: Let $X$ be a discrete metric space of bounded geometry. We prove that $X$ has property A if and only if the canonical map $$λ:C^*_{u,max}(X)\to C^*_u(X)$$ is an isomorphism.

title: Dynamical frames through Sz.$-$Nagy$-$Foias dilations
abstract: We present a unified operator-theoretic treatment of dynamical frames based on defect operators, Stein equations, and the Sz.-Nagy-Foiaş dilation theory of contractions. An explicit realization of the minimal isometric dilation relates generating vectors to the wandering subspace and provides a geometric interpretation of standard frame constructions. For Parseval dynamical frames, polar decomposition yields a complete factorization of the generating families through the adjoint defect operator. General dynamical frames are described in terms of positive solutions of a Stein equation, leading to an equivalent formulation of the frame index. We also collect characteristic-function criteria for strong stability and joint strong stability. In the diagonal case, the characteristic function expresses the classical separation and Carleson conditions in operator-theoretic terms. The emphasis is on explicit constructions, direct proofs, and a common framework for known results.

title: Dependence measures as spectral risk measures
abstract: For a bivariate copula $C$ with $(U,V)\sim C$, the conditional distribution functions $L_t=\partial_1C(U,t)$ are random variables with means $t$, so that measures of directed dependence become risk functionals. The absolute Lorenz curves of the variables $L_t$ form the rearranged copula $C^\uparrow$. In this picture Chatterjee's rank correlation $ξ$ is a squared Sobolev seminorm and the rearranged Spearman correlation an $L^1$ norm of $C^\uparrow-Π$, and both arise from one spectral risk measure, applied either to the conditional laws of $V$ or to the laws of $L_t$. The resulting classes $ω_φ$ and $κ_φ$ of spectral dependence measures have mirror-image axiomatic properties. For every spectrum we determine the exact upper bound of $κ_φ$ in terms of $ξ$, and we prove sharp inequalities between $ξ$, $κ_φ$ and the values of $C^\uparrow$, which show how little global measures say about the tails. For plug-in estimators based on the empirical checkerboard copula we obtain consistency, rates and a resolution limit, and a simulation study shows that tail-localised measures separate copulas with identical $ξ$. An application to large credit portfolios illustrates the results.

title: Two approaches of estimation for a tempered fractional Brownian motion with drift
abstract: We investigate the problem of estimation for a tempered fractional Brownian motion with drift of the form: $X_t=μt + σB_{H,λ}(t)$, for all $t\geq 0$. Based on discrete observations of $X$ and by using the method of moments with the ergodic theorem, we construct estimators of the drift parameter $μ\in\R$ and noise parameters $ σ^2,H,λ\in(0,\infty)$. We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators, including convergence in probability, almost sure convergence, and asymptotic normality. Finally, by using Gladyshev's results \cite{gladyshev1961new} we provide some consistent alternative estimators of $σ^2$, $H$ and $λ$, when $μ=0$ and $H\in (0,1)$.

title: Fano blowups of Grassmannians along sub-Grassmannians
abstract: Let $\tilde X$ be the successive blowup of the Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(d,n+1)$ with $n\ge3$, in arbitrary characteristic, along sub-Grassmannians of codimension $r_1,\dotsc,r_s\ge2$ that meet transversely. We prove that, if $d\ne2$, then $\tilde X$ is Fano if and only if $\sum_i(r_i-1)\le n$, and we give a similar criterion for $d=2$. As applications, we prove that the successive blowup of $\mathbb{P}^4$ along $s$ planes that meet transversely is Fano if and only if $s\le4$. We also determine when the successive blowup of a smooth quadric fourfold along planes of one family that meet transversely is Fano.

title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, I: the mass matrix and the polygon model
abstract:
A canonical metric $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ on $S^n \setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$, where $\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}=(p_1,\ldots,p_{\ell})$ and $n \ge 3$, is a metric conformal to the round metric that is complete, scalar-flat, and asymptotically flat at each puncture $p_i$. For $n=3$ these metrics are the Brill--Lindquist time-symmetric initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and their ends carry ADM masses. In this paper we study the masses, through the mass matrix, as functions on the conformal moduli space $M_{\ell}(S^n)$.
  The mass matrix $η=(η_{ij})$ is a symmetric matrix with zero diagonal and vanishing row sums (these matrices form the space $H_{\ell}$), and it determines the \emph{normalized ADM mass} at the $i$-th end via $\hat{\mathfrak{m}}_i=\sum_{j\ne
  i}e^{η_{ij}}$. We prove that the mass map $Ξ\colon M_\ell(S^n)\to H_{\ell}$ is a homeomorphism onto its image.
  On the other hand, the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_\ell(S^n)$ is homeomorphic to the moduli space of those equilateral $\ell$-gons in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$ whose sides, extended to infinity, end at distinct points (the Gauss map). By a theorem of Kapovich--Leeb--Millson and Balser, every polystable configuration is the Gauss image of such a polygon, and the Gauss map identifies the space of all equilateral $\ell$-gons with a natural compactification of $M_\ell(S^n)$. In particular, the mass matrix has an explicit description in terms of the pairwise vertex distances of the polygon.
  The mass matrix diverges as punctures collide. The degeneration, its renormalization, and the resulting compactification of the moduli space are the subject of a sequel to this paper.

title: Borel combinatorics of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$-shift actions and hypersmooth equivalence relations
abstract: We conjecture that for each integer $\ell\geq 2$, the equivalence relation arising from the shift action of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$ on $2^{ω^{\ell}}$ is hypersmooth. We prove this conjecture for $\ell=2$, reduce the general case to a problem in Borel graph colorings, and establish the general case in measure. We also show that under certain mild hypotheses on a hypersmooth equivalence relation $E$, every finite-index Borel super-equivalence relation of $E$ is hypersmooth.

title: Integral zero-sum incidence identities and Davenport constants in rank three
abstract: We study the Davenport constant of finite abelian groups through signed identities among zero-sum subsequences. An integral incidence identity of degree $t$ for a sequence assigns integer weights to its nonempty zero-sum subsequences so that the weights add up to one, while those of the subsequences containing any given nonempty set of at most $t$ terms add up to zero. Over a finite abelian $p$-group $H$, the zero-sum subsequences of a sequence of any length have an indicator polynomial of degree at most $D(H)-1$, and this gives a transfer principle: if, for each $t\ge0$, every sequence of $L(t)$ terms over $Q$ admits such an identity of degree $t$, then $D(Q\oplus H)\le L(D(H)-1)$ for every finite abelian $p$-group $H$. For $m\in\{2,3,4\}$ we construct integral identities at length $L(t)=m(t+3)-2$ over $C_m^3$, and prove that these thresholds are sharp over fields of characteristic zero or characteristic not dividing $m$. For a prime $p\nmid m$ and $0\le a\le b\le c$, we prove that \[ D(C_{mp^a}\oplus C_{mp^b}\oplus C_{mp^c}) =m(p^a+p^b+p^c)-2. \] In particular $D(C_{15}^3)=43$ and $D(C_{20}^3)=58$, which are the two smallest cases of the conjecture $D(C_n^3)=3n-2$ left open in the literature. The proofs of the base cases for $m \in \{3,4\}$ are computer-assisted. All of the results in this paper have been formalised in Lean 4.

title: A counterexample to the subgraphings approximate the cost problem
abstract: We prove that for every $k\ge 2$, the free group $\mathbb{F}_k$ on $k$ generators admits a finite generating set $S$ such that the Schreier graphing of the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_k$ with respect to $S$ does not admit spanning subgraphings that would approximate the cost of the action. In particular, this gives an example of a graphing that spans a treeable countable pmp equivalence relation, but does not admit a spanning subtreeing.

title: Local Limit Theorems and Edgeworth Expansions for some classes of inhomogeneous Markov chains
abstract:
In this note, we prove local central limit theorems and expansions in the central limit theorem for inhomogeneous Markov chains satisfying a one-step lower ellipticity condition. As for the local limit theorem, in the general inhomogeneous case, compared with \cite{DS}, we are able to prove results without two-sided ellipticity, although only in the one-step case. Compared with \cite{PeligradLLT1,PeligradLLT2}, we are able to prove local limit theorems without a lower $ψ$-mixing condition. Concerning Edgeworth expansions, compared with \cite{DHPTRF1}, we are able to get results without two-sided ellipticity (under some sequential Diophantine conditions). Our conditions are then verified for Markov chains in a random dynamical environment with a one-sided Doeblin condition under very mild assumptions. For Markov chains in a random environment, we also consider the more general case of $φ$-mixing chains and then, under some mild periodicity assumptions on the environment, we prove local central limit theorems and first-order Edgeworth expansions (without any ellipticity assumptions), matching the results for deterministic homogeneous chains. When the chain is driven by a topologically mixing subshift of finite type, we obtain high-order expansions for $φ$-mixing chains under some Diophantine conditions of a deterministic system generated by a periodic point.
  We then apply our results to bounded additive functionals of posterior states in disordered quantum trajectories and establish local central limit theorems and first-order Edgeworth expansions.

title: Characterizing nonlocal Sobolev spaces as generalized Bessel potential spaces
abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal Sobolev spaces $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $p \in (1,\infty)$, defined via a general class of nonlocal gradients $D^ρ$ associated with a kernel function $ρ$. As our main contribution, we establish three new equivalent characterizations of these spaces. First, we describe $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ in terms of Fourier multipliers involving the symbol of the nonlocal potential associated with $D^ρ$. Second, we give a thorough functional analytic treatment of the nonlocal $ρ$-Laplacian $Δ^ρ$, which allows us to represent general nonlocal Sobolev spaces through its square root $(-Δ^ρ)^{1/2}$. Third, we show that $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ coincides with the image $g_ρ* L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for a suitable convolution kernel $g_ρ\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, which confirms that these spaces are genuine potential spaces. These results generalize the well-known fact that, in the special case of the Riesz kernel, the resulting fractional Sobolev spaces coincide with the classical Bessel potential spaces. In this spirit, the present work can also be viewed as introducing a natural notion of generalized Bessel potential spaces.

title: Variants of Expansivity, Shadowing and Spectral Decomposition
abstract: In this paper, we first distinguish a very recently introduced notion of mean asymptotic expansivity from asymptotic expansivity. Then, we extend the spectral decomposition theorem due to Smale to bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms with the shadowing property. We also extend a measurable spectral decomposition theorem due to Shin to shadowable measures for bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms. Each of the chain transitive sub-systems obtained by Shin can be further decomposed into chain mixing systems by using the ideas of Richeson and Wiseman. Next, we use a probabilistic argument to recover both Smale-like and Bowen-like spectral decompositions for expansive homeomorphisms with the shadowing property. Moreover, we investigate inter-relations among several variants of the shadowing property including the eventual shadowing property, the thick shadowing property, the ergodic shadowing property, the mean ergodic shadowing property and the $M_α$-shadowing property.

title: Diagnosis and Recovery in AI Workflows with Scarce Expert Capacity
abstract: We study sequential decisions in AI workflows and other automated execution systems where failures of uncertain origin require recovery under limited shared expert capacity. Recovery choices affect future diagnostic demand, while expert availability changes which recovery actions are worthwhile. We coordinate diagnostic requests, expert dispatch, and checkpoint-based recovery to maximize expected net operating value. A finite-horizon model tracks uncertain error locations, remaining time, and shared expert capacity. Structural analysis shows how competition for diagnosis changes unaided recovery. When a full rebuild from checkpoint 0 is the best unaided fallback after failure, a larger expert pool can justify retaining more work despite a lower chance of immediate success. Capacity can also raise net operating value before fixed staffing costs while reducing diagnostic hours when advice is requested only after a failed trial. Our Diagnosis-Resource-Recovery Control (DRRC) policy coordinates these decisions through local recovery lookahead and estimates of service requirements and remaining time; its learning-augmented variant uses task-specific quality and duration estimates. In controlled simulations, larger pools draw more requests before repair, and selective diagnosis raises net value chiefly by reducing recovery costs. In a digital twin based on 177 software defects, DRRC with reference-assisted diagnosis increases mean timely completion by 3.27 percentage points and mean net value by 1.85% relative to automated recovery, although the net-value advantage remains uncertain across repositories. Expert capacity changes when workflows seek advice and how much work they preserve. Expansion may raise or lower diagnostic hours, so capacity and recovery design should be assessed jointly by their contribution to net operating value.

title: All unital reversible nonsymmetric rings of order 256
abstract: A ring is reversible if $ab=0$ implies $ba=0$, and symmetric if $abc=0$ implies $acb=0$. Szabo proved that the smallest order of a unital reversible nonsymmetric ring is $256$. We classify all such minimal rings: up to isomorphism there are exactly $186$ of them, $19$ of characteristic $2$ and $167$ of characteristic $4$, and there are none of characteristic $8$ or higher. All of them are local with residue field $\mathbb{F}_2$, the nilpotency index of the Jacobson radical is $4$ or $5$, and $120$ of them form $60$ pairs $R$, $R^{op}$ of non-isomorphic rings. The classification is obtained by a general method of deformation of graded algebras over $\mathbb{Z}/2^e\mathbb{Z}$, whose completeness is proved, and it is checked against the known examples: $\mathbb{F}_2Q_8$, Szabo's example and the ten rings in the family of generalized quaternion rings studied by Grau, Oller-Marcén and Szabo. The presentations of the $186$ rings and the code are provided as ancillary files.

title: Decorated lattices: hyperuniformity and limit theorems
abstract:
We introduce \emph{decorated lattices}, a point process obtained by placing finite random point configurations in lattice cells. A stationary mark field selects the motif laws and acts as a random environment transmitting dependence between cells, while allowing flexible local arrangements. Using this construction, one can efficiently generate large regions of disordered patterns with desired local behavior while the random environment controls the asymptotic density fluctuations.
  Under moment and summability assumptions, we derive an explicit decomposition of the Bartlett spectral measure into contributions from conditional motif fluctuations and correlations between marks. This yields criteria for hyperuniformity, or generally $p$-uniformity. Independent, nondegenerate count fluctuations destroy hyperuniformity, whereas suitable dependence governed by the random environment can restore it despite random and unequal cell counts. Once count fluctuations are sufficiently suppressed, motif geometry and its spatial correlations govern the finer order of uniformity. Under mixing assumptions, we also establish central limit theorems for linear statistics, with fluctuations governed by cell counts or, at a finer scale, by the first spatial moments of the motifs.

title: Two categorifications of the Kekulé relations
abstract: We give new relations in the kernel of the foam evaluation. As a consequence we obtain categorifications of all the Kelulé relations introduced by Morrison. Along the way, we discover an equivalent set of relations for which we provide categorifications as well.

title: Unirationality of Meromorphic Differential Strata
abstract: We prove that all components of the meromorphic differential strata are unirational in genus $2\le g\le 5$ and with relatively low number of poles. In particular, it follows that the moduli space of pointed even spin curves $\mathcal{S}_{5;1}^+=\mathcal{S}_5^+\times_{\mathcal{M}_5}\mathcal{M}_{5,1}$ is unirational.

title: Phase Transitions in Heavy-Tailed Mean Estimation under $\ell_p$ Norms
abstract: We study the problem of estimating the mean of a random vector in $\mathbb R^d$ under $\ell_p$ norms, assuming only the existence of a covariance matrix. In the Euclidean norm, the sample mean is already optimal in expectation, and robust estimators are usually needed only to obtain high-probability tails. Our results show that this picture changes for $\ell_p$ norms with $p>2$: robustification is already necessary even for the expected risk. We prove that the minimax risk exhibits a sharp phase transition, controlled by the interaction between the sample size $n$, the dimension $d$, and the norm parameter $p$. In the large-sample regime, the classical Gaussian rate remains achievable. In the complementary regime, heavy-tailed distributions create a genuinely non-Gaussian obstruction. Furthermore we show that the simple estimator: coordinate-wise median of means whose number of buckets chosen according to the geometry of the loss, optimally tracks this phase transition in its expected risk minimax. We also show that natural projection-based median-of-means estimators for general norms, despite achieving the optimal confidence trade-off relative to the sample-mean benchmark of Lugosi and Mendelson (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2019), can be polynomially suboptimal for $\ell_p$ norms even in the constant-probability regime.

title: The $k$-th Milnor and Tjurina numbers: conjectures and a bifurcation formula for pairs
abstract: We study the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities and extend these invariants to pairs of plane holomorphic germs. We first show that a conjectured upper bound of Hussain, Yau and Zuo on the ratio between the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities in three-dimensional complex space does not hold: it fails already for the simplest singularity, a non-degenerate quadratic one, and the ratio tends to infinity as the order grows. We then prove that a conjecture of Shi, Yau and Zuo on semiquasihomogeneous singularities holds for plane curves, for every order and over formal power series, and show that it fails in dimension three. Using the theory of higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of foliations in dimension two, we introduce these invariants for pairs of plane germs. For every order, we show that the higher-order Milnor number of a pair is determined by the Milnor number of the pair and the algebraic multiplicity of the associated foliation, and we compute the difference between the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of the pair. Finally, we establish a bifurcation formula comparing the higher-order Milnor number of a pair with that of the product of the germs. As a consequence, we characterize semitame meromorphic germs as those for which these two numbers agree at some order, or equivalently at every order.

title: A formally verified convergence theorem for the tug-of-war scheme of the normalized $p$-Laplacian
abstract: We present a complete formalization, using Lean 4, of the convergence of $p$-harmonious functions to the viscosity solution of the Dirichlet problem for the normalized $p$-Laplacian, $2 \le p < \infty$, as the step size goes to zero. By $p$-harmonious functions we mean solutions of the dynamic programming principle of tug-of-war with noise. Our proof follows the argument of Barles and Souganidis and is formalized in full, depending only on Mathlib and the standard axioms of Lean. In particular, we include the asymptotic expansion of the scheme, the viscosity properties of the half-relaxed limits, existence and uniqueness for the discrete problem, the comparison principle and uniqueness for the homogeneous equation, Aleksandrov's theorem, and Jensen's lemma.

title: The Estermann Problem with Almost Proportional Summands
abstract:
We obtain a family of estimates for short Weyl sums $$ \left| \sum_{x-y<m\le x}e^{2πiαm^n} \right| \ll y\left( \frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{q}{y^n} \right)^{\frac{s-1}{s\cdot2^{n-1}}} \bigl(\log(qy)\bigr)^{ \frac{(n-1)^s+s-2}{s\cdot2^{n-1}}}, $$ where $n\ge3$ and $s\ge2$ are fixed integers, $x\ge y\ge2$, $α\in\mathbb R$, $a\in\mathbb Z$, $q\in\mathbb N$, $(a,q)=1$, and $\left|α-\frac{a}{q}\right|\le\frac{1}{q^2}$.
  For $n\ge4$, we also derive from the modern form of Vinogradov's mean value theorem the estimate $$ \left| \sum_{x-y<m\le x}e^{2πiαm^n} \right| \ll y\left( \frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{q}{y^n} \right)^{\frac{1}{n(n-1)+2}} \log y. $$
  Using these estimates, repeated Dirichlet approximation, and an estimate in the intermediate range, we establish an asymptotic formula for the number of representations $$ p_1+p_2+m^n=N,\quad |p_i-μ_iN|\le H,\quad i=1,2, \quad |m^n-μ_3N|\le H, $$ where $p_1,p_2$ are primes, $m$ is a positive integer, and $μ_1,μ_2,μ_3$ are fixed positive numbers whose sum is $1$. The asymptotic formula holds in the range $$ N^{1-θ_n}(\log N)^{A_n}\le H\le N^{1-δ}, \qquad θ_n=\min\left\{\frac{1}{2n},\frac{2}{n^2}\right\}, $$ where $0<δ<θ_n$ is fixed, $A_3=3$, $A_4=\frac{61}{4}$, and $A_n=6n-12+\frac{22}{n}-\frac{12}{n^2}$ for $n\ge5$. In the cubic case, the logarithmic exponent in the previously known lower bound for $H$ is reduced from $10$ to $3$. For $n\ge4$, the exponent of $N$ is reduced from $1-\frac{1}{n(n-1)}$ to $1-\frac{2}{n^2}$.

title: A DGLA approach to global extensions and deformations of Lie algebras
abstract: In this paper, we study the global extension problem of Lie algebras from the perspective of dgLas and the Maurer--Cartan formulism. We propose a new equivalence relation of global extensions, generalizing the early work of Agore and Militaru. This new concept can be better adopted in the study of classical contraction and deformation problems for Lie algebras. Meanwhile, we construct dgLas that control based formal deformations of global extension structures under these equivalences. As byproducts, we obtain the classification of infinitesimal deformations in terms of the cohomology of the controlling dgLas and the corresponding obstruction theory. We relate the dgLa controlling deformation of global extensions under framed equivalence to that of non-abelian extensions constructed by Frégier, obtaining a geometric interpretation of the decomposition of global cohomology into as a disjoint union of non-abelian cohomology. As an application, we study a particular family of an Inönü--Wigner contraction from $\g\rtimes_{\mathrm{ad}}\g$ to $V_{\mathrm{ab}}\rtimes_{\mathrm{ad}}\g$ in the framework of global extension, deformation, and the dgLa approach.

title: Controllability of Acoustic Waves by Point Sources: Reachable States and Stable Reconstruction
abstract:
We study the terminal controllability of the three-dimensional acoustic wave equation driven by finitely many fixed point sources, with zero initial data and time-dependent amplitudes supported in a finite interval. Although finitely many fixed sources cannot control the whole energy space, we establish the following results:
  (i) For source amplitudes in the first-order Sobolev space in time, the terminal state has finite energy if and only if all amplitudes vanish at both endpoints of the control interval.
  (ii) We derive an exact frequency-domain identity for the terminal energy involving a Gram matrix whose diagonal entries are one and whose off-diagonal entries are given by the sinc function, depending on frequency and source separation.
  (iii) For every positive control time, the terminal control operator is bounded below and is an isomorphism onto its closed reachable range, which has infinite codimension even among states satisfying the finite-propagation support condition.
  (iv) We establish a necessary and sufficient radiation-field criterion for reachability, provide stable reconstruction of the unique controls, and characterize the best approximation of non-reachable targets.
  The optimal coercivity constant equals one before the shortest source travel time. At long times, it decays as the inverse square of the control time for two sources and as the inverse fourth power for three equally spaced collinear sources. We also obtain upper bounds for general configurations and illustrate the theoretical results through reproducible Galerkin computations.

title: Simple abelian varieties with prescribed endomorphism ratio
abstract:
Let $A$ be a simple abelian variety over an algebraically closed field, and set $m(A)=2\dim A/[\operatorname{End}^0(A):\mathbb Q]$. We prove that, for every prime $p$ and every positive rational number $μ$, there exist simple abelian varieties of characteristic $p$ with endomorphism ratio $μ$, both of $p$-rank zero and of positive $p$-rank. In particular, we answer a question of Oort in a stronger form.
  Our construction combines Honda-Tate theory with explicit deformations of $p$-divisible groups using Breuil windows. An explicit Frobenius matrix, realized in a window with quaternionic multiplication, gives two reduced generic slopes with coprime denominators. Their coprimality, together with specialization and constancy of dimension, determines the full geometric endomorphism algebra. Polarized Serre-Tate theory and Grothendieck algebraization lift these deformations to abelian schemes. A related construction with an additional etale factor yields the positive-$p$-rank result.

title: Weighted unit equations in cyclic cubic orders
abstract: We study nonrational integral units $u,v$ satisfying $au+sv=1$, with integers $1<a<s$, in varying cyclic cubic fields. The ratio $u/v$ generates the joint order $R=\mathbb{Z}[u,v]$ and gives effective finiteness for each fixed first weight and each fixed gap. Consecutive weights yield exactly seven simultaneous-isomorphism classes, at $a=2,4,13$; in every proper order among them, $\{-1,u,v\}$ generates $R^\times$.

title: Projective Models of Genus 21 K3 Surfaces
abstract: We construct projective models for general primitively polarized K3 surfaces $(S,h)$ of genus $21$ (degree $h^2=40$) inside the 12-dimensional fine quiver moduli space $X = N(3;3,4)$ parameterizing stable representations of the $3$-Kronecker quiver with dimension vector $(3,4)$. As a corollary, we show that the corresponding moduli space $\mathscr{M}_{21}$ is unirational and prove O'Grady's generalized Franchetta conjecture for genus $21$. Then we investigate the geometry of $(S,h)$ through its Fourier--Mukai partner $S' = M_{S}(4,h,5)$ and construct an explicit isomorphism $f : S^{[2]} \xrightarrow{\sim} S'^{[2]}$ together with a common closed embedding into the projectivization $\mathbb{P}^{17}$ of the space of global sections of the normalized universal bundle, using the polarization $H_2 - 4δ_2$. Finally, we identify the Brill--Noether locus $\mathfrak{B} = \{Z \in S^{[3]} : h^0(F \otimes I_Z) \ge 2\}$ scheme-theoretically with the $\mathbb{P}^2$-bundle $Y' = \mathbb{P}_{S'}((F')^*)$ and exhibit an isomorphism $S^{[3]} \xrightarrow{\sim} M_{S'}(3,h',6)$.

title: Dirichlet problems and Green functions for the octonionic Monge--Ampère equation
abstract:
We study the Dirichlet problem for the octonionic Monge-Ampere equation on smooth bounded domains in the octonionic plane $\mathbb{O}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^{16}$. For a smooth positive density that is nondecreasing in the unknown function, we prove existence and uniqueness of a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic solution whenever there is a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic subsolution with the prescribed boundary values. The result also holds on relatively compact domains with smooth boundary in flat translation quotients.
  On smooth bounded strictly octonionic pseudoconvex domains, we construct the unique Green function with zero boundary values and singularity $-|q-a|^{-6}+O(1)$ at an interior pole $a$. We prove $C^{1,1}$ regularity locally up to the boundary away from the pole, together with sharp bounds for the gradient and the full real Hessian. The proof combines boundary estimates based on translations and spin rotations with weighted estimates obtained by differentiating along rotations and dilations.

title: Uniform compactness in a family of $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann problems
abstract: In their paper on non-coercive boundary value problems, Kohn and Nirenberg show that a priori estimates for all forms satisfying $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann boundary conditions follow from a compactness estimate. Inspired by Hamilton, we show that these a priori estimates are stable under deformations of the complex structure, the hermitian metric and the volume form of the underlying manifold. We use a parameter $m$ to encode a deformation of this data. We show that if a family of $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann problems depends smoothly on $m$ and the compactness estimate(s) hold (with constants uniform in $m$), then the family of solution operators also depends smoothly $m$. As a consequence we obtain sufficient conditions for the Bergman kernel to vary smoothly in a family of domains. We also provide a sufficient condition for the uniform compactness estimate(s) to hold in a family of domains.

title: $p$-ellipticity for systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients
abstract: We extend the concept of $p$-ellipticity for (single) elliptic operators, that we introduced in arxiv:1611.00653, to the case of systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients. The $p$-ellipticity condition from this paper turns out to be equivalent, up to a factor depending on $p$, to a condition for systems introduced (and equally named) by Dindoš, Li and Pipher in arXiv:2007.13190. We prove several key properties of $p$-ellipticity akin to those that have been known to hold in the scalar case (arxiv:1611.00653). In some respects, however, the vector case fundamentally differs from the scalar one. As an application we establish the contractivity on $L^p$ of the operator semigroup generated by systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients and subject to Dirichlet, Neumann or mixed boundary conditions.

title: Functional Information, Optimal Channel Simulation and Lossy Source Coding
abstract:
We characterize, within a constant number of bits, the minimum achievable rate for several one-shot coding problems, such as channel simulation and lossy source coding. The basis of our work is a new information measure between random variables $X, Y$ that we call the functional information $I_F(X \to Y)$. We show that this quantity characterizes the minimum one-shot rate $R^*(X \to Y)$ of channel simulation, in which a sample $Y \sim P_{Y \mid X}$ is communicated in the presence of common randomness: $I_F(X \to Y) \leq R^*(X \to Y) < I_F(X \to Y) + 1.45$. For the achievability result, we construct an explicit code using the Poisson functional representation.
  Using these results, we develop new bounds for one-shot variable-rate lossy source coding: given some distortion measure $Δ$, we use $I_F(X \to Y)$ to define the functional rate-distortion function $R_F$. Then, letting $R_O$ denote the one-shot operational rate-distortion function with private encoder randomness and distortion measure $Δ$, we make use of our channel simulation result to show that $R_F(D) \leq R_O(D) < R_F(D) + 2.45$ at every positive distortion level $D$.
  Finally, we generalize our channel simulation result by introducing the Rényi $α$-functional information $I_{F, α}(X \to Y)$ and show that it characterizes the minimum Arimoto-Rényi conditional entropy for channel simulation, ${R^*_α(X \to Y)}$, associated with the Campbell cost: ${I_{F, α}(X \to Y) \leq R^*_α(X \to Y) \leq I_{F, α}(X \to Y) + O(1/α)}$.

title: Ramsey sets are canonically Ramsey
abstract: A set $A$ of points is called Ramsey if, for each $r$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $A$. We show that for each Ramsey set $A$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space, regardless of the number of colors used, contains a monochromatic or a rainbow congruent copy of $A$. This answers a question raised in virtually every paper on the topic.

title: Averaging for multi-scale McKean-Vlasov equation
abstract: We consider a system of Stochastic Differential Equations with two time scales, so called slow-fast system of SDEs. As customary when studying slow-fast dynamics, we seek a coarse grained description of the system, obtained, in the limit of scale separation, by 'averaging out' the fast component of the dynamics (so-called averaging limit). We study slow-fast systems where the fast variable is described by a process which is non-linear in the sense of McKean i.e. by an SDE whose coefficients depend on the law of the process itself, while the slow variable is a linear SDE (linear in the sense of McKean). We show that, when the fast variable is a McKean-Vlasov process and, additionally, the coefficients of the SDE depend on the position of the slow process, the limit of scale separation is not provided by the usual ansatz which one would expect by applying classical averaging paradigms. We identify the limit and provide complete proof.

title: Curves in $\PP^{3}$ are Complete Intersections or Golod
abstract: Let $I\subset S$ be an unmixed, codimension 2 ideal in a regular local ring, or an unmixed, codimension 2 ideal that is homogeneous in a positively graded polynomial ring over a field. We prove the statement of the title when $\pd_{S}(S/I) \leq 3$, and conjecture that this dichotomy holds in codimension 2 with any projective dimension.

title: Joint quadratic base changes of elliptic surfaces with torsion Z/4Z and Z/2Z x Z/6Z
abstract:
We study elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ obtained from an elliptic surface by imposing two quadratic conditions, each of which produces a new point. By the Kani-Rosen decomposition, the joint cover is rational only when the branch loci of the two conditions meet; for two quadratic conditions this means that they share a root. We apply this to two surfaces.
  For Elkies's rank-four K3 surface with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$, a catalogue of $194$ quadratic conditions contains exactly two such pairs. One recovers the rank-six curve of the authors; the other gives a second, inequivalent curve with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$ and rank six.
  For the universal curve with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$, $42$ conditions give exactly $21$ rational joint covers, which yield seven curves of rank two. Two more arise from a tower of conditions. Five of these nine curves are the curves of Dujella, Kazalicki and Peral; the other four are not equivalent to any of them.
  In both cases we determine the Mordell-Weil groups over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ exactly, and we prove that the curves are pairwise inequivalent under invertible changes of parameter, even over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$.

title: Causality and order restricted inference in the Aalen additive hasard model
abstract:
We study a graphical model (DAG) with time to event as a response variable. We use the Aalen additive hazard model for modelling the effect on the response variable of covariates, combined with a multiple linear regression for earlier layers in a DAG. This enables modelling covariates affecting the event process both directly and indirectly. The indirect component effect is represented by a product $θ_1(t)β_2(t)$, where $θ_1(t)$ describes the effect of the independent covariate on the dependent covariate and $β_2(t)$ is the effect of the dependent covariate on the final time to response variable, in the additive hazard model. We estimate $β_2(t)$ by the order-restricted estimator recently introduced in Anevski and Merai (arXiv:2606.23882v2), thereby enabling disease models with early onset or late onset covariate effects. Combining our previously obtained results with the DAG allows for modelling early onset or late onset covariate effects together with direct and indirect covariate effects, which should be of particular interest for studying causality for complex diseases.
  We present a nonparametric plug-in estimator of the indirect effect. We derive the limit distribution of the plug-in estimator of the indirect component, and show that it has $n^{1/3}$ pointwise asymptotic rate and a limit distribution which is proportional to the Chernoff distribution.

title: Augmented Lagrangian methods with Nesterov acceleration for convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints
abstract: In this paper, we develop Nesterov accelerated augmented Lagrangian methods for composite convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints. The methods are derived through a compatible discretization of inertial primal-dual dynamics, yielding a unified framework that couples difference extrapolation of the constraint mapping with a projected multiplier. Under convexity and weighted summability of the primal stationarity errors, we prove boundedness of the primal-dual iterates and simultaneous $\mathcal O(k^{-2})$ last-iterate rates for the objective residual and constraint violation. Under strict parameter conditions, the primal-dual sequence converges to a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker pair, and both residuals improve to $o(k^{-2})$. These results require no strong convexity of the objective or constraints. Numerical experiments examine the performance of the proposed methods.

title: The dual of separated metric compact Hausdorff spaces is an infinitary variety of algebras
abstract: A metric compact Hausdorff space is a Lawvere metric space equipped with a compatible compact Hausdorff topology (which does not need to be the induced topology). These spaces maintain many important features of compact metric spaces, but the resulting category is much better behaved. We prove that the category of separated metric compact Hausdorff spaces is dually equivalent to a variety of infinitary algebras.

title: Iso-Multiplication Modules over Noncommutative Rings: Triangular Classification and Rational Rigidity
abstract: A right A-module M is called iso-multiplication if for every submodule N of M there is a two-sided ideal B of A such that N ?A MB. We construct noncommutative examples of isomultiplication modules which are not multiplication modules, including triangular algebras of arbitrary dimension. We classify all iso-multiplication modules over T_2(k) without a finitegeneration assumption. For a semiprime right Goldie ring we prove that the classical localization of an iso-multiplication module is multiplicity-free. Further consequences address composition length and local rings; we distinguish these from standard Morita, Ore-localization, and chaincondition results.

title: Matrix Star-Triangle Relations
abstract: We propose a matrix generalization of the star--triangle relations and identify solutions underlying the $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ chiral Potts models.

title: Tightness of bulk crossing heights for the planar discrete Gaussian free field
abstract:
Let $φ_N$ be the planar discrete Gaussian free field in $[-2N,2N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$, with zero boundary condition imposed by killing the associated simple random walk on exit. We consider the least height $H_N$ at which the two-sided level set $\{|φ_N|\leq a\}$ contains a nearest-neighbor left--right crossing of $[-N,N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$. We prove that $(H_N)_{N\geq1}$ is tight, uniformly over all box sizes. More precisely, for every $a\geq0$ and $N\geq1$, \[
  Φ\!\left(-a\sqrt{\frac{2}{\log2}}\right)
  \leq\mathbb{P}(H_N>a)
  \leq4\exp\!\left\{-2^{-29}\frac{a^2}{\log(2+a)}\right\}, \] where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. The upper bound yields uniform polynomial moments and a uniform exponential moment of $H_N^2/\log(2+H_N)$. For the upper bound, we compare a marked loop-soup exploration with a graph in which independent site variables open incoming edges. We then estimate connections in a massive field using two auxiliary vertices and bound the Gaussian remainder when the mass is removed. The lower bound uses a Gaussian translation inequality and a square-shell estimate for the Dirichlet energy, without using the massive-field argument. In particular, a height independent of $N$ gives any prescribed crossing probability below one, whereas every fixed finite height has a uniformly positive failure probability.

title: On the planar four-junction solution to a vector-valued Allen-Cahn system
abstract: This paper concerns entire minimizing four-junction solutions to a two-dimensional Allen-Cahn system with a four-well potential. In a suitable regime of unequal surface tensions, the construction yields a family of solutions with varying opening angles of phase sectors. The proof employs two-direction slicing arguments for tight energy bounds and localization of the diffuse interface, together with a new iteration scheme that controls change of approximating sharp interfaces at successively smaller scales.

title: Submatrices of character tables and centers of ordinary and queer q-Schur superalgebras
abstract: We obtain bases of the centers of the ordinary $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$ and the queer $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$ in terms of Casimir elements of the Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}_r$ and the Hecke-Clifford algebra $\mathcal{H}_r^c$, respectively. The key step is to find an invertible submatrix of the character table of $\mathcal{H}_r$ or $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ whose column index set is the support of the corresponding $q$-tensor module appearing in Schur-Weyl duality: for $\mathcal{H}_r$ this is the set $H_{m,n}(r)$ of $(m|n)$-hook partitions of $r$, while for $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ this is the set $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ of strict partitions of $r$ of length $\leq n$. Unlike the case of ordinary $q$-Schur algebras, the submatrix formed by taking the row index set to be the same as the column index set need not be invertible. We determine that the row index set should be chosen as $H_{\min\{m,n\},\max\{m,n\}}(r)$ for $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$, and as the preimage of $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ under the Glaisher correspondence for $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$.

title: The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system
abstract:
We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4πm,4π(m+1))\times(4πk,4π(k+1))$, then \[
  \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k
  =(1-x)^{χ(M)-1}(1-y)^{χ(M)-1}(1-xy)^{χ(M)}, \] where $χ(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block.
  At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4π,0)$ and $(8π,4π)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.

title: Linearization and local controllability of nonautonomous differential inclusions
abstract: In this paper we study the linearization of nonautonomous differential inclusions, whose right-hand side is integrably Lipschitz in the state variable and measurable in time. We establish measurability results for time-dependent graphs and identify the Clarke tangent cone to the set of their measurable selections in $L^\infty\times L^1$. Combining this characterization with a subtransversality argument, we obtain a lower estimate for the Clarke tangent cone to the set of all admissible trajectories starting from a fixed set. As an application, we give sufficient conditions for local controllability around a closed terminal set.

title: The ordered sum-rank metric and linearized multiplicity codes: NRT meets sum-rank
abstract: In this work, we introduce linearized multiplicity codes, which are a common generalization of linearized Reed--Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes. We also introduce the ordered sum-rank metric, which is a common generalization of the sum-rank metric and the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman (NRT) metric (or ordered Hamming metric). We provide a Singleton bound for the ordered sum-rank metric and show that linearized multiplicity codes attain it. That is, they are maximum ordered sum-rank distance (MOSRD) codes. We introduce the support lattice for the ordered sum-rank metric and study duality, support distributions and weight distributions of MOSRD codes. We also show that MOSRD codes are ordered MDS, dually quasi MSRD and, under some divisibility conditions, MSRD (and thus MDS). For linear MOSRD codes, we give lower bounds on the field extension degree by the number of matrix columns, and upper bounds on the block length by the base field size. We conclude by showing that linearized multiplicity codes attain such bounds exactly in almost all cases, and the same growth order in all cases.

title: Hausdorff continuity of logarithmic and Riesz capacities
abstract: Let $E_n$ be $α_n$-uniformly perfect compact sets that converge to a compact set $E$ in the Hausdorff distance $d_n=d_H(E_n,E)$. We prove that the logarithmic capacity of $E_n$ converges to that of $E$ whenever $\log(1/α_n)=O(\log(1/d_n))$ and that no factor tending to infinity can be inserted in this bound. A common energy-transfer theorem also yields Hausdorff continuity of Riesz capacity under local capacity bounds, including bounds obtained from lower Hausdorff content density. Finally, we correct our earlier claims about the uniform convergence of Green functions.

title: Long time derivation of the Boltzmann equation from dynamics of short-range potentials
abstract: We derive the Boltzmann equation from the Newtonian dynamics of particles interacting through a short-range repulsive potential for arbitrarily long times, in the Boltzmann--Grad limit. This extends the recent hard-sphere result of Deng, Hani and Ma (arXiv:2408.07818) to short-range potentials. Compared with hard spheres, two new difficulties arise: (i) in the absence of a Burago--Ferleger--Kononenko-type bound (Ann. of Math. 147 (1998), 695--708, doi:10.2307/120962), a bounded number of particles may undergo an unbounded number of collisions within a short time; and (ii) since collisions last a positive time, three or more particles may interact simultaneously. To overcome (i), we treat such clusters of recollisions as single objects, called boxes, keeping track only of their entry and exit structure, so that internal collisions do not enter the combinatorial counting. The multi-particle collisions in (ii), together with the boxes, lead to more complicated molecules, which requires adapting the counting estimates and the cutting algorithm.

title: Energy-flow bubbles at the Schwarzschild horizon and their Regge-pole clock
abstract: For a circularly polarized plane wave scattered by a Schwarzschild black hole, the time-averaged energy flow on the side of the horizon facing the wave contains small, sealed recirculation cells. In the main family, pairs of zero circles are born on the axis and slide into the horizon in periodic frequency windows; at higher frequencies further cells appear off the axis. We map the cells for $κ=ωr_s/c\le10$ and show that each is the interference of a background integral with the leading photon-sphere Regge surface wave. A cell can die only at a zero of the circularly polarized field on the horizon, and all sixteen measured deaths are such zeros. A parabolic-cylinder analysis at the top of the potential barrier reduces this to a phase condition with a constant $π/4$ and no fitted parameter; recorded before the measurement, it predicted eight deaths in $6\leκ\le10$ to within 0.012 in $κ$. Electromagnetic duality makes the core of each main-family cell a circle of linear polarization; inside such a cell, flow lines lie on nested tori and close into torus knots of one chirality.

title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
abstract:
We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity.
  In the language of commuting squares, this shows that the span condition, previously introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation, is not a necessary condition for isolation.

title: A characterisation of almost gentle algebras
abstract: A finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field is gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special biserial. We prove the corresponding characterisation for almost gentle algebras, that is, an algebra over such a field is almost gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special multiserial, which answers a question of Green and Schroll. As a consequence, the property of having a special multiserial trivial extension is invariant under stable equivalence.

title: Stability of Carathéodory Outer Measures Generated by Spatial Gauges
abstract: We study outer measures generated by covering costs that depend on both the diameter and the location of a covering set. After establishing the metric and Borel-regularity properties of this construction, we investigate its stability under perturbations of the spatial gauge. For power gauges, we prove a uniform logarithmic criterion: if the exponent perturbation multiplied by $\log(1/r)$ converges uniformly to $λ$, then the induced measure is multiplied by $e^{-λ}$. Pointwise asymptotic equivalence, however, is insufficient: on $[0,1]$ we construct bounded gauges whose ratio is eventually equal to one at every fixed point, although their induced measures differ by a prescribed factor. In the converse direction, continuity of the ratio in the spatial variable on a Baire space yields equality of the measures on every compact subset of a suitable dense $G_δ$ set. The results identify a concrete obstruction to pointwise-to-measure stability and a localization principle, while leaving open the corresponding question for all Borel sets.

title: A Solution to the Birkhoff Problem
abstract: For a commutative uniserial ring $R$ of length $n$ we describe the indecomposable objects in the monomorphism category of $R$ independent of the specific ring for $n\leq 5$ and only dependent on the residue field for $n = 6$. Thus, the classification problem for the monomorphism category of $\mathbb{Z}/p^6 \mathbb{Z}$ reduces to the known case of $\mathbb{F}_p[x]/(x^6)$, resolving the Birkhoff Problem.

title: Weighted composition operators between Qp spaces: Boundedness and compactness
abstract: We characterize boundedness and compactness of weighted composition operators $W_{u,\varphi}:Q_{p_1}\to Q_{p_2}$, where $W_{u,\varphi}f=u(f\circ\varphi)$, $p_1>0$, and $0<p_2<1$. A separation theorem for the two terms in $(W_{u,\varphi}f)'$, together with value and derivative embedding theorems, gives two capacity conditions on $u$ and $\varphi$. For $p_1=1$ and $p_1>1$, the derivative condition has a maximal-integral and an area-integral form respectively.

title: Structure of gaps and generalized Wilf's conjecture
abstract: In this article, we study the gaps, the maximal gaps, and the pseudo-Frobenius elements of generalized numerical semigroups of minimum embedding dimension. For these semigroups, we give an explicit description of the set of gaps, explicit formulas for the genus and the number of maximal gaps, and an explicit description of the set of pseudo-Frobenius elements in terms of the blocks of consecutive gaps of an associated numerical semigroup. In particular, we obtain an explicit formula for the type. As a consequence, we show that the type is unbounded even in minimum embedding dimension. Further, we prove that every generalized numerical semigroup with minimum embedding dimension has at least as many non-gaps below its gaps as gaps, and therefore satisfies the generalized Wilf's conjecture. We also prove the conjecture for generalized numerical semigroups in $\mathbb{N}^2$ graded by two-generated numerical semigroups, and asymptotically in higher dimension. For an arbitrary generalized numerical semigroup we bound the number of non-gaps below the gaps in terms of the genus and the type. Finally, we introduce nearly-symmetric generalized numerical semigroups and classify them in minimum embedding dimension. Although the type is unbounded in minimum embedding dimension generalized numerical semigroups, nearly-symmetric ones have type at most two.

title: Multiplicity of sign-changing solutions to higher-order $Q$-curvature equations
abstract: In this paper, we employ the dual cone method to establish the existence of infinitely many sign-changing solutions to the $Q$-curvature problem involving $GJMS$-operators of arbitrary order $m$ on closed Riemannian manifolds of dimension $n > 2m$, under the assumptions that the operators are coercive and positivity-preserving and that the manifold admits appropriate symmetries. To demonstrate the applicability of our framework, we provide explicit examples on both closed Einstein manifolds and closed special Einstein products. Notably, one of the major contributions of this work is deriving explicit conditions that guarantee the coercivity of $GJMS$-operators on closed special Einstein products.

title: Representability of Intertwining Operators for Weak Modules of Vertex Operator Algebras
abstract: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra. For every weak $V$-module $W$, we construct a weak $V \otimes V$-module $\mathcal{R}(W)$ representing the bifunctor $\mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-}$ of intertwining operator spaces, in the sense that there exists a natural isomorphism \[ \mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-} \cong \Hom_{V\otimes V} \ab\big(-\otimes -, \; \mathcal{R}(W)). \] As applications of this natural isomorphism, we first establish a Yoneda-type lemma for spaces of intertwining operators, and then identify the unique largest locally restricted submodule $\mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime)$ of $\mathcal{R}(V^\prime)$ with the coend of the bifunctor $-\otimes-^\prime$: \[ \mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime) \cong \int^{M} M \otimes M^\prime, \] where $M$ ranges over restricted $V$-modules. Finally, the connection between $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ and the regular representation $\mathfrak{D}_ξ(W)$ constructed in \cite{Li02} is established, where $ξ\in \C^{\times}$. In particular, if $V$ is a $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra and $W$ is a restricted $V$-module, then $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ is also a restricted $V \otimes V$-module and is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak{D}_ξ(W)$.

title: A Graph Theory Assisted Method for Determining Limiting Probability Distributions of Higher Order Markov Chains
abstract: This paper presents a graph theory assisted method that checks a sufficient condition for the existence of the limiting probability distribution of a higher order Markov chain and identifies this distribution when the condition is satisfied. This method is more effective as compared to the direct verification of the condition since the latter hinges wholly on computations of the full spectrum on a large-size transition matrix. Even though the graph theoretic tools employed here are well known, their utilization in the context of a higher order Markov chain is new. This method is also implemented as an easy-to-use MATLAB function {\tt gtam}. Several illustrative examples are provided too.

title: Fundamental groups of closed four-manifolds with positive biorthogonal curvature
abstract: In this paper, we prove that a group is the fundamental group of a closed, connected, oriented smooth four-manifold admitting a metric of positive biorthogonal curvature if and only if it is finitely presented. This answers a question of Bettiol. The manifold can be chosen to be stably parallelizable, hence spin with vanishing signature, and with Euler characteristic $2(1-p+q)$, where $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of generators and of nontrivial relators in a given finite presentation. Moreover, we show that the class of closed oriented four-manifolds admitting positive biorthogonal curvature is closed under surgery along embedded circles. As applications, we obtain metrics of positive biorthogonal curvature on the boundary of every compact oriented five-manifold that has a handle decomposition with handles of index at most two, which includes every oriented $S^2$-bundle over a closed oriented surface. We also obtain such metrics on $Y\times S^1$ for every closed orientable three-manifold $Y$ of positive scalar curvature and, after connected sum with copies of $S^2\times S^2$, on a large class of four-manifolds with arbitrary fundamental group. Finally, we show that for the fundamental group of a finite aspherical two-dimensional complex $X$ the minimal Euler characteristic of such manifolds equals $2χ(X)$.

title: Stochastic Multivariate Taylor Measure Functions
abstract: We introduce stochastic multivariate Taylor measure functions (SMTMFs), which extend the multivariate Taylor measure function framework through random Taylor coefficients and a possibly random Taylor parameter. We establish their measurability properties and derive sufficient conditions for the associated processes to be martingales, including criteria based on conditional covariance and continuous semimartingale decompositions. We construct standard Brownian motion as an almost surely uniformly convergent limit of finite SMTMFs using the Levy-Ciesielski representation. We also show that the completion of the finite stochastic MTMF space under the expected uniform norm contains Brownian motion, Brownian bridges, fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter H, and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes with integrable initial conditions. Our main result characterizes this completion as the Bochner space, under an admissibility condition on jointly measurable stochastic Taylor coefficients. The proof uses dyadic piecewise linear interpolation to approximate integrable continuous stochastic processes in the expected uniform norm. Thus, the completed SMTMF space encompasses the full class of integrable continuous random functions on a compact time interval.

title: Higher Integrability of Differential Form Globally Solving Certain Minimization Problem
abstract: Let $0\leq k\leq n-1,1<p<\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}\left(B;Λ^k\right)$, where $Λ^k$ is the vector space of all $k$-forms in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $B$ is an open ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In this article, with one global higher integrability assumption on $du$, we study the global higher integrability of $dv$ where $v$ is the unique minimizer of the following functional: \begin{align*} \overline{w}\mapsto \int_{B} \left \lvert d\overline{w} \right \rvert^p \text{ where } \overline{w} \in u+W^{1,p}_{d^*,T}\left(B;Λ^{k}\right). \end{align*} As a machinery, with a similar higher integrability assumption on the $k+1$-differential form $\widetilde{F}$, we prove one local higher integrability of $d\widetilde{W}$ where $\widetilde{W}\in W^{1,p}\left(B_r\left(0\right);Λ^{k}\right)$ weakly solves: \begin{align*} d^*\left(\left \langle G \left(d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right), d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right \rangle^{\frac{p-2}{2}}G \left(d \widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right)\right)=0 \text{ in } B_r\left(0\right), \end{align*} for $G:B_r\left(0\right)\rightarrow GL\left({n\choose k+1};\mathbb{R}\right)$ symmetric, bounded, and uniformly elliptic measurable map, which is sufficiently close to the identity map $I:Λ^{k+1}\rightarrow Λ^{k+1}$. For each of the above mentioned cases, we prove one strong $\left(q,q\right)$ type estimate. As the primary tools, we use the Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality, Fefferman-Stein inequality, and one classical regularity result of K. Ulhenbeck.

title: Hidden symmetries and echolocation
abstract: We study the echolocation problem: whether local spectral data determine a point up to isometry. We characterize cospectrality by the existence of a spectral symmetry exchanging the two point evaluations and introduce a pointwise analogue of Sunada's method for constructing such symmetries. This yields cospectral, non-similar points on closed hyperbolic surfaces of every genus at least three and on round lens spaces. We also obtain Neumann examples on a scalene triangle and on a planar slit domain, and reinterpret a known Dirichlet example of Dixon, Miah, Safronov, Snyder, Vakaryuk, and Wyman through the same framework.

title: A Critical Choquard Problem for a Quasilinear Schrödinger Operator with Singular Discontinuous Nonlinearity
abstract: In this article, we study the quasilinear Schrödinger equation $-Δu - Δ\bigl(|u|^{2α}\bigr)\,|u|^{2α-2}u =λ\left(χ_{\{u<b\}} u^{-β}+\left(\int_Ω\frac{H(y,u)}{\left|x-y\right|^μ} dy\right)h(x,u)\right)$ in $Ω$, $u>0$ in $Ω$, $u=0$ on $\partialΩ$, where $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is a smooth bounded domain, $b>0$, $0<μ<2$, $α>\frac12$, $0<β<3$, and $h$ has critical exponential growth with primitive $H$. We show that there is $λ^*_b\in(0,\infty)$ such that the problem has a positive solution if and only if $λ\in(0,λ^*_b]$. For $λ<λ^*_b$, this solution is $g(v_λ)$, where the change of variables $g$ makes the problem semilinear and $v_λ$ is a local minimizer of the transformed energy in $H^1_0(Ω)$. If $h$ satisfies a lower bound at the critical scale $\exp\bigl(2α\,g^{-1}(u)^2\bigr)$, we obtain a second positive solution for every $λ\in(0,λ^*_b)$. The level estimate for this solution must be done at this scale, and not at the scale $e^{u^{4α}}$ used for semilinear problems. This bound excludes $h=f\,e^{u^{4α}}$ with $f$ of polynomial growth. For $α>1$, we obtain a second solution for $h=u^{4α-1}e^{u^{4α}}$, provided that the maximum of the first solution exceeds a constant depending only on $α$. For $α\leq1$, this question remains open.

title: Global dynamics of large smooth solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
abstract: We establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions containing vacuum to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with bulk viscosity depending on the density, in smooth bounded simply connected domains, subject to the Navier-slip boundary conditions. Without any restriction on the size of initial data, we obtain time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponentialconvergence to equilibrium in Sobolev spaces for the density and velocity. Moreover an initial vacuum point will persist and force the exponential growth of density gradients.

title: Approximate $K$-Conjugacy of Minimal Cantor--Circle Extensions I: The Rigid Case
abstract: We study approximate $K$-conjugacy for minimal Cantor--circle extensions with arbitrary circle homeomorphism cocycles, allowing orientation reversal. Under the assumption of classical rigidity, we show that two such systems are approximately $K$-conjugate if and only if there exists an ordered unital graded $K$-theory isomorphism satisfying the finite coefficient $K$-condition. Our approach combines dynamical corrections along Kakutani--Rokhlin towers with the classification and uniqueness theory of $C^*$-algebras. Moreover, the crossed-product isomorphisms implementing approximate $K$-conjugacy can be chosen as inner perturbations of a fixed isomorphism and its inverse.

title: Boundary singularities for weak solutions of semilinear elliptic problems throughout the subcritical range
abstract: Let $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \ge 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial Ω$. We construct positive very weak solutions for the problem $Δu + u^p = 0$ in $Ω$ for all $p \in [(N+1)/(N-1),(N+2)/(N-2))$ when $N \ge 3$ and for all $p \ge (N+1)/(N-1)$ when $N = 2$. These solutions vanish in a suitable trace sense on $\partial Ω$ but are singular at prescribed isolated points. This gives a completely affirmative answer to a conjecture of del Pino-Musso-Pacard.

title: Concircular Sections Along Submanifolds
abstract: We introduce an equation which generalises that of a concircular vector field to sections of the ambient tangent bundle along submanifolds. Totally umbilic hypersurfaces and various overdetermined systems (such as Obata's and Tashiro's equations) are obtained as specific cases. Given an ambient manifold $M$ and a connected submanifold $P$ of dimension at least $2$, the solution space $W(P;M)$ is shown to have dimension at most $\mathrm{dim } M+1$ with all solutions being of `special type' whenever it exceeds $\mathrm{codim } P+1$. This bound is shown to be sharp. When the submanifold $P$ is simply connected we show the maximum dimension is attained exactly when $P$ has constant sectional curvature $κ$ relative to the ambient manifold $M$. In the case of maximum dimension we introduce a bilinear form $\mathbb{I}$ on $W(P;M)$ which is Riemannian, degenerate or Lorentzian, depending on the sign of $κ$ and show $P$ immerses into $(W(P;M),\mathbb{I})$'s unit quadric. Hence our main result shows that whenever $P$ is simply connected, has dimension of at least $2$, and has constant curvature $κ\neq0$ relative to its ambient manifold $M$, there is an isometric immersion (which we construct explicitly) of $P$ with its metric induced from $M$, into the $\mathrm{dim } M$-dimensional space form of curvature $κ$.

title: Sparse Rotatable Arrays (SRAs) for Cell-Free MIMO: Network-Wide Design of Antenna Activation and Panel Orientation
abstract: This paper investigates a sparse rotatable array (SRA)-enabled cell-free multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system. Under a network-wide antenna activation budget, distributed access points (APs) select active antenna elements from their installed arrays and adjust panel orientations, enabling joint control of sparse array apertures and antenna directivity. To avoid frequent hardware reconfiguration in response to instantaneous channel variations, we formulate a two-timescale stochastic optimization problem to maximize the expected minimum-user rate. Long-term antenna activation and panel orientations are optimized based on user spatial distributions and statistical channel state information (CSI), while short-term precoders adapt to instantaneous CSI. Under line-of-sight (LoS) propagation, we derive the optimal single-user antenna allocation, characterize the two-user max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) and establish conditions for discrete activation and panel rotation to attain the continuous-position benchmark, and obtain a closed-form multi-AP zero-forcing (ZF) allocation benchmark under a continuous antenna-count relaxation. For the general mixed-integer nonconvex stochastic problem, we develop an alternating algorithm based on sample-average approximation (SAA), integrating uplink-downlink (UL-DL) duality for short-term precoding, weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) surrogates for panel-orientation optimization, and multi-start greedy search for antenna activation. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed design outperforms the fixed-array benchmark, improves all-user service reliability with fewer active antennas, and adapts effectively to nonuniform user spatial distributions.

title: Counterfactual Screening of Rare Secondary Overloads in Power Grids with a Stochastic Surrogate for Electromagnetic Transient Simulations
abstract: Power-system operators continually ask what would happen if a component failed now. Single-phase-to-ground faults cleared by single-pole tripping and automatic reclosure usually have no lasting consequences. In rare cases, however, the transient excited during the open-phase interval drives distant lines or transformers into overload that persists after the faulted line is restored. We develop a counterfactual screening framework for these secondary overloads, combining a linear stochastic swing surrogate with cross-entropy importance sampling. The surrogate represents the open-phase corridor through an effective coupling factor and localized multiplicative noise, with both parameters learned from electromagnetic-transient (EMT) simulations rather than prescribed. Closed-form propagation of the mean and covariance permits deterministic calibration without Monte Carlo sampling. On the reduced WECC 240-bus system, a globally calibrated model substantially improves finite-time agreement with the EMT electromechanical state. The global models are calibrated at reclosure and tested on disjoint faulted lines under a longer open-phase interval. Line- and operating-state-specific models use additional reclosure data from the assessment lines and provide smaller further gains at the cost of more separate fits. The fitted coupling is lower than the phase-counting baseline, consistent with the direction anticipated by sequence-network analysis. Cross-entropy importance sampling directs computational effort toward contingencies associated with persistent overload and yields rare-event probability estimates together with a map linking initiating faults to the elements they endanger. By separating offline EMT calibration from repeated surrogate evaluation, the method supports probabilistic contingency screening and identifies where detailed high-fidelity assessment is most valuable.

title: Energy and Radius Estimates for Molecules
abstract: The question of whether ionizing a system of well-separated atoms requires energy has remained open for decades, even though the answer is, from a physical point of view, obviously positive. The analog question for a system of molecules is even more challenging, partly because the molecular geometry is not known a priori and may change when electrons are added or removed. In this work, we investigate and analytically solve the first problem in the special case of a mixture of hydrogen and helium atoms. As a consequence, the van der Waals law for a system of hydrogen and helium atoms, which was proven in [6] assuming our result, now follows as a corollary without assumptions. Moreover, we prove a new lower bound for the `size' of a stable molecule with several nuclei, which improves upon the lower bounds from [1] with even less assumptions. Using among others this lower bound, we prove that it costs energy to ionize a system consisting of an $H_2$ molecule and a perfectly conducting half-infinite plate, provided that they are well-separated. The long-range asymptotics of their interaction energy was analyzed in [3] assuming our result.

title: Learning Advantage Function Surrogates via Convex Conjugate Matching
abstract: A policy trained to make per-unit decisions, such as how much of a product to order, tells us the best action but not the cost of deviating from it. That cost, the advantage function, is what downstream systems need when they have to depart from the per-unit optimum: to estimate the impact of ordering more or fewer units, to respond to a one-off vendor discount, or to satisfy a shared capacity constraint. The advantage function is what makes such trade-offs computable, yet pure policy-learning algorithms often produce the policy alone, without a critic that would yield it. We propose a method to train an advantage function surrogate through price perturbations motivated by a Fenchel-Young loss. We describe a two-stage recipe (fit the policy, then the cost model) and illustrate it on a multi-period inventory management problem.

title: Maximal Independent Sets in Set Systems
abstract: We prove a general theorem on the existence of small maximal independent sets in set systems satisfying natural local density conditions. For an antichain whose degrees are uniform and whose small sets lie in few blocks and whose links overlap little, we show that there is a maximal independent set whose size is asymptotically given by an explicit expression in the degrees, as the degrees grow. The proof comes with a polynomial-time algorithm that finds such a set. This improves on known results for independent sets in uniform hypergraphs; in particular, in a linear uniform hypergraph of large bounded degree, we find an independent set of explicit asymptotic size. Among the applications, we obtain complete arcs in finite projective spaces that come within logarithmic factors of the counting lower bound, improving the known results on Segre's complete arc problem. We also show that, for a wide class of multivariable polynomials, there is a maximal set in a finite field avoiding solutions of the polynomial whose size lies within logarithmic factors of the elementary lower bound.

title: Totally Positive Interpolation and Critical Sampling of Positive Operator Orbits
abstract: How few observations are needed for the stable recovery of the initial state of a linear dynamical system? We study this question for systems governed by a positive operator, with fixed sensors and freely chosen sampling times and positive weights. Our main tool is an interpolation theorem for translates of a nonzero continuous integrable totally positive function. For every uniformly separated sequence of centers, we choose one node near each center so that the corresponding collocation operator is boundedly invertible. The displacement, node separation, and operator bounds depend only on the kernel and the lower separation of the centers; no upper bound is needed on their gaps. If a single integer orbit is a frame, we construct weighted Riesz bases whose sampling counts attain the spectral lower bound up to a bounded additive error. The same method yields bases from continuous functional calculus, including explicit resolvent bases. In the case of normal operators, we give a single-orbit frame for which every admissible weighted design has sampling count growing faster than the radial spectral count.

title: Embedding of Barnes-Wall lattices into Cayley-Dickson algebras
abstract: The family of Barnes-Wall lattices includes the balanced Barnes-Wall lattice $M_n$ over $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{2}]$ and two ordinary Barnes-Wall lattices $L_n$ and $L'_n$ over $\mathbb{Z}$, which are geometrically equivalent to each other. Embedding of these lattices into the Cayley-Dickson algebras of an appropriate dimension is considered. It is shown that for all $n \geq 2$ the lattices $M_n$ and $L_n$ are closed under multiplication and are generated by the sets of pairwise products of their elements. The lattices $L_n \cdot L'_n$, $L'_n \cdot L_n$, and $L'_n \cdot L'_n$, generated by pairwise products of elements of the lattices $L_n$ and $L'_n$, also are studied.

title: Interacting Brownian Particles with Local Time Driven Jumps and Memory
abstract: We study a system of Brownian particles on the real line whose jump intensities are excited by pairwise collision local times and decay exponentially between encounters. For every finite number of particles and every interaction strength, we construct a global solution and prove uniqueness in law. Under mean-field scaling, exchangeable chaotic initial data, and uniform integrability of the initial intensities, we prove propagation of chaos on path space. The limit is a nonlinear jump-diffusion whose intensity is driven by the density of its own position; it is unique among such processes with locally bounded mean intensity. The proof combines uniform intensity and local-time estimates, tightness of particle and pair empirical measures, identification of conditional collision local times, and a coupling argument for nonlinear uniqueness. No moment assumptions are imposed on the initial positions or the jump-size distribution.

title: On Win's Conjecture for Edge-Disjoint Perfect Matchings
abstract: In 1982, Win conjectured that, for every even integer $n$ and every integer $k$ $1\le k\le n-2$, any graph $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $d_G(x)+d_G(y)\ge n+k-2$ for every pair of nonadjacent vertices $x,y$ contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings. In this paper, we prove a stronger result for all sufficiently large even $n$. More precisely, we show that under the same degree-sum condition, $G$ contains $\lfloor k/2\rfloor$ pairwise edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles, together with an additional perfect matching when $k$ is odd, all pairwise edge-disjoint. Consequently, we confirm Win's conjecture for all sufficiently large even $n$, with a threshold independent of $k$.

title: Stability of Plasma Echo Growth and the Sharp Sobolev Stability Threshold for the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau Equation
abstract: We establish stability of growing plasma echo cascades for the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau equation with Coulomb collisions near a global Maxwellian. The occurrence of plasma echoes, or even a growing cascade in a reduced model, does not by itself establish this stability. We prove that the amplification persists under changes in the linearized operator, including collisions and the exact evolving background coefficients, and under nonlinear perturbations. This yields optimality of the exponent $1/3$ obtained by Chaturvedi, Luk, and Nguyen in the Sobolev stability threshold. Specifically, we construct solutions with initial Sobolev perturbations of size $ν^{1/3}[\log(1/ν)]^p$ whose transport profiles exhibit norm inflation before the enhanced-dissipation time scale $ν^{-1/3}$. Since collisions preclude the backward Sobolev construction used in collisionless echo arguments, we prepare the initial data at physical time zero and control the entire forward evolution.

title: Deligne pairing isomorphisms for projective duals and higher-rank associated hypersurfaces
