abstract: Let $p>2$ be a prime and $F/\mathbf{Q}_p$ be a finite extension. We prove that every admissible smooth mod $p$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$, with a central character, and satisfying a Casimir annihilation condition, has finite length.

title: Resurgent Analysis of the Single-Orbit Term in the Selberg Trace Formula
abstract: We study the large-time asymptotic expansion, the Borel-Laplace transforms and the Stokes phenomenon of the single-orbit term in the Selberg trace formula. By a single-orbit term we mean the contribution from a primitive closed geodesic orbit and its iterations on a compact hyperbolic surface, and its formal large-time expansion is divergent. We prove that the divergent formal series is uniformly $1$-Gevrey asymptotic to the convergent single-orbit term and recover the single-orbit term by a Laplace integral along the positive real axis. Other directions for the Laplace integration are also explored by analyzing the singularities of the Borel transform of this $1$-Gevrey formal series. It turns out that the series obtained by Borel transform is meromorphic on the two-sheeted Riemann surface of $\sqrtξ$, with simple poles corresponding to the resonance spectra of the hyperbolic cylinder. The Laplace transform can be performed along almost every direction on the two-sheeted Riemann surface. Finally, the Stokes structure as the limit of the difference between Laplace integrals along different directions can be computed by a convergent sum of the exponential of resonance spectrum. These results demonstrate the phenomenon that the resurgent structure of a single-orbit term in the Selberg trace formula is reflected by its associated cylinder resonance spectra.

title: Entropy and frame measures for self-affine measures
abstract: Let $M$ be a real expanding $d\times d$ matrix and let $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\R^d$ consist of $N\ge2$ distinct vectors. We study the existence of frame measures for the self-affine probability measure $μ$ generated by the maps $S_i(x)=M^{-1}(x+d_i)$ with equal weights $1/N$. Extending the entropy obstruction for self-similar measures with a common scalar contraction, we prove that $μ$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy of the first symbol given the spatial point is positive. In particular, this holds whenever $N>|\det M|$, without assuming absolute continuity or imposing arithmetic conditions. When $M$ has integer entries, $\mathscr D\subset\Z^d$, and $N=|\det M|$, the measure $μ$ admits a frame measure if and only if $μ$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor.

title: Positive Regulation of an Axial Dispersion Tubular Reactor by Optimal Boundary Feedback Control
abstract: The dynamics of the reactant in an isothermal axial dispersion tubular reactor is considered. Our goal consists in designing the inlet reactant concentration, under the form of a state feedback law, in order to modify the state behavior according to relevant process requirements, while keeping the positivity and stability properties of the uncontrolled dynamics. The designed control is also constrained to be positive to respect physical requirements. First, we state and analytically solve a parameterized optimal feedback design problem. Next, we address a positive observer-based feedback stabilization problem. The results are illustrated by means of numerical simulations.

title: Well posedness of the MHS equation with Grad Rubin boundary conditions near a dipolar field in an exterior domain
abstract: In this article we study the well posedness of the MHS system in the exterior of a disk. We investigate the case of Grad and Rubin boundary conditions and obtain solutions by perturbing around the dipolar magnetic field. Unlike prior work in the case of bounded domains, we show that one needs to impose a "codimension four"-type condition on the boundary data in order to obtain solutions. Furthermore, due to the tangency points that appear in this situation, we need to develop a careful analysis of the solutions around these points.

title: Large deviations and the asymptotic geometry of Lorentz balls
abstract: We study the uniform distribution on finite-dimensional Lorentz balls $B_{q,p}^n$ in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. We prove a Sanov-type large deviation principle for the empirical measures of the absolute coordinates of a random vector uniformly distributed on $n^{1/q}B_{q,p}^n$. The rate function is given by an entropy deficit under a weighted quantile constraint. We show that the entropy maximizer is unique and characterize its distribution function as the unique increasing solution of a nonlinear boundary-value problem. The limiting distribution has compact support, for which we obtain an explicit bound. These results establish the conjectured empirical limit of Kabluchko, Prochno and Sonnleitner [Journal of Functional Analysis, 288(1):110682, 2025] in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. As consequences, we determine the exponential volume asymptotics of Lorentz balls and obtain asymptotic independence of any fixed number of coordinates. We also prove a law of large numbers for Lorentz norms with finite parameters and use it, together with the volume asymptotics, to obtain a Schechtman--Schmuckenschläger type theorem for intersections of volume-normalized Lorentz balls. We further derive a variational formula for the logarithmic intersection asymptotics. The proof combines an exponential change of measure with quantile interpolation and a variational argument that does not assume regularity of the maximizing quantile in advance.

title: A Lifted Hessian-Riemannian Gradient Flow for LQR Synthesis under Passivity Constraints
abstract: The static state-feedback gain that renders a linear system passive at an external port and minimizes a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) cost cannot be computed by convex optimization, since the passivity certificate and the LQR cost are coupled bilinearly through the common gain. A previous indirect approach restricts the gain to a convex inner approximation of the passivity region, which is conservative and whose construction scales exponentially with the number of gain entries. This paper proposes a direct approach. The set of strictly passivating gains is the image of a convex lifted set of inverse storage matrices and transformed gains. We describe this set by a strict linear matrix inequality and an affine equality for every feedthrough matrix with positive semidefinite symmetric part, including feedthrough matrices with a singular symmetric part, and minimize the LQR cost over it by a gradient flow whose metric is the Hessian of a logarithmic barrier. For multi-input systems, this Hessian is singular along gain changes that preserve the storage function, and we complete the metric along these directions by the metric of the gain space. We prove that the flow exists for all times, that every gain along the flow is strictly passivating with an explicit storage function, and that the cost decreases monotonically while the gains remain in a compact set of stabilizing gains. Numerical examples show that the flow attains a lower cost than the indirect approach, that the completion is required for multi-input systems, and that the flow can converge to a local minimizer on nonconvex passivity regions.

title: Linear Dynamics of Composition Operators on Zygmund Spaces of Rooted Trees
abstract: We conjugate composition operators on the Zygmund and little Zygmund spaces of an infinite, locally finite rooted tree $T$ by the second-difference isometries. A path Green kernel gives row-finite matrices that characterize boundedness and yield exact operator norms. A rigidity result holds on the chain $\mathbb{N}_0$. Boundedness on $\mathcal{Z}_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is equivalent to $\varphi(n)=qn+b$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with $q\in\mathbb{N}_0$ and $b\in\mathbb{Z}$. For these symbols, $\varphi(n)>n$ eventually characterizes Li-Yorke chaos of $C_\varphi$ on either Zygmund space, allowing noninjectivity and periodic vertices. If $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $\mathcal{Z}_0(T)$ and $\varphi^k(T)$ eventually avoids every finite set, then for each $λ\ne0$, $λC_\varphi$ is Li-Yorke chaotic on either space exactly when the norms of its powers are unbounded. For $\varphi_q(n)=q(n+1)-1$ with integer $q\ge2$, the corresponding conditions are $|λ|q^2>1$ on both Zygmund spaces and $|λ|q>1$ on the little Lipschitz space. For bounded $C_\varphi$ on $\mathcal{Z}_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$, topological mixing and Devaney chaos each hold exactly for injective symbols with no periodic vertices and eventual slope $q\ge2$. For such bounded operators with strictly increasing $\varphi$ and $\varphi(0)>0$, $q\ge2$ also characterizes hypercyclicity and frequent hypercyclicity.

title: On Sobolev spaces and Koksma-Hlawka-type inequalities of fractional order
abstract: Spaces of fractional smoothness in the sense of Riemann-Liouville of order $0<α<1$ were introduced in [J. Dick, Ann. Math. Pura Appl., 187, 385-403, 2008]. Dick also proved Koksma-Hlawka type inequalities for these spaces, using a notion of fractional discrepancy. In [M. Gnewuch et al., Constr. Approx., 63, 647-711, 2026] upper error-bounds for QMC-integration on these spaces were obtained using $(t,m,s)$-nets and it was proved that the above mentioned Koksma-Hlawka inequalities by Dick are sharp. One step in the proof of the upper bounds was the embedding of the spaces of fractional smoothness into Bessel potential spaces, also called fractional Sobolev spaces. We prove that, up to norm equivalence, spaces of fractional smoothness and Bessel potential spaces are equal. From this we deduce that the upper error bounds for QMC-integration from Gnewuch et al. are indeed optimal for spaces of fractional smoothness. Furthermore, we obtain two types of Koksma-Hlawka inequalities for Bessel potential spaces. The first type uses the fractional discrepancy as introduced by Dick. The second type adopts an approach by Triebel from [H. Triebel, EMS Press, 2010] by using the norm of the (local) discrepancy function in an adjoint Bessel potential space.

title: Beyond Finite Dimensions: Duflo-Serganova Cohomology, the Formal Superdimension, and a Kac-Wakimoto Theorem for Unitarizable Supermodules
abstract: The main results of this manuscript are fourfold. First, we introduce relative holomorphic discrete series supermodules over basic classical Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{g}$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(n\vert n)$. These are unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents are Harish-Chandra modules of relative holomorphic discrete series representations. We show that these are exactly the unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose globalizations have supermatrix coefficients square-integrable modulo the center. Second, we define the formal superdimension of a relative holomorphic discrete series supermodule as the parity-weighted sum of the formal dimensions of its $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents. We show that it equals, up to sign, the value at zero of an $L$-packet supercharacter obtained by averaging over the Weyl group. Third, we prove a Kac-Wakimoto theorem for formal superdimension: it is nonzero if and only if the highest weight is maximally atypical. For integral highest weights, it equals the superdimension of a finite-dimensional simple supermodule with the same degree of atypicality. We realize these supermodules through derived Zuckerman functors. For nonintegral highest weights, it is computed by generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology. Finally, to establish the Kac-Wakimoto conjecture, we develop the theory of generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology for unitarizable supermodules. We prove that the cohomology of a unitarizable simple supermodule is unitarizable and either zero or simple.

title: Harish-Chandra Modules for the Lie algebra of Divergence-Free Vector Fields on a Two-Dimensional Torus
abstract: Let $\mathcal S_2$ be the Lie algebra of divergence-free Laurent polynomial vector fields on a two-dimensional torus. We determine its simple weight modules with uniformly bounded weight multiplicities. As a consequence, we obtain a classification of its simple Harish-Chandra modules, i.e., weight modules with finite-dimensional weight spaces, which are either simple generalized highest weight modules or simple quotients of tensor fields modules.

title: Collapsibility of Vietoris--Rips complexes of hypercube graphs in codimension two
abstract: Shukla conjectured that the collapsibility number of the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ of the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph at scale $r$ equals $2^r$ for all $n\ge r+1$. We prove the conjecture for $n=r+2$ and every $r$, which gives the first known cases with $r\ge 4$ beyond the cross-polytope case $n=r+1$. Writing $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ as the independence complex of the graph $H_{n,r}$ that joins two points when their Hamming distance exceeds $r$, we construct a cover of $H_{r+2,r}$ by $2^r$ co-chordal subgraphs. The key general tool is the inequality that, for every graph $G$, the $θ$-number of Bıyıkoğlu and Civan of the independence complex of $G$, and hence the collapsibility number of that complex, is at most the co-chordal cover number of $G$; this strengthens Woodroofe's regularity bound. We also show, using a theorem of Alon, Jin, and Sudakov, that the induced matching number of $H_{n,r}$ equals $2^r$ for every $n>r$, and that $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is vertex decomposable if and only if $r=1$ or $n=r+1$. As consequences, we determine the top degree of nonvanishing homology and the coconnectivity of $\mathrm{VR}(I_{r+2};r)$, and we prove split injectivity in top-degree integral homology. Finally, assuming a recent skew Hamming set-pair theorem of Gao and Zhao, we prove that the collapsibility number of $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is at most $2^{r+1}-4$ for all $n>r\ge 2$.

title: Non-stationary motion of an inextensible closed string
abstract: We consider a non-stationary motion of an inextensible closed string. The motion of the string is governed by nonlinear and nonlocal hyperbolic equations. The nonlocality of the equations is caused by the unknown tension of the string and reflects the inextensibility of the string. We show that the initial value problem to the equations of motion is well-posed locally in time. In the proof, it is crucial to show a strict positivity of the tension when the string is in motion. To this end, we derive a sharp lower bound of the Green's function for a periodic boundary value problem. We also derive a blow-up criterion of smooth solutions, which states that any singularities on the velocity or on the tension of the string do not take place before a curvature singularity appears.

title: Extensions of $q$-supercongruences arising from a quadratic summation of Gasper and Rahman
abstract: In this paper, inspired by recent work of Guo and Zhao, and of Guo and Zudilin, we establish two parametric extensions of their $q$-supercongruences using Gasper and Rahman's quadratic summation, the Chinese remainder theorem, and the creative microscoping method. These extensions yield two one-parameter generalizations of the $q$-supercongruences considered by Guo and Zhao and by Guo and Zudilin.

title: On the invariants of L-functions of degree 2, II: twisted conductor
abstract: We continue our study of the invariants of the $L$-functions of deree 2 twisted by Dirichlet characters. In a previous paper, we proved that twisting does not change degree and internal shift. Our aim now is to show a corresponding theorem for the conductor. This paper is intended as the second part of a series aiming to prove a general version of the Weil converse theorem with minimal assumptions on the shape of the functional equation of twists.

title: Radial symmetry for the positive Kähler--Einstein Dirichlet problem on the ball
abstract: We prove radial symmetry for every strictly plurisubharmonic function $u$ on the unit ball in $\C^n$, $n\ge2$, that is smooth up to the boundary, vanishes there, and has complex Hessian determinant $μe^{-u}$ for a constant $μ>0$. The known Fubini--Study family therefore exhausts all such solutions. For the corresponding complex Monge--Ampère mean field equation, this establishes the Berman--Berndtsson symmetry conjecture in the smooth class and gives uniqueness throughout the known existence range. The classification also yields the sharp Moser--Trudinger inequality on the ball in Cegrell's finite-energy class.

title: The monoid of orientation preserving mappings on a chain
abstract: We introduce new kinds of regular monoids of transformations consisting of mappings which preserve or reverse the orientation of a finite cycle.

title: Triples in matroid circuits
abstract: We prove that, if $X$ is a four-element independent set in a vertically $5$-connected representable matroid $M$, then either there is a circuit of $M$ that contains at least three elements of $X$, or there is a representation $A$ of $M$ such that each column of $A$ has at most two non-zero elements and each of the columns indexed by $X$ has exactly one non-zero element. We also prove a version of this result without the connectivity assumptions.

title: Branch-and-Cut for Maximum $k$-Independent Sets with Spectral Bounds
abstract: We develop a branch-and-cut method for finding maximum distance-independent sets in graphs. Our approach solves a sequence of fixed-size clique problems, combining graph reductions with combinatorial and spectral bounds. We give a compact formulation, derive strengthened inequalities, establish conditions for using spectral information, and evaluate them in a comprehensive computational study.

title: Linear Algebra over Bands
abstract: We introduce Eckmann-Hilton operators on bands, which allow for a suite of matroidal constructions, in particular, matroid unions and matroid stable intersections. This enables the construction of general linear monoids over bands. Geometrically, we show that matroid stable intersection extends the transverse intersection of linear spaces over fields and the stable intersection of tropical linear spaces, lending new insight into intersection theory on bands.

title: Quantitative approximation for Fourier neural operators in controlled ordinary differential equations
abstract: Fourier neural operators (FNOs) avoid the curse of parametric complexity when approximating the solution operator of certain partial differential equations (PDEs). While recent studies primarily focus on PDEs, in this article we derive upper error bounds for approximating the solution operator of controlled ordinary differential equations (CODEs) $\dot{y}=f(y,u)$ using a FNO. Under a Carathéodory setting and suitable regularity assumptions, including a smallness condition, we prove that the size of the FNO grows at most algebraically in $1/\varepsilon$, namely like $\varepsilon^{-(1+d/(2(s-1)))}$ up to logarithmic factors for GELU networks, and is thus sub-quadratic for sufficiently smooth $f$, where $d=1+n_y+n_u$ and $s$ denotes the Sobolev regularity of $f$. Our proof is based on emulating the Picard iteration through the layers of the FNO while exploiting the differentiation formula of the discrete Fourier transform. This result contributes to the quantitative approximation theory of FNOs for physically motivated problems and provides a theoretical foundation for leveraging a FNO as efficient forward surrogate for the solution operator of CODEs, especially in inverse parameter estimation where repeated evaluations of the forward operator are needed.

title: On Hamilton-Jacobi equations and perceptron models
abstract: The solution to a finite-dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi equation is classically known to admit a variational representation in two situations: when the nonlinearity is convex or concave, by the Hopf-Lax formula; and when the initial condition is convex or concave, by the Hopf formula. We identify a third situation: the space variable is split into two groups of coordinates, the nonlinearity is the scalar product of the two corresponding partial gradients, and the initial condition is the sum of a convex function of the first group of coordinates and of an arbitrary Lipschitz function of the second group. This structure is precisely that of the Hamilton-Jacobi equations describing the limit free energy of perceptron models. We illustrate this point by identifying the limit free energy of a class of perceptron models that can be rewritten as bipartite spin glasses, with Ising spins in one layer and bounded soft spins in the other. We also discuss how to extend the approach to several other classes of models, including general Ising and spherical perceptrons, possibly with labelled patterns.

title: Constructing high-dimensional representations of twin groups via several techniques
abstract: In this article, we consider the twin group $T_n$ for a positive integer $n$ and present two techniques for constructing high-dimensional and complicated representations of $T_n$. The first technique consists of composing a known representation of $T_n$ with the well-established Cohen map, while the second technique relies on the tensor product of two known representations of $T_n$. To implement these techniques, we consider the two representations $η_1$ and $η_2$ of $T_n$ introduced recently by Nasser. The first technique is applied to the representation $η_1: T_n \longrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{F}_n)$, which maps $T_n$ into the automorphism group of the free group $\mathbb{F}_n$ with $n$ generators. The second technique is applied to the representation $η_2: T_n \longrightarrow \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}])$, which maps $T_n$ into the general linear group over the ring of Laurent polynomials in an indeterminate $t$. Using these techniques, we construct new high-degree representations of $T_n$ and examine, for some of them, structural properties such as faithfulness and reducibility. This work provides new avenues for developing representations of $T_n$ and related groups using these techniques.

title: Projective planes with abelian collineation groups of type (F) are Desarguesian
abstract: We use prime ideal factorization and residue class fields of cyclotomic integer rings to prove that every abelian direct product difference set is classical. This implies that every projective plane of order $n$ with an abelian collineation group of order $n(n-1)$ is Desarguesian, proving a conjecture of Jungnickel and de Resmini. As a consequence, we obtain the classification of circular Costas maps and of Costas polynomials conjectured by Muratovic-Ribic, Pott, Thomson and Wang and by Torres and Rubio.

title: Rigidity and classification of complete translating solitons and self-expanders with constant curvature in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$
abstract: For complete immersed surfaces in Euclidean four-space whose mean curvature vector has constant length, translators are affine planes parallel to their fixed nonzero velocity, and self-expanders are planes through their centre. This rigidity requires no Lagrangian assumption, properness, volume growth control, or bound on the second fundamental form. Complete Lagrangian translators and self-expanders in $\mathbb{C}^{2}$ with constant Gaussian curvature are flat and, up to unitary equivalence, are properly embedded products of two complete planar curves. Translating factors are lines or grim reapers. Expanding factors are lines through the origin or nonstraight self-expanders. The proofs use moving frames, a transnormal function, a cubic tensor identity, and analytic continuation.

title: Deformation Quantization of Coisotropic A-branes
abstract:
Motivated by the Gukov--Witten proposal that the endomorphism algebra of a coisotropic A-brane should be described by a deformation quantization of its transverse holomorphic symplectic geometry at the perturbative level, we study deformation quantization on transverse holomorphic symplectic manifolds $(M,Ω)$. Extending the approach of Nest--Tsygan to this setting, we show that, under an admissibility condition, equivalence classes of deformation quantizations are in bijection with \[
  \hbar H^2\bigl(\operatorname{F}_1Ω^\bullet(M,\mathbb C),d\bigr)
  [[\hbar]], \] where $\operatorname{F}_1Ω^\bullet(M,\mathbb C)$ is the differential ideal generated by transverse $(1,0)$-forms.
  We further illustrate this framework through examples arising from mapping tori, $T$-duality, and coisotropic lifts in cotangent bundles. These examples clarify the roles of admissibility and the transverse Atiyah class, as well as the distinction between deformation quantizations and global star products. Finally, for a coisotropic A-brane $M$ induced from a transverse complex manifold $Q$, we use transverse jets and the Fock representation to construct a perturbative level action $End(M)\curvearrowright Hom(M,Q)$ under suitable compatibility assumptions, providing a geometric realization of the brane quantization philosophy.

title: Minimax Growth and Morse Indices for the Critical Choquard Equation on the Sphere
abstract: We study the conformally critical Choquard equation on $\mathbb S^n$, \[ -Δ_{\mathbb S^n} v(ξ) + \frac{n(n-2)}{4} v(ξ) = \left(\int_{\mathbb S^n} \frac{|v(η)|^p}{|ξ-η|^μ} dV_η\right) |v(ξ)|^{p-2} v(ξ), \] where $n\ge 3$, $0<μ<n$, and $p=(2n-μ)/(n-2)$ denotes the conformally critical Choquard exponent. For the standard action of \(G=O(k)\times O(\ell)\) with \(k,\ell\ge 2\) and \(k+\ell=n+1\), we use the cohomological index and orbit interval partition to build attained minimax levels with sharp growth \(c_j\asymp j^{2p/(p-1)}\). All \(G\)-invariant solutions at \(c_j\) change sign for \(j\ge 2\). If \(p\ge 2\), positivity of the Riesz form on nodal truncations gives \(N_G(v)\le m_G(v)\), and \(N_G(v)\le j\) whenever \(E(v)=c_j\). Here \(N_G\) counts nodal domains, and \(m_G,ν_G\) are the invariant Morse index and nullity, respectively. In particular, \(c_2\) is the least energy of \(G\)-invariant sign-changing solutions, with such solutions having two nodal domains. Under the additional assumption that every critical point of the reduced functional \(Ψ\) at level \(c_j\) is isolated in the full critical set of \(Ψ\), the critical group theory gives \(m_G\leq j\leq m_G+ν_G\) for a selected critical solution. For \(p\ge 2\), only finitely many angular blocks contribute to the full index and nullity, and every nonconstant \(G\)-invariant solution has transverse negative directions. When \(k=\ell\) and \(μ>0\) is sufficiently small, we compute the radial index and nullity in the \((1,0),(0,1),(1,1)\) blocks of solutions from minimizing the reduced energy over \(G\)-invariant functions odd under factor interchange.

title: Criterion for Glasner property and IC-Rigidity for actions on homogeneous space
abstract: Let $G$ be a semi-group acting continuously on a compact metric space $X$. The action $G\curvearrowright X$ is called Glasner if for every infinite set $A\subseteq X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $g\in G$ such that $gA$ is $\varepsilon$-dense in $X$. Let $\mathcal{K}(X)$ denote the space of nonempty compact subsets of $X$. A $G$-invariant Borel probability measure on $\mathcal{K}(X)$ is called an invariant random compact (IRC), and the action is IC-rigid if $δ_X$ is the only IRC supported on infinite compact subsets of $X$. In this paper we give a pair-correlation criterion implying both IC-rigidity and the Glasner property. As an application, we prove both these properties for finitely generated $\operatorname{Ad}$-Zariski-dense semi-groups acting on compact homogeneous spaces $G/Λ$, where $G$ is connected and noncompact with simple Lie algebra and $Λ<G$ is a cocompact lattice; in particular, this applies to finitely generated Zariski-dense semi-groups of $\mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. We also derive a Fourier-analytic criterion for semi-group actions on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and use it to prove IC-rigidity for actions arising from suitable matrix-valued polynomials.

title: A Recursive Construction of Perfect Arrays of Every Shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$ over the Unit Quaternions
abstract: We extend the recursive construction of perfect and odd perfect sequences over the simple unit quaternions $\Qe=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$ of Blake to arrays of any dimension. The three operations of that construction act on one direction of an array at a time, and are valid whenever the array is periodic in the remaining directions. Starting from a perfect array $P$ of shape $M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ they give perfect arrays of shape $2^a\times M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ for every $a\ge0$, with explicit index functions and with the array orthogonality property for the divisor $2$ in the lifted direction; from $a=5$ on these arrays are, in general, Kronecker products of a sequence with $P$ in neither order. Applied direction by direction, the construction gives perfect arrays over $\Qe$ in every shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$, and in every shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_{d-1}}\times N$ for which a perfect sequence of length $N$ over $\Qe$ exists. The contrast with the binary alphabet is sharp: a perfect binary array of shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$ exists only when $\sum a_k$ is even and $\max a_k\le\frac12\sum a_k+1$, by a theorem of Jedwab and Kraemer on Menon difference sets in abelian $2$-groups, whereas over $\Qe$ there is no constraint on the shape. We also show that, unlike the one-dimensional case, single arrays carrying a non-central twist do exist in two dimensions, and determine where the one-dimensional non-existence argument breaks.

title: Relationship between generic Hecke algebra modules and $0$-Hecke algebra modules
abstract: Let $H_{R,a}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ be the Hecke algebra over a principal ideal domain $R$ with parameter $a\in R$. The representation theories of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ differ substantially and have largely been studied independently. In this paper, we relate the categories of finitely generated modules of these two algebras through specialization functors from the category of finitely generated $H_{\mathbb{C}[v^{1/2}];v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules. We first investigate the fundamental properties of these functors concerning dimensions, essential surjectivity, and characters. We then construct $H_{\mathbb{C}[v^{1/2}];v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules which, through these functors, provide connections between skew Specht modules of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and $0$-Hecke skew Specht modules of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$, and between Kazhdan--Lusztig cell modules of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and dual plactic class modules of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$. Both families of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules are closely related to regular Schur labeled skew shape posets. We further explore how specialization functors relate the Frobenius characteristic to the quasisymmetric characteristic and connects the branching rules for skew Specht modules with those for $0$-Hecke skew Specht modules. Finally, we use the established connection with Kazhdan--Lusztig cell modules to obtain a result on the classification of dual plactic class modules up to isomorphism.

title: A hyperhamiltonian approach to symmetry of the Dirac equation
abstract: The Dirac equation is the simplest wave equation invariant under the Poincaré group, and was indeed determined by Dirac precisely by requiring this invariance. Moreover it is invariant under dilations of the wave function, as follows by its linear character. It is known that the Dirac equation possesses, besides these, other symmetries, which in this sense are the special part of the Dirac equation's full symmetry. In previous work we have shown that the Dirac equation can be cast in hyperhamiltonian terms. Here we show that the symmetries can also be described in hyperhamiltonian terms.

title: Singular Kähler-Ricci solitons and complete gradient shrinking Kähler-Ricci solitons on non-compact manifolds
abstract: We construct a class of complete gradient shrinking Kähler-Ricci solitons on non-compact toric manifolds by exhausting a family of singular Kähler-Ricci solitons associated to multiple divisors. The construction method will be also extended on non-compact $\mathbf G$-manifolds.

title: Rigidity of Stationary Domains for Robin Torsion in the Plane
abstract: For every positive Robin parameter, we prove that a bounded simply connected planar domain with $C^{2,α}$ boundary is stationary for Robin torsional rigidity under an area constraint if and only if it is a disk. No convexity, curvature bound, or additional condition on the overdetermined constant is assumed. The difficulty is that the stationarity condition couples the boundary trace of the Robin torsion function, its tangential derivative, and the boundary curvature. We encode this condition through a normalized Airy stress function and construct a superharmonic auxiliary function by a quartic minimization calibrated on disks. The boundary structure of this auxiliary function allows us to identify a point where it attains its minimum on the boundary and has a nonnegative outward normal derivative. The strong maximum principle and Hopf's boundary point lemma then force the auxiliary function to be constant. Consequently, for any stationary domain in the class under consideration, the Robin torsion function has a constant boundary trace, and the stationarity condition forces the boundary curvature to be constant.

title: Fast HOSVD via Randomized Preconditioning and Mixed Precision
abstract: Computing dominant mode subspaces is a major cost in the higher-order singular value decomposition (HOSVD) and its sequentially truncated variant (STHOSVD). Randomized Tucker algorithms can reduce this cost by approximating the required subspaces from small sketches, but may introduce additional approximation errors. We exploit the extreme aspect ratios of tensor unfoldings, whose mode dimensions can remain manageable while being orders of magnitude smaller than the products of the remaining dimensions. Instead of directly approximating the desired subspaces, we sketch the entire unfolding at a scale comparable to its mode dimension to preserve its full row-space geometry, and use randomized preconditioning to recover the desired singular subspaces through small matrix factorizations. We develop randomized preconditioned HOSVD and STHOSVD algorithms incorporating numerical truncation, and further accelerate their large matrix multiplications using mixed precision. Our analysis shows that truncation adds only a term quadratic in the numerical threshold to the classical HOSVD tail-energy bound, while mixed precision introduces a relative \(O(\sqrt{u_\ell})\) correction to the tail-energy term and an additive \(O(u_\ell)\) term under suitable conditions, where \(u_\ell\) is the lower-precision unit roundoff. On synthetic and real tensors, our methods achieve speedups of a fewfold to several dozenfold over classical HOSVD and STHOSVD, with runtimes competitive with those of other randomized methods. The double-precision versions match the classical reconstruction errors to numerical precision, and the mixed-precision variants yield nearly identical errors.

title: Multivariable $(\varphi, N)$-modules and $(\varphi, N_\nabla)$-modules
abstract: The goal of this article is to introduce the category of effective filtered multivariable $(\varphi, N)$-modules and the category of multivariable $(\varphi, N_\nabla)$-modules of finite $E_Δ$-height over the rigid-analytic open polydisk $\mathcal{O}_Δ$, and to establish an exact tensor equivalence between them. This generalizes Kisin's analytic classification of filtered $(\varphi, N)$-modules and provides the rigid-analytic foundation for multivariable $p$-adic Hodge theory.

title: Quantitative homogenization of Stokes flow in a perforated domain under low regularity of data and geometry
abstract: We study the homogenization of the steady Stokes equations with no-slip conditions in a domain perforated by $\varepsilon$-periodic obstacles, whose limit is Darcy's law for the homogenized pressure $p^\ast$. We prove the quantitative error estimate with rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, natural in the presence of a boundary layer, only assuming that $f-\nabla p^\ast\in H^1$. Such estimates were previously available only under strong smoothness assumptions, such as $f\in C^{1,1/2}$. Our geometrical assumptions are also less stringent than in the previous analyses. The outer domain and the reference fluid cell need only be Lipschitz, the perforations may deviate from periodicity in a layer of width $O(\varepsilon)$ near the outer boundary, and the solid part may be connected (in three dimensions) and attached to the outer wall. In the absence of a boundary layer, the same argument yields the rate $O(\varepsilon)$ assuming only $f\in H^1$.

title: Classes of non-invertible simple derivations of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$
abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $n\geq 3$ be an integer. For $2\leq j\leq n-1$, let $a_j\in k$, and $g_j(x_j)\in k[x_j]\setminus k.$ We give two classes of simple and non-invertible $k$-derivations of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n].$ The first class consists of the $k$-derivations $(1 +x_1^{m_2}x_2)\partial_{x_1}+x_1^{m_1}\partial_{x_2}+(a_2 x_3 +g_2(x_2))\partial_{x_3}+\cdots+(a_{n-1}x_n + g_{n-1}(x_{n-1}))\partial_{x_n},$ where $m_1$ and $m_2$ are two positive integers such that $m_2$ does not divide $m_1$. The second class consists of $k$-derivations $(1-x_2^α x_1^β)\partial_{x_1} +x_1^m\partial_{x_2}+(a_2 x_3 +g_2(x_2))\partial_{x_3}+\cdots+(a_{n-1}x_n + g_{n-1}(x_{n-1}))\partial_{x_n},$ where $α\geq 1,β\geq 1$ and $m\geq β+1$ are integers, under the assumption that $a_j=0,$ for all $2\leq j\leq n-1$ or deg$_{x_2}g_2(x_2)=1$.

title: The least Carmichael numbers with $k$ prime factors
abstract: Let $S_k$ denote the least Carmichael number with exactly $k$ prime factors. Like the later searches of Pinch, our algorithm builds the prime factors of a candidate in increasing order and stops as soon as the preproduct $P$ satisfies $Pλ(P) > B$. At that point there is at most one possible cofactor, and we recover all of its prime factors at once in polynomial time. We prove an unconditional bound on the number of candidates the search examines, in terms of how far $B$ exceeds the product of the first $k$ primes. When the search is run in doubling passes, this gives a running time of $e^{O(k)} = S_k^{O(1/\log k)}$ under a natural conjecture on the size of $S_k$. We also show that the constant in the exponent is sharp for the set of square-free numbers that the bound counts. Finally, we compute $S_k$ for every $k \leq 64$; Pinch had computed it for $k \leq 35$.

title: Two-Dimensional Kowalevski Top Problem as the Genus Two Full Jacobi Inversion Problem -Formulation Using Kolossoff Variables-
abstract: For the Kowalevski top, we introduce another variable in addition to time variable, and formulate as the two-dimensional model. In this paper, since the results for the genus two full Jacobi inversion problem for the two variables Kowalevski top are already known, we utilize these results in reverse, introducing Kolossoff variables, to derive a more transparent formulation of the genus two full Jacobi inversion problem. Since there are two implicit equations of motion using Kowalevski variables, we derived two explicit equations of motion using Kolossoff variables, which is different from the Kolossoff method to derive only one explicit equation and to use Hamiltonian-Jacobi theory.

title: The Exact Optimal Delivery Scheme for the Cyclically $L$-Separated Placement in Multi-Access Coded Caching
abstract: This paper investigates the $(K, L, M, N)$ multi-access coded caching (MACC) system introduced by Hachem et al. The system consists of a server storing $N$ equal-sized files, $K$ cache nodes, each with a storage capacity of $M$ files, and $K$ users, each accessing $L$ consecutive cache nodes in a cyclic wrap-around topology. The server transmits coded information to the users via an error-free capacitated broadcast channel, such that each user obtains its own requested file as a combination of the server transmission and the accessible caches' content. Our objective is to minimize the worst-case transmission load over all possible user demands. First, for the cyclically $L$-separated placement, we derive a new converse bound using the acyclic index coding bound. By carefully counting all valid cache supports, the proposed converse improves upon an existing bound for the same placement. We then develop a linear coded caching scheme based on a novel determinant-based interference alignment strategy, which achieves the new converse bound exactly. Exploiting the determinant structure of a random generating matrix (each of whose columns corresponds to one user), this scheme simultaneously aligns interference across all users into low-dimensional subspaces, while preserving the decodability of their desired packets. Furthermore, by averaging acyclic index coding bounds over cyclic user permutations, we derive a general converse bound applicable to arbitrary uncoded cache placements. By combining the proposed scheme with memory sharing, we demonstrate that the achievable transmission load is within a factor of two of the global bound under uncoded placement. Finally, theoretical and numerical comparisons demonstrate that the proposed scheme generally achieves a strictly lower load than existing schemes.

title: Optimal Quadrature and the Curse of Dimensionality for a Veronese Class
abstract: We study integration on a $3^d$-dimensional trigonometric space whose unit ball has all coordinate mixed partial derivatives bounded by one. With evaluations anywhere in $\mathbb{R}^d$, we determine the exact minimal worst-case error among all deterministic algorithms using at most $n$ function values. An optimal quadrature formula is obtained by truncating an exact product quadrature formula on $\{1/2, 1/2+π\}^d$. All weights are positive. For each error tolerance $0<\varepsilon<1$, the information complexity grows exponentially in $d$ with the common base $Λ\approx 1.10546546$. The correction of order $\sqrt{d}$ to the logarithm of the information complexity and the corresponding error limit are determined by the standard normal distribution function. For $b\ge 1$ and $n=\lceil b^d\rceil$, the error tends to one, one half, or zero according as $b<Λ$, $b=Λ$, or $b>Λ$.

title: Relaxation of one-dimensional variational problems without growth constraints
abstract: We study the integral representation of the relaxation of integral functionals of the form u-> \int f(x,u(x),u'(x)) dx, for Sobolev functions u\,: (a, b) $\rightarrow$ RN with fixed Dirichlet boundary conditions. Unlike classical works on the subject, we require a very mild growth condition on the Lagrangian f to make our statement as natural and general as possible. We state four different situations in which we manage to obtain an explicit expression for the relaxation on BV , which is usually the natural framework for such weak growth conditions. Our goal is also to express a few unifying assumptions on the Lagrangian to obtain the expected relaxation formula.

title: Affine pairs of minimizing units in totally real non-Galois cubic fields
abstract: Let $Γ$ be a rank-two subgroup of the integral norm-one units in a totally real non-Galois cubic field. We prove that two distinct affinely equivalent minima of Godwin's spread on $Γ\setminus\{1\}$ generate $Γ$ and determine its complete minimum set: a pair with sum $\pm2$ or a triple of integral translates of product one. Every minimum generates the order $\mathbb{Z}[Γ]$. For an order whose norm-one units have such a pair, the order generated by its units is the smallest suborder with the same minimum value. We also give explicit families and a maximal order with minima in two distinct affine classes.

title: Explicit Tartakowsky theorem and universality criterion sets over totally real number fields
abstract: We prove an explicit version of Tartakowsky's theorem over all totally real number fields. Namely, a positive definite integral lattice of rank at least five represents every totally positive integer that it represents locally, provided that the norm of the integer exceeds an explicit bound, exponential in powers of the volume of the lattice and of the discriminant of the field. As an application, we give explicit criterion sets for universal quadratic forms over all but finitely many real quadratic fields. Finally, we determine the minimal criterion sets for an infinite family of real quadratic fields.

title: Sign Primal-Dual Gradient Dynamics for Supply-Demand Coordination under Binary Human Feedback
abstract: This paper addresses supply-demand coordination, in which a supplier sets prices to balance the demands of multiple buyers against limited resources. Existing studies typically solve the supply-demand coordination problem with a distributed algorithm called primal-dual gradient dynamics (PDGD), assuming that each buyer discloses the value of its own utility or marginal utility function. In contrast, we assume that each buyer discloses only binary information, namely whether it wants more or less of the current amount, and propose Sign PDGD. Sign PDGD is a PDGD algorithm in which the buyers' update depends only on the sign information. We analyze the convergence of Sign PDGD by interpreting it as a sliding mode control (SMC). For a quadratic cost and linear constraints, we show that under a gain condition, the primal and dual variables converge to the optimal solution. Numerical simulations on a toy resource-sharing problem confirm the two-phase behavior of SMC and show that the primal and dual variables approach the optimal solution.

title: Tunneling effect in some singular wells
abstract: The Schrödinger operator in one dimension is considered. When the electric potential has a linear/V-shaped well, an approximation of the ground-state is established at fixed distance from the well. In this situation, the classical WKB analysis and the localization techniques à la Agmon near a non-degenerate minimum do not work. We propose an alternative to the WKB analysis better suited to the shape of the well and we prove that our Ansatz is an exponentially good approximation by means of revisited (and simplified) Agmon estimates.

title: High-order Crank-Nicolson method via diagonal Padé factorization
abstract: We present a numerical method to solve the time-dependent Schrödinger equation at arbitrary order of accuracy in the time step, particularly well suited for tridiagonal Hamilton operators. The method is based on a factorization of the diagonal Padé approximants of the matrix exponential into products of linear factors, which preserves tridiagonal matrix structure at every time step and yields a propagator of order 2q in the time step at a cost of O(qN) operations. The propagator is exactly unitary by construction, and at lowest order q=1 it reduces to the standard Crank-Nicolson algorithm. We further extend the method to any Hamiltonian admitting a decomposition into a sum of tridiagonal or diagonal operators via high-order split-operator techniques (McLachlan, 2022), retaining O(qN) scaling at each time step. We also analytically show and numerically verify that the precision is dictated by the split-operator method. This covers a broad range of physically relevant cases, including higher-dimensional systems, higher-order spatial discretizations, and non-separable potentials.

title: Some notes on Erdős' last equation
abstract:
We study the Diophantine equation $$n^h(x_1 + \ldots + x_n) = x_1 x_2 \cdots x_n,$$ where $h \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, and $x_1 \le \ldots \le x_n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. We define the solution set $ELE(h, n)$ consisting of all such integer tuples. We derive bounds on $x_n$ and $x_{n-1}$ in $ELE(h,n)$. We prove that $x_1 \cdot\ldots\cdot x_n \le n^h(n^h + 1)(n^h + n - 1)$. We also show that for $h = 1$, $x_{n-1} \le n + \max_{d \mid 2n^2 - 2n,\, d \le \sqrt{2n^2 - 2n}} d$, and for $h \ge 2$, the inequality $x_{n-1} \le 2n^h$ holds in $ELE(h, n)$. Moreover, we study the minimal value $g(h, n)$ of the largest coordinate $x_n$, and define $g(h) = \min_{n \ge 2} g(h,n)$. We prove that $$ \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{g(h,n)}{\frac{\log \log n \cdot \log \log \log \log n}{\log \log \log n}} \ge 1. $$ We also estimate the growth of the number of solutions. We show that for any $\varepsilon > 0,$ we have $\sum_{m \le n} |ELE(h,m)| < n^{h+1+\varepsilon} $
for sufficiently large $n$, and that $|ELE(h,n)| > n^{1 - \varepsilon}$ for infinitely many $n$.

title: On homogeneous hypertournaments
abstract:
Sullivan recently constructed continuum many countable homogeneous $n$-hypertournaments for every $n\ge3$ by forbidding configurations he calls pair-cancelling. We show that, for every family $\mathcal F$ of pair-cancelling $n$-hypertournaments, the class of all linearly ordered finite $\mathcal F$-free $n$-hypertournaments is Ramsey and has the ordering property. In particular, freely ordered $\mathbf{H}_4$-free $3$-hypertournaments are Ramsey, answering a question of Cherlin, Hubička, Nešetřil, and the author from 2021. For every odd $n\ge3$, we give a simple Ramsey expansion with the expansion property for even $n$-hypertournaments by naming an $(n-1)$-hypertournament and a free linear order.
  We also show that, for $n\ge6$, no unbounded hereditary strong amalgamation class of finite $n$-hypertournaments has EPPA. Moreover, we prove the failure of EPPA for all Sullivan's classes with $n\ge4$, and for the even $5$-hypertournaments.
  We conjecture that even hypertournaments and classes omitting a family of pair-cancelling hypertournaments, together with the homogeneous cyclic order in arity three, are the only countably infinite homogeneous $n$-hypertournaments for $n\ge3$. We give some supporting evidence.

title: Group classification and equivalence of two classes of evolution equations of arbitrary order
abstract: We revisit the group classification of the $(1{+}1)$-dimensional evolution equations $u_t=F(u_n)$ and $u_t+uu_x=F(u_n)$ of arbitrary order $n\geq2$, where $u_n=\partial_x^n u$, and describe the usual point equivalence groups of the two classes. We recover the known contact equivalences between the three second-order equations with seven-dimensional maximal Lie invariance algebras and extend the hodograph construction to points where $u_x=0$. For $n>2$, the dimensions of the contact symmetry algebras distinguish the two classes. We give reciprocal transformations linking the two classes at order three and formulate a nonlocal classification problem. We also classify the extensions of the Lie invariance algebra of the Burgers equation in a wider class of Galilei-invariant equations.

title: Intersection theory and Chern classes on normal varieties II
abstract: We prove a uniform bound linear in the rank for the local correction terms in the Riemann--Roch formula for reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We also establish the usual tensor and symmetric-power formulas for second Chern characters and prove Wahl's asymptotic Riemann--Roch conjecture and its higher-rank generalization. These results yield second Chern classes of reflexive sheaves on arbitrary normal projective varieties, compatible with pullback by finite surjective morphisms. We characterize their discriminants as infima of normalized discriminants of compatible vector bundles on smooth alterations. As applications we prove Bogomolov's inequality, effective restriction and boundedness theorems on normal projective varieties, a Miyaoka-type inequality, and a Segre-class criterion for bigness of reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces.

title: The Odd Shift is not sofic in dimensions $d \ge 3$
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the Odd Shift $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimensions $d \ge 3$. Our proof uses lower bounds from communication complexity, specifically the result of Raz and Spieker on the nondeterministic communication complexity for the connectivity problem. We also prove that $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimension $d=2$ under the assumption we call Mute Ocean.

title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for unique equilibrium states
abstract: Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold of dimension at least three, $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and $R\ge2$ be an integer. We construct a $\mathcal C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ and an observable $f\in\mathcal C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ such that $(T,\varphi)$ has a unique equilibrium state $μ$ and $μ(f)=0$. The system $(T,μ)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ but not of order $R+1$ for Hölder observables, and $n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f\circ T^i$ does not satisfy the central limit theorem. The main results have been formalised in Lean 4.

title: Homogeneous Bracket Flows with Three-Form Flux on the Full Flag Manifold SU(3)/T^2
abstract:
We develop an algebraic framework for homogeneous metric flows with closed three-form flux on reductive homogeneous spaces. The geometric data are encoded by the complete reductive bracket $μ$ on $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak k\oplus\mathfrak m$, while the flux is treated as an additional invariant datum $H$ satisfying $d_μH=0$. For the metric equation \[ \partial_tg =
-2\operatorname{Ric}_g +
\frac12\mathcal K_{g,H}, \] we derive the corresponding bracket evolution \[ \dotμ=
-π(P_{μ,H})μ, \qquad P_{μ,H} =
\operatorname{Ric}_μ^{\sharp} -
\frac14\mathcal K_{μ,H}^{\sharp}. \]
  We apply this formulation to the full flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/T^2$. For a prescribed closed invariant three-form, we compute explicitly the quadratic flux operator, the induced three-parameter metric system, and the evolution of the transported bracket coefficients. The system has exactly four positive stationary points. They correspond to the normal homogeneous Einstein metric and the three invariant Kähler--Einstein metrics. The normal stationary point has unstable index two, whereas each Kähler--Einstein stationary point has unstable index one.
  When the flux also evolves by the Hodge heat equation, we derive the closed system for its amplitude and the three metric coefficients. Every isotropic solution becomes extinct in finite time, with $h^2/λ^2\to0$. For a nonzero transverse mode the absolute perturbation is of order $(T-t)^{3/5}$, whereas the perturbation relative to the collapsing scale is of order $(T-t)^{-2/5}$. We relate the invariant three-form to the NS--NS sector of the strict $\mathrm{SU}(3)$-structure ansatz in type IIA supergravity.

title: Sharp Fourier Extension Inequalities on $ \mathbb{S}^2 $ for All $q>4$
abstract: For the ordinary Fourier extension operator on $\mathbb S^2$, we determine the optimal $L^2(\mathbb S^2)\to L^q(\mathbb R^3)$ constant for every real $q>4$, and characterize the nonzero complex extremizers. The result extends the sharp quartic theorem of Foschi and the even-exponent results of Oliveira e Silva--Quilodrán to exponents for which the usual convolution identities are unavailable. The proof has two stages. A continuous inequality for the moments of $\sin r/r$, combined with a trace estimate along the symmetry orbit of a maximizer, reduces the problem to $4\leq q\leq6$. On this interval, the second variation imposes a scalar necessary condition. We contradict it by spectral estimates for spherical harmonics, moment comparisons, and, near $q=4$, a quantitative use of the quartic deficit. The resulting constant is attained exactly by scalar multiples of characters.

title: Parameter Recovery for the Modified Leray-alpha Model via Continuous Data Assimilation
abstract: In this study, we extend the recursive length-scale recovery method for the simplified Bardina model to the three-dimensional modified Leray-alpha model. The main difficulty is that the unknown parameter also occurs in the nonlinear convection term, so estimating the error in the parameter update requires control of second spatial derivatives of the velocity error. We combine continuous data assimilation with a recursive update of the squared length scale, using observed low Fourier modes and computed high Fourier modes. Under uniform regularity bounds on the reference solution and suitable conditions on the observations and the recovery procedure, we prove geometric convergence of both the parameter and velocity errors at the update times. When the update-window lengths are uniformly bounded, this convergence is exponential in time at the update times.

title: The exact semisimplicity criterion for Brauer algebras of type $C$
abstract: We determine exactly when the Brauer algebra of type $C$, denoted by $\B_r(C,δ)$, is semisimple over $\C$, where $δ\neq0$. We first analyze the two admissible cases for homomorphisms from the top layer to the second layer. We construct an auxiliary operator on the space spanned by symmetric Brauer diagrams with a fixed bottom partial diagram and exactly two horizontal edges in each row. Using this operator, we prove that, in each admissible case, the corresponding quadratic condition is necessary and sufficient for the existence of a nonzero homomorphism. The constant terms of these quadratic expressions depend on sums of contents of horizontal $2$-strips in bipartitions. We then show that a failure of semisimplicity is detected by cell modules in the second layer. Finally, by relating the content sums for admissible bipartition pairs to the known sums for horizontal $2$-strips in ordinary partitions, we obtain an explicit finite set of exceptional nonzero parameters.

title: The Göttsche conjecture and the Göttsche--Yau--Zaslow formula
abstract:
The aim of these notes is to give an account, intended for the non-specialist, of the two proofs of the Göttsche conjecture given, respectively, first by Tzeng, and shortly after by Kool, Shende and Thomas.
  Given a smooth, complex, projective surface $S$ and a positive integer $δ$, the Göttsche conjecture predicts that if $L$ is a sufficiently positive line bundle on $S$, then the number of $δ$-nodal curves in a general $δ$-dimensional linear subsystem $Λ\subset |L|$ is given by a universal polynomial of degree $δ$ in the four numbers $L^2$, $L K_S$, $K_S^2$, and $c_2(S)$.
  Besides, the Göttsche--Yau--Zaslow formula expresses the generating function of the aforementioned numbers of $δ$-nodal curves in terms of three explicit quasimodular forms and two unknown universal power series, whose coefficients can be determined by recursion.

title: The random analyst
abstract: Modern data-analysis pipelines increasingly involve searching among candidate analyses before reporting an estimate. We investigate the replicability of the resulting conclusions by studying independent repetitions of the entire search-and-report procedure on new samples. Can the reported estimates become increasingly similar across studies while remaining systematically displaced from the scientific target? We first show that this can happen in a simple Gaussian model. Although every prespecified candidate estimator is unbiased and consistent, searching over exponentially many candidates within each study yields a selected estimator converging to a limit different from the target, a selection-induced pseudotruth. Across independent repetitions, the reported estimates thus become replicable but systematically inaccurate, while the selected candidates differ with probability tending to one. We then study dependent Gaussian candidates, including marginal regression coefficients, and show that Gaussian width governs the displacement, which persists when squared width is of the same order as sample size. Metric entropy and generic chaining reveal that the effective complexity of the search is determined by the geometry of statistically distinguishable analyses rather than by their nominal number. Large-deviation arguments further extend the phenomenon beyond Gaussian models. Numerical agreement between independent studies therefore need not indicate either a stable analytical path or proximity to the scientific target.

title: Gorenstein toric Fano $d$-varieties have Picard ranks at most $2d$
abstract: We show that the Picard rank of $d$-dimensional Gorenstein toric Fano varieties is at most $2d$. This generalizes Batyrev's conjecture of Picard ranks for smooth toric Fano varieties, which was proved by Casagrande for all $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial Gorenstein toric Fano varieties. The convex-geometric proof is a generalization of Casagrande's proof and Eikelberg's theory of non-$\mathbb{Q}$-factorial toric Picard groups, with key ideas from work of Debarre, Øbro, Fujita and the first author. The proof was found using ChatGPT 6.1.

title: The $N$-channel white-noise Schrödinger operator in all three Dyson classes. I. Explicit stationary admittance distribution, density of states and outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals
abstract: We obtain an explicit stationary distribution of the matrix Riccati variable---the boundary admittance---for an $N$-channel Schrödinger operator with Gaussian white-noise disorder, in all three Dyson symmetry classes $β=1,2,4$. Uniform absorption regularizes the Riccati dynamics, and the distribution's normalization factorizes into outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals. This gives a common route to the density of states and the sum of Lyapunov exponents, extending Halperin's scalar solution to coupled channels. Exact finite-$N$ formulas connect two spectral regimes: the Lifshitz tail, including its symmetry-dependent prefactor, and the collective large-$N$ edge. We reduce the $β=4$ and even-$N$ $β=1$ problems to unitary orthogonal polynomials and an auxiliary recursion. Their critical double-scaling limit yields edge profiles on the $N^{-4/5}$ energy scale, governed by a complex Painlevé-I tritronquée solution and a linear auxiliary equation. We conjecture that these profiles describe a universal edge regime of random band matrices.

title: Creation Sequences for Numerical Semigroups and Exact Counts of Semigroup Partitions
abstract: A numerical semigroup is a subset of the non-negative integers that contains $0$, is closed under addition and has finite complement. A threshold graph is built by adding vertices one at a time, each new vertex being isolated or dominating, and the record of these choices is its \emph{creation sequence}. Reading the creation sequence as a lattice path gives an integer partition and, through the Keith--Nath correspondence, a numerical set in which the dominating vertices are the elements and the isolated vertices are the gaps. We show that threshold graphs with an isolated vertex correspond bijectively to numerical sets, and we study numerical semigroups through their creation sequences. We prove that in the creation sequence of a numerical semigroup of multiplicity $m$ every block of ones and every non-initial block of zeros has length less than $m$, we give criteria for partitions with a unique smallest part and with two distinct part sizes, and we classify all partitions with at most four parts. We show that every partition $λ$ with $g$ parts corresponding to a numerical semigroup satisfies $\ell(λ)\geλ_1$ and, more strongly, fits inside the staircase $(g,g-1,\dots,1)$; equivalently, its creation sequence begins with a Dyck path. Its size equals the genus plus the Weierstrass weight of the semigroup, and asymptotically at most half of all partitions correspond to numerical semigroups. Finally, we obtain exact formulas for the numbers of partitions of $n$ corresponding to numerical semigroups of genus $g$, multiplicity $m$ and Frobenius number $f$, valid in the sharp ranges $g\ge n/2$, $m>n/3$ and $f\ge n-\frac{n-1}{4}$. These formulas solve the open problems posed by Burson, Nam and Sisneros-Thiry \cite{BNS}, recover all of their counting theorems, and correct several of their statements.

title: Analysis and Design of Spatially Coupled LDPC Codes for Pulsed-Jamming-Resilient Space Telemetry
abstract: Jamming is a major threat to space telemetry downlinks, which operate under severe power and bandwidth constraints. This paper develops a jamming-aware analysis and design framework for protograph-based spatially coupled low-density parity-check (SC-LDPC) codes. For pulsed jamming with jamming state information (JSI) at the receiver, we derive a two-state protograph-based extrinsic information transfer (PEXIT) recursion that tracks the messages originating from clean and jammed symbols separately and merges them at the check nodes through a mutual-information-matched Gaussian approximation. For non-interleaved pulsed jamming, we map each pulse realization, through the serialization of the lifted codeword, to a profile of jammed fractions over the variable-node types, and we prove that, under random lifting, this profile determines the local channel-state statistics. The resulting position-dependent thresholds are the objective of a constrained differential-evolution search over protographs, coupling memories, and edge spreadings. At different code rates, the designed ensembles are compared with the Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS) accumulate, repeat-by-4, and jagged accumulate (AR4JA) LDPC codes whose block length matches the SC-LDPC constraint length, with longer AR4JA codes whose block length is comparable with the size of the sliding window decoder, and with non-optimized SC-LDPC codes. Under pulsed jamming with random pulse positions and with JSI, the ensembles designed over random pulse realizations, decoded through sliding window decoding, reach a bit error rate of $10^{-4}$ at lower signal-to-noise ratios than all the benchmarks.

title: Fourier--Stieltjes palettes on compact abelian groups
abstract: Let G be an infinite compact abelian group and let K={0,a_1,a_2,...}, where a_1>a_2>...>0 and a_n\to 0. We construct a nonzero real, even, purely singular Rajchman measure whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in K. We then classify the compact abelian groups on which every positive null palette is exactly realizable in each of four classes: purely singular measures, atomless purely singular measures, strongly continuous purely singular measures, and Rajchman purely singular measures. Exact realization by a purely singular measure is always possible; atomless exact realization fails precisely for groups topologically isomorphic to \mathbb{T}\times F with F finite; and universal exact Rajchman realization is equivalent to \operatorname{Tor}(\widehat G) being infinite, or equivalently to G/G_0 being infinite. On \mathbb{T} we also give palette-dependent sufficient conditions for exact Rajchman realization. Finally, if U\subset\mathbb{C} is open and 0\in\overline U, we construct a continuous Rajchman measure with nonzero singular part whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in U, assuming metrizability of G when 0\notin U. This gives a negative answer to an open-range absolute-continuity question of Ohrysko and Wojciechowski.

title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
abstract: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

title: A scaling approach to double phase equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$
abstract: We study radial solutions of the double phase equation $-Δ_p u - \operatorname{div}(|x|^{-b}\,|\nabla u|^{q-2}\nabla u) = f(|x|,u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, whose operator admits a scaling that acts on both phases simultaneously. Our first main result is a sharp description of the continuous and compact embeddings of the radial energy space into weighted Lebesgue spaces $L^s(\mathbb{R}^N;|x|^{-c})$ with an explicit characterization of their admissible regions in the $(s,c)$-plane. The two critical edges reflect the two phases: on the edge attached to the $p$-phase compactness is lost by spreading to infinity, while on the edge attached to the weighted $q$-phase it is lost by concentration at the origin. Our second main result concerns equations with one critical term on each edge. We show that bounded Palais-Smale sequences either converge or lose at least the energy $β^\ast = \min\{β_1,β_2\}$, where $β_1$ and $β_2$ are the explicit single-phase thresholds, and that this level is optimal when the critical terms are unweighted. Thus, the two mechanisms cannot combine to lower the compactness threshold. Combining these results with a Pohožaev identity, variational methods for scaled functionals and the Fadell-Rabinowitz cohomological index, we prove nonexistence results, obtain an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues on the scaling line and infinitely many solutions for pure power equations, and show that large superscaled and small subscaled perturbations of the doubly critical equation yield multiple solutions.

title: High-probability Uniform Mixing via Dobrushin Contraction and Accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
abstract: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, since its invention and subsequent rise to widespread use, has been motivated by its ability to accelerate convergence to equilibrium compared to diffusive methods, both in terms of dependence on condition number and dimension. In the present work, we establish this acceleration simultaneously in both aspects for critically damped Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin with persistent uniforms. More precisely, for target measures $μ(dx)\propto e^{-U(x)}dx$ with $m$-strongly convex, $L$-gradient Lipschitz, and $L_H$-Frobenius Hessian Lipschitz potentials, we show that the method mixes to $\varepsilon$-accuracy in total variation using $\mathcal O\bigl((κ^{1/2}+L_H^{1/2}m^{-3/4})\,d^{1/4}\bigr)$ gradient evaluations up to logarithmic factors, both uniformly over starting points in domains of high equilibrium probability and from warm starts. The proof incorporates ideas from previous studies by Bou-Rabee and Chen et al. that show either aspect of acceleration separately, into novel coupling technology. This new coupling technology for general Markov chains extends earlier frameworks aimed at capturing fast local equilibration in the presence of slow global mixing. Specifically, via a weak-$(1,1)$ maximal inequality that follows from Hopf's maximal ergodic theorem, we uncover a stability mechanism in high-probability domains with respect to equilibrium. This enables straightforward localization to naturally arising domains of fast local mixing, and seamlessly fits broad local frameworks via Dobrushin contraction, Wasserstein contraction and local Harris' theorems. We develop the Dobrushin formulation.

title: Dimension-free spectral laws and the risk of spectral filters
abstract:
Spectral properties of the sample covariance are key to modern machine learning with high-dimensional data. Random matrix theory (RMT) supplies powerful tools; however, most classical results assume proportional asymptotics, where $d/n$ tends to a finite limit. In functional data analysis and kernel methods, a fixed infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is often the more natural setting for the observations, beyond the scope of proportional asymptotics. This calls for a dimension-free spectral theory for i.i.d. observations $\boldsymbol{x}_1, \dots, \boldsymbol{x}_n$ in a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with trace-class population covariance $Σ$. Building on the dimension-free ridge regression analysis of Cheng and Montanari (2024), we establish two deterministic equivalents with explicit nonasymptotic error bounds. The first approximates the empirical spectral law $\widehatμ_n$ of the sample Gram matrix by a deterministic law $μ_n$. The second characterizes the conditional prediction risk of analytic spectral filters in linear regression.
  Previous sharp approximations to prediction risk in this setting have focused on ridge regression and closely-related problems. Our analysis covers a broader class of filters at the bulk scale, with an explicit user-friendly spectral stability condition to check. We apply our theory to power and critical spectral laws, and we recover the proportional regime. For prediction, we study (negative) ridge estimators, iterated ridge, and gradient flow. Mathematically, building on the idea of stochastic interpolation, we construct a deterministic backward path to interpolate the spectral parameter. The resulting bounds on resolvent and mixed-resolvent traces give mesoscopic approximations to the spectral law within the bulk and, by Cauchy's formula, deterministic equivalents for the prediction variance and squared bias of analytic spectral filters.

title: Weak error of approximation of a Lévy-type process using dynamic cutting
abstract: In this note we consider, on one hand, the implementation of the parametrix method for estimation of the distance between functionals $\Ee^x f(X_t)$ and $\Ee^x f(\widetilde X_t)$ of two Lévy-type processes $X$ and $\tilde X$. On the other hand, we estimate the weak error appearing by substituting small jumps by a (time-inhomogeneous) diffusion. Both methods rely on the time-dependent cutting procedure, designed to remove small jumps in a time-dependent way.

title: Simultaneous reconstruction of an obstacle and its wavenumber for the Helmholtz equation: a robust optimization approach
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to recover simultaneously the shape and wavenumber of an object from noisy radar or sonar measurements. The physical problem is modeled in a bounded domain with the Helmholtz equation and appropriate transmission conditions. The approach relies on a Kohn-Vogelius formulation of the inverse problem and uses Nesterov's accelerated gradient descent combined with shape optimization techniques. To address the robustness of the method with respect to measurement noise, we are looking to minimize a convex combination of the expected value and variance, which we achieve by using a Karhunen-Lo{è}ve expansion. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through twodimensional numerical experiments.

title: Average character degree below 14/3
abstract: We prove that a finite group with average irreducible character degree less than $14/3$ is solvable if it has no chief factor isomorphic to $A_5$. This answers a question of Aziziheris and Eivazzadeh.

title: Elliptic Gromov-Witten Invariants of Instanton Moduli
abstract:
We calculate the genus $1$ Gromov-Witten invariants with one tautological divisor insertion of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}(r,n)$ of rank-$r$, $c_2=n$ torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^2$ framed along the infinity divisor. As rational functions of the framing parameters, we determine the polar parts of these invariants by exploring the equivariant geometry of the Gieseker-Uhlenbeck map $\mathcal{M}(r,n)\to\mathcal{M}_0(r,n)$. We determine the polynomial part of these invariants by relating their large framing limits to the results \cite{ILPT} for the rank $1$ case, namely $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{C}^2)$. The degree-$0$ invariants with one divisor insertion are evaluated by studying the combinatorics of multi-partitions.
  We also prove reconstruction results for invariants with multiple insertions. Under the assumption that the eigenvalues of the divisor operator are linearly independent as functions of the Novikov variable, these results determine the full genus $1$ theory from the one-divisor series and the genus $0$ divisor operator.

title: Entropy of Noncommutative Spaces
abstract: We give an overview of the second quantisation of spectral triples and compute the entropy of the noncommutative space described by it in terms of a spectral action. This reviews earlier work by Chamseddine, Connes and the second author, but presented here concisely, including the procedure of second quantisation using infinite-dimensional Clifford algebras. We exemplify the theory by considering noncommutative metric spaces consisting of $N$ points. The entropy of these discrete spaces is explicitly computed, and we study the resulting entropic force as well as the evolution of the spaces in time.

title: Fundamental Tradeoffs in Sampling, Transmission and Information Freshness: Instantaneous Feedback
abstract: We study a time-slotted generate-at-will status-update system over an erasure channel with transmission success probability $q$, subject to average sampling- and transmission-rate constraints $f_s$ and $f_r$, respectively. The sampler-transmitter pair jointly decides whether to idle, retransmit a stale packet, or replace it with a fresh sample. We derive a universal lower bound on the optimal average age of information, analyze a class of stationary randomized policies, and obtain an optimal policy within this class that provides a $4$-approximation guarantee. The joint problem reduces to the sampling-constrained problem when $f_s\leq qf_r$ and the transmission-constrained problem when $f_s\geq f_r$. For $qf_r<f_s<f_r$, we formulate a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) and introduce the class $\barΠ$ of $(W,R)$ policies, where $W$ specifies a waiting threshold for transmission and $R$ specifies a packet-replacement threshold. We prove that, for every choice of Lagrange multipliers, the corresponding Lagrangian-relaxed Markov decision process admits an optimal policy in $\barΠ$. We then formulate a linear program (LP) over distributions of $(W,R)$ policies and prove that choosing a policy according to an optimal LP solution yields an optimal CMDP policy. Moreover, there exists an optimal LP solution assigning positive probability to at most three $(W,R)$ policies. Since $\barΠ$ is countably infinite, for every $ε>0$ we construct a finite subset $\barΠ_ε\subset\barΠ$ and show that the LP restricted to this set yields an $ε$-optimal policy. Finally, we derive a stronger pair of lower bounds by considering systems with only the sampling-rate or transmission-rate constraint. Using these bounds, we construct a policy randomizing among four $(W,R)$ policies with a $2$-approximation guarantee for $qf_r<f_s<f_r$.

title: Large gaps and the ten martini problem for monotone quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators
abstract: We prove the ten martini theorem for a large class of monotone potentials. The key strategy is to establish polynomially large gaps for periodic approximations.

title: The cost of enforcing long-run coverage: a phase transition in online conformal prediction
abstract:
Consider an online prediction setting, where at each time, we are given a new feature vector and asked to provide a prediction interval or prediction set that will likely contain the corresponding response. In this setting, if the data points are i.i.d.
